### F153 — ALIGN-GLOBAL-001 / ALIGN-LOCAL-001 / ALIGN-SEMI-001 / ALIGN-STATS-001 / GENOMIC-COMMON-001 / GENOMIC-MOTIFS-001 / GENOMIC-TANDEM-001 / MOTIF-CONS-001 (audit A4-3, WP39): the EMBOSS reader drops gap characters and every other non-letter from plain input sequences - one shared cleaner for all ports
- **Defect.** EMBOSS 6.6.0 removes every character that is not a letter or `*` from a plain input sequence BEFORE any length check, coordinate or score; no Seqeron port did. Minimal repro: `needle AC-GTTAGC.TT* ACGTTAGCTT` prints `# Length: 11`, `# Score: 58.0`; `SequenceAligner.NeedleAlign("AC-GTTAGC.TT*", "ACGTTAGCTT")` scored 43 (gap characters kept and scored); `WaterAlign` 43, `StretcherAlign` 27, `Merger` kept `.` and `-` in the merged sequence, `DotMatcher.Compute` scored a gap 0 and kept its position (68 of 300 random gapped pairs differed), `FindTandemRepeatsEtandem("ACACAC-ACACAC.ACAC")` counted the gap characters, `FindPatternHits` / `FindProteinPatternHits` / `FindTranslatedPatternHits` / `Supermatcher` / `NeedleAll` / matcher (`TopNTieOrder.Sim`) / `SeqMatchAll` / `MegaMerge` / `FindTandemRepeatsEquicktandem` likewise; `consambig` / `showalign` threw "Invalid alignment character" for a digit or a blank (the program drops them) and read `#` / `+` as invalid.
- **Source (what was actually opened).** EMBOSS `ajax/core/ajseqread.c` (`seqAppend`: `ajStrKeepSetAlphaC(.., "*.~?#+-")`), `ajseqtype.c` (`ajSeqTypeCheckIn` / `seqTypeFix`: an UNGAPPED type calls `ajStrRemoveGap`; the `seqType[]` table), `ajstr.c` (`ajStrRemoveGap` keeps exactly `A-Za-z*`), `ajseq.c` (`ajSeqIsNuc`, `ajSeqGapStandard`) from raw.githubusercontent.com/kimrutherford/EMBOSS (User-Agent `Seqeron-review/1.0`); the installed ACD files (`/usr/share/EMBOSS/acd/<program>.acd`: `type:` of each sequence input is `any` / `dna` / `nucleotide` / `protein` / `stopprotein`, all ungapped; `gapany` for consambig / showalign); the installed programs.
- **Measurement.** `scripts/alignment/measure_emboss_reader_chars.py`: each character 1..255 except newline / carriage return / `>` inserted into the middle of a sequence, run through needle, water, stretcher, matcher, merger, megamerger, seqmatchall, fuzznuc, fuzzpro, fuzztran, etandem, equicktandem, dotmatcher, palindrome (both sequences, nucleotide and protein; the output with the character equals the output without it): **199 characters are dropped by every program** (everything except the 52 ASCII letters and `*`; `*` is kept, a protein stop, an error in a nucleotide-typed input). Alignment readers (consambig, showalign; `gapany`): `. ~ -` gaps, `? # +` the unknown residue (`ACGT#CGT`, `ACGT+CGT`, `ACGT?CGT` give the same consensus and set type), every other non-letter dropped, rows padded after cleaning (non-ASCII bytes depend on the C library's `isalpha` and the locale: dropped here, not part of the oracle). A sequence that is empty afterwards: "Unable to read sequence" (zero length).
- **Fix.** `EmbossSequenceReader` (Infrastructure, public, one file): `Clean` (letters and `*`), `CleanGapped` (alignment rows), `IsNucleotide` (the single `ajSeqIsNuc` rule: it replaces `DotMatcher.IsNucleotide`, `MotifFinder.IsEmbossNucleotideSequence` + `EmbossNucGapChars`, `StretcherAlign.IsNucleotideText`, `PairWordMatcher`'s `IsNucleotideWordSequence`, `EmbossAlignmentWriter.IsNuc`), `Clean(IReadOnlyList<EmbossSequence>)`. Called by every EMBOSS-named entry point: `NeedleAlign`, `WaterAlign`, `StretcherAlign`, `Merger`, `NeedleAll`, `Supermatcher`, `LocalAlign(Affine)TopN(.., TopNTieOrder.Sim)`, `DotMatcher.Compute`, `MegaMerge`, `SeqMatchAll`, `FindPatternHits` (string overloads), `FindProteinPatternHits`, `FindTranslatedPatternHits`, `FindTandemRepeatsEtandem`, `FindTandemRepeatsEquicktandem`, `GenerateEmbossConsensus`, `GenerateEmbossAmbiguousConsensus`, `ShowAlign`, `CalculateDistanceMatrix` (distmat). The raw route stays: the non-EMBOSS-named entry points (`GlobalAlign`, `LocalAlign`, `FindMotif`, the `DnaSequence` overloads, ...) keep every character literally (no caller of this repository needed a literal route into an EMBOSS-named entry, so no option was added). MCP descriptions of the 17 tools and `docs/mcp` regenerated (`gen-catalog.py --check` fresh, 548 tools).
- **Oracle.** `emboss_gap_oracle.tsv` (`generate_emboss_gap_oracle.py`, seed 20261126): 18 programs (the 17 plus distmat) x 240 rows = 4 320 rows whose inputs contain `- . ~ ? # + _`, digits, blanks, quotes, brackets, `*` (protein), lower case and non-ASCII letters; **4 320 / 4 320 equal** (needle / water / stretcher score + rows, matcher alignment lists, merger / megamerger merged sequence, seqmatchall match lists, supermatcher / needleall rows, fuzznuc / fuzzpro / fuzztran hits + the GFF header's sequence length, etandem / equicktandem reports, dotmatcher plots, consambig consensus, showalign text, distmat matrices). Needle scores 58 (Length 11) where the program does.
- **Tests.** `EmbossGapCharacters_Oracle_Tests` (18 oracle tests, the 58 example, the 256-code-point table of `Clean`, `CleanGapped`, `IsNucleotide`).
- **Not changed (cross-batch note).** `palindrome` reads its sequence the same way (measured: the same 199 characters); `RepeatFinder` (another batch's file) has no EMBOSS-named string entry, so nothing to switch. `distmat` (`MultipleAlignmentStatistics.CalculateDistanceMatrix`, `gapany` like consambig) uses `CleanGapped` and reads `? # +` as X (N in a nucleotide row) as well: 240 oracle rows (all `-nucmethod` / `-protmethod` values) equal.
- **Commit.** see the worklist tick of A4-3.

### F154 — ALIGN-STATS-001 (audit A4-5 and A4-2 (b), WP39): `ShowAlign` allocated O(L^2 / width) and overflowed at the extremes of `Width` / `Margin`
- **Defect.** `OutputSeq` built `new string(seq)` (a copy of the WHOLE row) for every block of every row: width 1 over two 100 kb rows = 6.2 MB of output, 60 GB allocated, 12 s; `Margin = int.MaxValue` -> raw `OutOfMemoryException: Array dimensions exceeded`; `Width = int.MaxValue` took 9.4 s for a 9-column alignment; `int iend = pos + width + margin - 1` overflowed 32 bit.
- **Fix.** `OutputSeq` appends the slice of the `char[]` (`StringBuilder.Append(char[], first, count)`, the `EmbossText.Substring` clipping kept), the upper-case ranges are only looked at when there are any; `Width` is clamped to the alignment length (the text of one block is the same: `pos + width + margin - 1` reaches the end either way), the position arithmetic is 64 bit, and the display text is bounded by the documented `MultipleAlignmentDisplay.ShowAlignMaxOutputCharacters` (2^27 characters; blocks x lines x (margin + width + 1) computed in 64 bit BEFORE the rows are normalised or anything is built): a larger request is an `ArgumentException` of the `SequenceAligner.ResourceLimit` style (the program streams its output and has no such limit). The dead local `char[] r` / `_ = r;` of `Output` is gone.
- **Oracle.** `showalign_oracle.jsonl` 600 / 600 equal (unchanged); `emboss_gap_oracle.tsv` showalign 240 / 240.
- **Tests.** `MultipleAlignmentDisplay_ShowAlign_Tests`: `Width_BeyondTheAlignment_...` (the text equals the text of the alignment width, instantly), `Margin_OrWidth_AboveTheOutputLimit_IsRefusedBeforeAnythingIsBuilt` (exception text, < 64 MB allocated, 40-million-column case, the last margin that fits is accepted), `Output_AllocationIsLinearInTheText_NotQuadratic` (width 1 over 2 x 20 000 columns: < 120 MB; 1.6 GB before).

### F155 — GENOMIC-COMMON-001 (audit A4-6, WP39): `MegaMerge` `MinimalMatchSet` without the O(k) list shifts - and the measured cost of the 20 kb poly-A case is NOT this loop
- **Finding.** `MinimalMatchSet` shifted the list tail for every `RemoveAt(0)` / `RemoveAt(i)` and sorted the whole list again after every truncation. Fixed: the head is an index, one pass compacts the survivors in place, the shortened matches (new keys) are sorted on their own and merged into the sorted survivors; same result, same `InvalidOperationException`s in the same order (every remaining match is still examined against every kept one: the program's loop, O(k) per kept match).
- **Measurement (against the audit's attribution).** `SeqMatchAll` of two poly-A sequences (no `MinimalMatchSet` at all) takes 2.85 s / 10.8 s for 4 000 / 8 000 residues and `MegaMerge` 2.94 s / 10.85 s: the 69 s of the 20 kb case are the maximal-match enumeration of the shared suffix-tree engine (`SuffixTreeAlgorithms.FindMaximalExactMatches`: for every query position all text occurrences of the longest match are collected before the left-maximal ones are kept, O(n x m) for repeats), not the minimal-match loop (60 000 matches: 0.2 s after the change, `List.RemoveAt` shifts about 1-2 s before). The installed `megamerger` is quadratic as well: 1 500 poly-A residues take it 20 s, 3 000 more than 100 s. Cross-batch request (B05, `SuffixTree/Algorithms/SuffixTree.Core/SuffixTreeAlgorithms.cs`): collect only left-maximal occurrences (a left-character summary per node makes the enumeration output-sensitive); registered below.
- **Tests.** `GenomicAnalyzer_MegaMerge_Tests`: `MinimalMatchSet_EqualsTheListShiftingOriginal_OnRandomRepetitiveMatchLists_ExceptionsIncluded` (400 repetitive match lists: the original loop is kept in the test as the reference, results and aborts equal), `MinimalMatchSet_OfSixtyThousandDiagonalMatches_IsFast`, `PolyA_IsTheProgramsResult_ForTheLengthsTheProgramFinishes` (600 / 1 500: megamerger 6.6.0 prints the whole sequence, "Matching region a 1-n : b 1-n"), `TandemRepeat_MegaMerge_IsTheProgramsResult_AndCancellable`. The 600 / 600 megamerger oracle is unchanged.

### F156 — ALIGN-MULTI-001 / GENOMIC-TANDEM-001 (audit A4-4, WP39): option boundaries of the minimap2 chaining, mgaps clustering and etandem ports measured on the programs
- **Finding.** The audit listed `MinimapChainOptions` (`KmerSize = 0`, `Bandwidth = -5`, `MaxChainIterations = 0`, ... `ChainGapScale = NaN`), `NucmerClusterOptions` (negative / NaN values) and `etandem -threshold int.MinValue` (`DivideByZeroException` "while the program returns 0 hits") as accepted-but-wrong. Measured on the installed programs (minimap2 2.26, mgaps 3.23, etandem 6.6.0; `generate_option_boundary_oracle.py`, 30 + 17 + 12 rows): **the programs accept almost all of these values**; the only rejections are `mm_check_opt` "-k and -w must be positive" (k <= 0) and the `mm_sketch` assertion k <= 28; mgaps rejects nothing (negative, zero, NaN, infinite values run). The `etandem` claim was wrong in the other direction: the program does NOT return 0 hits for `-threshold -2147483648` - it dies with SIGFPE ("Floating point exception", exit status 136; `etandem.c`: `reportRoot->bestScore = thresh - 1` wraps to INT_MAX, the report loop takes the root (repeat size 0) as the top entry and divides by it) whenever one repeat qualifies, and prints nothing when none does (`AAAAAAAA`, `A`); the port's `DivideByZeroException` was the same death.
- **Source (opened).** minimap2 v2.26 `options.c` (`mm_check_opt`), `sketch.c` (assertion), `lchain.c` (`comput_sc`: `sc -= (int)(lin_pen + .5f * log_pen)`), `etandem.c` (`etandem_report`, `etandem_finalReport`, `thresh - 1` at the report root) from raw.githubusercontent.com (User-Agent `Seqeron-review/1.0`); the installed programs on the boundary values.
- **Fix.** (1) `MinimapChainOptions.KmerSize` outside 1 - 28 is an `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (message quotes the program); every other value is accepted with the program's arithmetic - and the C float-to-int conversion of a NaN / infinite / huge penalty (`cvttss2si` gives INT_MIN; .NET gives 0 / saturates) is reproduced (`CInt`, unchecked subtraction), so `ChainGapScale` = NaN / Infinity / 1e30 give the program's chains. (2) `NucmerClusterOptions`: every value accepted; the `(int)(f x separation)` of the port became the program's `(long)` conversion (`CLong`: NaN / beyond-64-bit = LONG_MIN), so `-f nan / inf / 1e30` (no fraction added) and `-f 1e10` (everything joins) equal mgaps. (3) `FindTandemRepeatsEtandem`: `threshold - 1` is explicitly unchecked and the program's SIGFPE is an `InvalidOperationException` that says so (raised exactly when the program would die: threshold = int.MinValue and a repeat qualifies; otherwise the empty list). (4) `CollectAnchors(queryOccurrenceFraction: NaN)`: the program accepts it (`q_occ_frac > 0` is false: filter off; -1 and inf too: measured), the port already equalled it - locked by a test. The XML docs state each rule.
- **Tests.** `OptionBoundaries_Oracle_Tests` (5): 30 minimap2 option values (chain score + anchor count of every hit equal to the program's PAF `s1` / `cm`; the oracle runs use `-r 500,500`: the long-join bandwidth is the registered A4-7), 17 mgaps option values (clusters equal), `KmerSize` 0 / -3 / 29 / 40 / int.MinValue / int.MaxValue refused, the `q_occ_frac` values, 12 etandem rows (5 crash rows throw, 2 empty rows at int.MinValue, int.MinValue + 1 and above exact).
- **MCP.** `minimap2_chains`, `nucmer_clusters`, `find_tandem_repeats_emboss` descriptions state the rules (catalog `--check` fresh, 548 tools).

### F157 — ALIGN-LOCAL-001 / ALIGN-MULTI-001 / ALIGN-SEMI-001 / ALIGN-STATS-001 / GENOMIC-COMMON-001 / GENOMIC-MOTIFS-001 / MOTIF-CONS-001 (audit A4-1, WP39): the ports added in WP36 - WP38 poll the ambient cancellation token; six MCP tools take a token
- **Defect.** `AlignmentCancellation.Poll` / `ThrowIfRequested` count = 0 in `DotMatcher`, `Minimap2Chaining`, `NucmerClusters`, `SequenceAligner.Merger`, `SequenceAligner.TopNSim`; `GenomicAnalyzer.MegaMerge` polled before / after the match listing only; `FindTranslatedPatternHits`, `ShowAlign`, `GenerateEmbossAmbiguousConsensus` took no token; `FindNucmerClusters` passed its token to `FindCommonRegions` and never into `NucmerClusters.Cluster`. Measured: `DotMatcher.Compute` 3 000 x 3 000 = 0.5 s (100 kb x 100 kb about 10 min), `NucmerClusters.Cluster` of 300 000 collinear matches (one cluster: the program's own O(c^2) chain DP) did not return in > 2 min, `Minimap2Chaining` of a 57 kb tandem repeat 10.8 s. MCP `dotmatcher`, `minimap2_chains`, `merger`, `fuzztran`, `showalign`, `consambig` had no `CancellationToken` parameter.
- **Fix (the existing ambient mechanism, `SequenceAligner.Cancellation.cs`).** New trailing `CancellationToken cancellationToken = default` (entering the scope) on `DotMatcher.Compute`, `Minimap2Chaining.Chain` / `CollectAnchors` / `MapChains`, `NucmerClusters.Cluster`, `SequenceAligner.Merger`, `GenomicAnalyzer.FindTranslatedPatternHits`, `MotifFinder.GenerateEmbossAmbiguousConsensus`, and `ShowAlignOptions.CancellationToken`; `FindNucmerClusters` passes its token into `Cluster`; `MegaMerge` passes its token into `MinimalMatchSet`. Polls: one per diagonal (`DotMatcher`), every 64 anchors / 256 chains (`Chain`), every 65 536 k-mer positions and per 256 query minimizers (`CollectAnchors` / `Sketch`), per match of the filter / union / DP passes (`NucmerClusters`), per path-matrix column and every 1 024 walk steps (`Merger`), per row of the big / small / diff passes and per reported alignment (`TopNSim`), per kept match (`MinimalMatchSet`), per frame and every 65 536 residues (`ProteinPatternHitsCore`: also `fuzzpro`), per row / 1 024 columns of the consensus and per block of the display (`ShowAlign`), per row and 8 192 columns (`consambig`). MCP: the six tools take the token and hand it to the library (`BeginCancellationScope` / the library parameter).
- **Not interruptible (stated).** The maximal-match enumeration of the shared suffix-tree engine (`SuffixTreeAlgorithms.FindMaximalExactMatches`, B05) runs to completion before `MegaMerge` / `SeqMatchAll` / `FindCommonRegions` see its list; it is the part of a poly-A `MegaMerge` that takes minutes (F155).

### F158 — ALIGN-MULTI-001 / ALIGN-LOCAL-001 / GENOMIC-COMMON-001 (audit A4-2, WP39): resource guards for the big allocations of the new ports (the ShowAlign part is F154)
- **Defect.** Measured: `Minimap2Chaining.CollectAnchors(polyA100k, polyA100k)` -> `OutOfMemoryException` after 10 s (every position is a minimizer, `mid_occ` becomes 100 001: 10^10 anchors); a 57 kb tandem repeat against itself 44 976 004 anchors, 5.2 GB allocated in 10.8 s (a `MinimapAnchor` is 20 bytes, the `List` doubles); `LocalAlignAffineTopN(.., maxAlignments: int.MaxValue, TopNTieOrder.Sim)` -> `OutOfMemoryException` at `new Vertex[k]` (the Waterman-Eggert order accepts it: 23 alignments); `MegaMerge` / `SeqMatchAll` / `DotMatcher.Compute` / `NucmerClusters.Cluster` materialise every match / segment / cluster with no bound.
- **Fix.** Documented public limits in `SequenceAligner.ResourceLimits.cs`, all raised as the one `SequenceAligner.ResourceLimit` `ArgumentException` BEFORE the allocation in 64-bit arithmetic: `MinimapMaxAnchors` (2^23: the sum of the occurrences of the query minimizers is counted before any anchor is stored; `Chain` refuses a longer list before it reads one; minimap2 itself has no such limit and drops frequent minimizers: the registered A4-7), `DotMatcherMaxSegments` (2^22, checked as the list grows), `NucmerMaxClusterMatches` (100 000 matches of ONE cluster: the program's O(c^2) chain DP, checked before the DP), `WordMatchMaxMatches` (2^22 matches of a pair; the engine's own list is checked as soon as the shared suffix-tree enumerator returns it - that engine is not bounded nor interruptible, F155 - and `WordTableMatches` while it builds), `TopNSimMaxVertices` (2^22). `TopNTieOrder.Sim`: the vertex list is allocated lazily (`VertexAt`), so `maxAlignments = int.MaxValue` means "every alignment" exactly as in the Waterman-Eggert order (the program calls `calloc(K)` up front and dies for such a K); the bound turns an endless list into the clear exception. `ShowAlign` Margin / Width: F154. The sequence-length limit of the 31-bit minimizer positions needs no check (a .NET string is at most 2^30 characters).
- **Tests.** `SequenceAligner_ResourceLimits_Tests` (+7, each asserts the exception text, the documented constant and a low allocation): `Minimap2CollectAnchors_PolyAAndTandemQueries_...` (100 kb poly-A, 60 kb period-2 tandem, an ordinary pair untouched), `Minimap2Chain_AboveTheAnchorLimit_...` (a list that throws when read), `TopNSim_MaxAlignmentsIntMaxValue_MeansEveryAlignment_...` (equal to the 100 000 run, both orders and both overloads accept it), `TopNSim_VertexListIsBounded_...`, `WordMatches_AboveTheMatchLimit_...` (5.1 million matches, seqmatchall and megamerger), `DotMatcher_SegmentList_IsBounded_...` (6.75 million segments), `NucmerCluster_OfMoreThan100000Matches_...`.

### F163 — ALIGN-GLOBAL-001 / ALIGN-LOCAL-001 / ALIGN-SEMI-001 (audit A4-8, WP40): `GapScoreProfile` alignments above the full-matrix limit

- **Verification.** 600 forced-recursion cases (6 methods x scalar / BLOSUM62 fractional, random profiles with free / interior / priced members, base-case sizes 1, 2, 9, 40, 300) row-for-row equal to the full matrix; the 1 000 Biopython oracle rows with base size 1 equal the full-matrix rows and the Biopython score; an 8 700 x 7 999 pair (69.6 M cells, automatic switch): Biopython scores 12 242 (global and local affine) / 13 824 (local linear = an independent numpy DP of the global linear scheme; Biopython 1.88's linear Needleman-Wunsch corner prints 12 499), **125 MB allocated against 835 MB of full matrices**. ### F164 — ALIGN-LOCAL-001 / GENOMIC-COMMON-001 / ALIGN-STATS-001 / MOTIF-CONS-001 (audit A4-9, WP40): edge-case coverage of the new EMBOSS ports; one FALSE doc claim, two behaviour fixes

### F167 — ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A5-1, WP41): minimap2 `X31Hash` sign extension of the first byte and the C-string end of the query name
- **Defect.** `Minimap2Chaining.X31Hash` (`khash.h` `__ac_X31_hash_string`: `h = (khint_t)*s; for (++s; *s; ++s) h = (h << 5) - h + (khint_t)*s` over a SIGNED `char`) zero-extended the first byte (`uint h = bytes[0]`) while the loop sign-extended the rest, and it hashed the whole string although a C string ends at the first NUL. The hash of the query name orders chains of equal score (`mm_gen_regs`: `hash ^= ...; hash64(...)`), so a name starting with a byte >= 0x80 (any non-ASCII first character, UTF-8 multi-byte) or containing U+0000 gave another primary / secondary choice than the program. Repro (auditor probe, 60 random references with three equal copies of a 300 - 600 base segment, query = the segment): names starting with U+00E9 differed from `minimap2 2.26` on 57 / 60, with U+4E2D on 53 / 60 (port primary `0:802-1195`, program primary `0:202-595`); ASCII names 0 / 60.
- **Fix.** `uint h = (uint)(sbyte)bytes[0]` and the hash stops at the first NUL byte (`Minimap2Chaining.Hits.cs`).
- **Oracle numbers.** `generate_minimap2_map_oracle.py` got a fifth group `qname` (330 cases, own seed `QNAME_SEED`, so the first 1 320 rows are reproduced byte for byte: the regenerated JSONL of the four old groups is identical to the committed content): query names from a UTF-8 pool (names starting with a 2-, 3- or 4-byte character 189, a non-ASCII character later in the name, names with U+0000 99, ASCII), references with 2 - 4 identical copies of the query (forward / reverse), `-N` / `-p` on some; PAF columns 3 - 12 and `tp cm s1 s2 dv rl` of every line equal on 330 / 330 with the fix (`minimap2_map_oracle.jsonl.gz`: 1 650 cases now). **Tests.** `Minimap2Map_Tests.Map_NonAsciiAndNulQueryNames_EqualMinimap2` (new group + counters of the classes). **Commit.** c4f2e8229.

### F168 — ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A5-2, WP41): resource guards and cancellation polls of the T-Coffee pair dynamic programs
- **Defect.** `biphasic_pair` / `fast_pair` at 20 000 x 20 000 residues: bare `OutOfMemoryException` after 1.4 s / 3.0 s; `-dp_mode gotoh_pair_wise` allocated 1.6 GB (traceback `int[l1+1][l2+1]`) without a check; `viterbi_pair_wise` computed `nmt * (I + 1) * (J + 1)` in 32-bit `int` (overflow beyond about 20 700 x 20 700) and 400 multiplications per cell with no poll (a 25 000 x 25 000 call ran 100 s); `TCoffeeLalignTopAlignments(topAlignments = int.MaxValue)` threw `OutOfMemoryException` (`new Vertex[K]`); `biphasic_pair` / the FASTA band / `glocal` / `gotoh_pair_wise_lgp` / `_sw` / the FASTA diagonal scan had no cancellation poll (a token cancelled after 1 s was observed after 3.6 s / 1.6 s); `KmerAnalyzer.CreateFracMinHashSketch(k = int.MaxValue)` allocated `new byte[k]`.
- **Source / measurement.** Installed `t_coffee` 13.41 under a 4 GB address-space limit: see the Evidence file (the program has no limit of its own: "FAILED TO ALLOCATE REQUIRED MEMORY (vmalloc)", exit status 1; a segmentation fault for gotoh_pair_wise at 40 000 x 40 000).
- **Fix.** `SequenceAligner.TCoffeeLimits.cs`: public `TCoffeePairDpMaxBytes` = 2 GiB and `RequireTcPairDp` (the `ResourceLimit` style, 64-bit, before the allocation) in `biphasic_pair_wise` (48 bytes per cell), `glocal_pair_wise` (40), `gotoh_pair_wise_lgp` (32), `gotoh_pair_wise` / `_sw` (4), `viterbi_pair_wise` (44, `TcRequireViterbiFits`), the FASTA band (20 per row x flagged diagonal) and the diagonal arrays of `evaluate_diagonals_with_ktup` / `_with_clist` / `very_fast_pair_wise`; a poll per row in `TcBiphasicMasks`, `TcGlocalMasks`, `TcGotohLgpMasks`, `TcGotohSwMasks`, `TcViterbiMasks` (match probabilities and recursion), `TcMakeFastaGotoh`, `TcIdscorePair`, per k-tuple occurrence in `TcDiagonalsByKtup` and per residue in `TcDiagonalsByLibrary`; the vertex list of `TcSim` grows lazily (limit `TopNSimMaxVertices`, as the matcher port); `KmerAnalyzer.CreateFracMinHashSketch`: no scratch buffer when the k-mer table is empty (B09 for B06). `AlignmentCancellation.OnPoll`: the internal test seam used by `PollCancellation` (A5-4).
- **Tests.** `SequenceAligner_TCoffeeLimits_Tests` (11: every limit + exception text + allocation < 64 MB + the int-overflow lengths, lazily grown vertex list, empty sketch, pre-cancelled + cancelled at the middle poll inside each method). **Commit.** 4ec4e8bab.

### F169 — ALIGN-MULTI-001 / ALIGN-STATS-001 (audit A5-3, WP41): null / out-of-range contract of the secondary public entry points
- **Defect.** A reflection fuzzer over every public static method of the owned classes (null / empty / extreme arguments, one parameter varied at a time over ordinary baselines; harness in the session scratchpad, 779 methods of `Seqeron.Genomics.Alignment` / `Analysis` and the MCP `AlignmentTools` / `AnalysisTools`) found `NullReferenceException` / `IndexOutOfRangeException` / `KeyNotFoundException` / `OverflowException` where an `ArgumentException` family exception is the library's contract: (1) `MuscleGuideTree` / `MuscleLocalAlign` / `MuscleProfileAlign` / `MuscleProfileScore` / `MuscleRefine` / `MuscleRefineWindows` / `MuscleScoreAlignment` (+ `MuscleRun`) with a null list or row, and a character above U+00FF (`_isResidue[256]`); (2) `KalignProgram.Parse` / `Run`, `PoaProgram.Run`, `ProbConsProgram.Parse` / `Run` (and the MCP `kalign_command`, `poa_command`, `probcons_command`) with a null argument or a null file text; (3) `Minimap2Chaining.Map` with a null target; (4) `TCoffeeKtupSimilarity`, `TCoffeePrimaryLibraryEntries` with a null list / element; (5) `TCoffeeSlowPairAlign`, `TCoffeeBiphasicPairAlign`, `TCoffeeLalignTopAlignments` with a character that is not a letter (`IndexOutOfRangeException` in `TcMatrix.Score`); (6) `Ksw2Aligner.SimpleMatrix(m <= 0 / int.MinValue / huge)`, `ExtendZ` / `ExtendD` with `m = int.MaxValue` (`m * m` overflow); (7) `AlignmentFormats.Format(.., A2m)` without the `state` annotation (`KeyNotFoundException`); (8) `PoaRun` / MCP `multiple_align_poa` with a null name / residues and a matrix with more than 128 symbols or a symbol above 127 (`IndexOutOfRangeException` in the `int[128, 128]` score table).
- **Source / measurement (installed programs).** `t_coffee` 13.41: a `*`, `-` or blank in a FASTA sequence is dropped by the program's reader (`slow_pair`, `biphasic_pair`, `lalign_id_pair` give the rows of the cleaned sequence), `U+00E9` ends the program with "ERROR: COREDUMP" (exit status 1); `muscle3` drops a non-letter byte of an unaligned input; argv entries of a real program are never null.
- **Fix.** `SequenceAligner.RequireNoNullElements` / `RequireProgramCall` (the shared message style `ArgumentNullException(paramName, "<Row|Argument|Target|Sequence> i is null.")`) at every entry point above; `RequireTcResidues` (letters only, `ArgumentException` naming the index and code point) at the three T-Coffee stages; `Ksw2Aligner.SimpleMatrix` refuses `m` outside 1 .. 256 and scores that do not fit `int8_t`, `CheckInputs` multiplies in 64 bits; `FormatA2m`: `ArgumentException` with the Biopython `KeyError` note; `PoaRun` null name / residues, `PoaScoreMatrix.Parse`: more than 128 symbols or a symbol above 127 -> `ArgumentException`; MUSCLE `PrepareMsa`: a character above U+00FF -> `ArgumentException` (Row i, column j). The documented program-abort of `GenomicAnalyzer.FindTandemRepeatsEtandem(threshold = int.MinValue)` (`InvalidOperationException`: the program's SIGFPE) stays by design.
- **Tests.** `SequenceAligner_NullContract_Tests` (10 test methods, 13 cases: one assertion per entry point with the parameter name, the program's own handling untouched), MCP `NullContractTests` (3). **Cross-batch escapes of the same fuzz run (information, other batches' files):** `SequenceAssembler` (B10: `FindAllOverlaps`, `FindOverlap`, `CalculateIdentity`, `CalculateStats`, `ComputeConsensus`, `ErrorCorrectReads`, `CalculateCoverage`, `AssembleOLC` NullReference), `ApproximateMatcher` (B04: `FindWithMismatches` / `FindWithEdits` NullReference, `FindFrequentKmersWithMismatches*` OutOfMemory), `RnaSecondaryStructure` (B11 owner: `CalculateStemEnergy` / `CalculateHairpinLoopEnergy` NullReference, IndexOutOfRange + hangs in the MFE / pseudoknot / partition-function entry points), `SequenceComplexity` (B04: `MaskLowComplexity`, `FindLowComplexityIntervals` OutOfMemory, `CalculateWindowedComplexity` IndexOutOfRange), `ComparativeGenomics.CalculateReversalDistance` (B18 NullReference), `KmerAnalyzer` (B06: `GenerateAllKmers` OutOfMemory / hang, `SelectMarkovOrder` / `MarkovOrderBics` Overflow / OutOfMemory), `ProteinMotifFinder` (`PredictCoiledCoils` Overflow, `FindDomainEnvelopes` hang), `RepeatFinder` (`FindApproximateTandemRepeats`, `MaskApproximateTandemRepeats` hang). **Commit.** 02e96c3df.

### F170 — MCP tool documents (audit A5-5, WP41): generated from the code's tool metadata, checked by a contract test
- **Defect.** 80 of the 216 documents of the Alignment server and the B09 tools of the Analysis server were stale against the `[McpServerTool]` / `[Description]` attributes (A5-5 counted 21 with a description difference at first look: the strict parameter comparison also finds 59 documents with missing defaults, parameter descriptions or Input Schema rows): missing parameters `local_align_top_n tieOrder`, `sum_of_pairs_score matrix`, `tcoffee_primary_library genomicTemplates`, `find_open_reading_frames` (`strand`, `ignoreNested`, `regionStart`, `regionEnd`, `orfFinderMinLength`, `allowDualCodingStopTables`), `find_pattern_hits sequenceAmbiguity`, `multiple_align_poa case`; stale descriptions of `format_alignment`, `merger`, `stretcher_align`, `write_alignment`, `fuzztran`, `generate_emboss_consensus`, ...; missing `default` of the needle / water / supermatcher / needleall penalties.
- **Fix.** `scripts/docs/McpToolDump` (a reflection dumper of every `[McpServerTool]`: name, description, parameters with type, default and `[Description]`) + `scripts/docs/sync_mcp_tool_docs.py` (regenerates `description`, `inputSchema.properties` (names, order, type, `default`, description, `required`) of the `.mcp.json` and the Input Schema table (and the description paragraphs when they are the old tool description) of the `.md`; hand text of the documents - output schema, examples, errors, hand-written summaries - is kept; `--check` lists every difference and exits 1). All B09 documents regenerated; `gen-catalog.py` regenerated + `--check` fresh (548 tools), link check OK. The anti-drift guard is a contract test over reflection, shared by the MCP test projects: `ToolDocsContractTestsBase` (`Seqeron.Mcp.Tests.Contracts`) with the fixtures `Seqeron.Mcp.Alignment.Tests.ToolDocsContractTests` (all 76 tools) and `Seqeron.Mcp.Analysis.Tests.ToolDocsContractTests` (the tools whose `methodId` names a B09 class): it fails when a tool's description, parameter set / order, type, default, parameter description, `required` or the `.md` table differ from its document. **Commit.** 23837b449.

### F171 — test quality of the WP39 / WP40 tests (audit A5-4, WP41): deterministic cancellation, no wall-clock latency assertions, exact values
- **Defect.** `CancelledWhileRunning_ShowAlign_StopsPromptly` failed under CPU load (the timed cancel landed in an earlier stage) and the 13 mid-run tests of A4-1 / A3-5 used the same wall-clock pattern; about 20 `Elapsed < N s` assertions ran on shared machines; `Is.Not.Empty` / `Is.GreaterThan(0)` assertions where the exact result of the program is known.
- **Fix.** `AlignmentCancellation.OnPoll` (internal, `AsyncLocal`: it flows to `Parallel.For` workers and does not touch other tests) + the test helper `PollCancellation.CancelInside(work, "Method", nth)`: the call runs ONCE and the token is cancelled at the n-th poll whose stack names the method (no sleep, no thread, no time bound; "polled inside X" and "mid-run" are asserted; the inputs shrank, e.g. 3 M-base suffix trees -> 300 kb); `SequenceAligner_Cancellation_Tests` (every `CancelledWhileRunning_*` test names its poll site); the direct-token polls of the B09 `GenomicAnalyzer*.cs` scans now call `AlignmentCancellation.Poll(token)` (the same check, plus the ambient scope and the seam). Wall-clock assertions: removed where an allocation bound already proves the point (`SequenceAligner_ResourceLimits_Tests` x2), replaced by deterministic allocation proxies (`GlobalCoOptimal` cap, `ShowAlign` width, `FindPalindromes`), `TandemRepeat` 2 kb baseline asserts the exact unit, the 1 Mbp complexity guards of the oracle tests keep a bound that is 10x the earlier one with the justification in a comment. Exact values: `Minimap2Seeds_Tests` / MCP `Minimap2ChainsTests` poly-A case = `mid_occ = 10`, `RS 24`, 35 anchors of `minimap2 --print-seeds`, `Stretcher_*` score 20 (installed `stretcher`), `CollectAnchors` of the ordinary pair = 1 866 anchors (installed minimap2). **Commit.** b04254759.

### F172 - EMBOSS programs (audit A5-7, WP42): the sequence-input qualifiers `-sbegin -send -sreverse -slower -supper -scircular -snucleotide -sprotein` of the 16 programs
- **Defect.** None of the ported programs accepted the qualifiers every EMBOSS program has for each input; the results of ranged / reverse-complemented input (positions, strand, numbering direction, offsets) were not available. Defects found on the way: `WaterAlign` returned the EMPTY alignment for a one-residue sequence (installed water 6.6.0 reports the best single column with the score -FLT_MAX: `ACGT` / `G` -> `G` at 3); fuzztran printed no coordinates for the reverse frames ("meaningless numbers", B09 F140 note) although they are deterministic (`S - |frame| - 3 start + 4`, with `S` = the range END for frame -3 of `-frame R` / `6`).
- **Source.** EMBOSS 6.6 `ajacd.c` (`acdSetSeq` / `acdSetSeqall` / `acdSetSeqset`), `ajseq.c` (`ajSeqSetRange`, `ajSeqReverseDo`, `ajSeqTrim`, `ajSeqIsNuc`, `ajSeqsetReverse`), `ajseqread.c`, `ajseqtype.c` (`ajSeqTypeCheckIn`, `seqTypeFix`), `ajmath.c` (`ajCvtSposToPosStart`), `ajalign.c`, the program sources of the 16 programs and `fuzztran.c` (raw.githubusercontent.com/kimrutherford/EMBOSS, `Seqeron-review/1.0`); installed EMBOSS 6.6.0.
- **Fix.** `EmbossSequenceQualifiers` (Infrastructure; `Parse` of a command-line fragment) + `EmbossInputSequence.Read` (Alignment: type check / repair, case, reverse complement with the `ajBaseComp` table, mirrored range, `ajSeqTrim`) -> `EmbossSequenceView`; `EmbossSequence.Qualifiers`, `EmbossProgramResult.MatrixName`, `EmbossAlignedSequence.WithView` (the two offsets swap sides for a reversed sequence); `NeedleProgram` / `WaterProgram` / `StretcherProgram` / `MatcherProgram` / `MergerProgram` (merger does not trim: whole sequences merged, `-sbegin` / `-send` have no effect; measured 180 / 180) / `MegaMerge(EmbossSequence, EmbossSequence, ..)` (megamerger merges the trimmed texts), qualifier-aware `Supermatcher` / `NeedleAll` (stream / set quirks measured: later `seqall` members keep the first member's offsets when only an end is given, a `seqset` decides the reversal from its first member), `FindPatternHits` / `FindProteinPatternHits` / `FindTranslatedPatternHits` / `FindTandemRepeatsEtandem` / `FindTandemRepeatsEquicktandem` / `DotMatcher.Compute` / `SeqMatchAll` (`SeqMatchAllHit`) / `CalculateDistanceMatrix` overloads with the qualifiers (per-program behaviour in `docs/algorithms/Alignment/Pairwise_Output_Formats_And_EMBOSS_Programs.md` section 9: etandem / seqmatchall / distmat ignore the range, dotmatcher scans the whole length over the cut text, fuzztran cuts the reversed text at the begin / end as given); `WaterAlign` aligns a one-residue sequence like the program; `TranslatedPatternHit.EmbossStart` / `EmbossEnd` of the reverse frames. MCP parameter `sequenceQualifiers` on 12 tools; `MultipleAlignmentDisplay.ShowAlign` calls `EmbossInputSequence.PositionStart` (the local `SposToPosStart` copy is removed: dedup of A5-7).
- **Oracle numbers.** `emboss_seqopts_oracle.tsv` (`generate_emboss_seqopts_oracle.py`, seed 20261127): 16 programs x 180 rows (needle, water, stretcher, matcher, supermatcher, needleall, merger, megamerger, seqmatchall, fuzznuc, fuzzpro, fuzztran, etandem, equicktandem, dotmatcher, distmat), 2 880 rows with random ranges (inside / at / beyond the ends / negative / zero / reversed), reverse, case, circular, type overrides and the refused combinations (3 - 17 % per program): all equal, including the whole pair-format text of the six aligners.
- **Tests.** `EmbossSequenceQualifiers_Oracle_Tests` (16 oracle tests + reader / parser / reverse-complement table unit tests), MCP `EmbossSequenceQualifiersToolsTests` (Alignment, Analysis; `merger` / `megamerger` `sequenceQualifiers` included). **Commit.** a54b4c74.

### F177 - EMBOSS programs (audit A6-2, WP43): the sequence-qualifier text is resolved as the ACD library of the program resolves it
- **Defect.** `EmbossSequenceQualifiers.Parse` accepted a strict subset of the command-line grammar and ignored the rest silently: (a) `-sbegin1 5` of a ONE-sequence program (`fuzznuc a.fa -pattern ACG -sbegin1 5` = `-sbegin 5`) was dropped (`Parse("-sbegin1 5", "").IsDefault` was true); (b) the unnumbered form after the files (`needle a.fa b.fa -sbegin 3` is `-sbegin2 3`: the qualifiers belong to the parameter that precedes them) was ignored for BOTH inputs; (c) `-sbegin1=5`, the unique abbreviations (`-sbeg1`, `-sre2`), `--sbegin`, `/sbegin`, `sbegin=5` and the boolean values (`-sreverse2 N`, `-slower1=yes`) were refused or dropped. **Correction of the audit claim:** the auditor's rule for the unnumbered form was incomplete: an abbreviation WITHOUT number after the second file (`-sbe 3`) applies to EVERY input (the master route is only taken when the general search finds the same item), and a numbered qualifier of another input or any non-sequence qualifier ends the tie (a later unnumbered qualifier then applies to all inputs): all measured below.
- **Source.** EMBOSS 6.6 `ajacd.c` (`acdArgsParse`, `acdIsQual`, `acdQualParse`, `acdFindQual`, `acdFindQualDetail`, `acdFindQualAssoc`, `acdFindQualMaster`, `acdTestQualC`, `acdTestAssoc`, `acdValIsBool`, `acdArgsScan`), `ajstr.c` (`ajStrToInt`, `ajStrToBool`, `ajStrIsFloat`, `ajStrPrefixS`, `ajStrIsAlnum`) (raw.githubusercontent.com mirrors of EMBOSS-6.6.0, `Seqeron-review/1.0`); installed EMBOSS 6.6.0: the `Commandline` echo of every program header and `EMBOSS_ACDLOG=1` (the ACD processing log: `set qualifier -sbegin[2] (param 0) = 3`, `set next qualifier ...` = the program's own statement of what each token set).
- **Fix.** `AcdCommandLine` (Infrastructure; a line-by-line port of the resolver for the qualifiers of the sequence inputs) over `EmbossAcdProfiles.g.cs` (the qualifier universe of each of the 16 programs, read from `<program> -help -verbose` by `generate_emboss_acd_profiles.py`: an abbreviation is unique only among ALL qualifiers of the program, `-se` is ambiguous in fuzznuc (`send,sequence`) and not in needle); `EmbossSequenceQualifiers.ParseInputs(program, text)` returns one entry per sequence input (1 or 2) and is used by the 16 MCP tools (`Parse(text, suffix)` stays, over a program-less profile); integer values = `strtol` decimal saturated to int (a 64-bit overflow is refused), boolean values = `ajStrToBool`; `-sformat -sask -squick -sdbname -sid -iquery -ufo -fformat -fopenfile` accepted without effect (residue strings have no file), `-ioffset` must be 0, every other qualifier or a stray word is refused (the program would take a stray word as a further parameter); the MCP `sequenceQualifiers` descriptions carry `EmbossSequenceQualifiers.CommandLineRules`.
- **Oracle numbers.** `emboss_acd_args_oracle.tsv` (`generate_emboss_acd_args_oracle.py`, seed 20261220): 16 programs x 130 random texts = **2 080 rows** (numbered / unnumbered names, unique and ambiguous abbreviations, `-` / `--` / `/` / no dash, any case, `=value`, `-no` negations, boolean and integer values the program accepts or refuses; 852 accepted, 1 016 refused by the program, 212 accepted by the program but not sequence qualifiers): the resolution (`name[pnum]=value`) of every accepted text and the refusal of every other equal on **2 080 / 2 080**; `emboss_seqopts_text_oracle.tsv` (`generate_emboss_seqopts_text_oracle.py`): 16 x 40 = **640 rows**, the same program runners as the A5-7 oracle (needle, water, stretcher, matcher, supermatcher, needleall, merger, megamerger, seqmatchall, fuzznuc, fuzzpro, fuzztran, etandem, equicktandem, dotmatcher, distmat) with the text after the sequence arguments: what the program REPORTS equal on 640 / 640.
- **Tests.** `EmbossAcdCommandLine_Oracle_Tests` (16), `EmbossSequenceQualifiersText_Oracle_Tests` (16), `EmbossSequenceQualifiers_CommandLine_Tests` (9: the forms of the audit, `-sbegin_asequence`, values, refusals with the program's messages), MCP `EmbossSequenceQualifiersToolsTests` (Alignment, Analysis: `fuzznuc -sbegin1 5`, `needle -sbegin 3 -send 8` = `-sbegin2 3 -send2 8`, `-sbe 3` on both, ambiguity). **Commit.** f49cacce.

### F178 - ALIGN-LOCAL-001 (audit A6-3, WP43): matcher `-gapopen` below `-gapextend`, integer options
- **Defect.** `MatcherProgram` refused every `-gapopen` below `-gapextend` (72 of 139 random rows: `-gapopen 0 .. 3` with the default `-gapextend 4` is a legal run of matcher 6.6.0; the first gap residue then costs less than a further one: SIM's `q = gapopen - gapextend` is negative; the scalar scoring rejected the positive `GapOpen`), `gapOpen = 1e308` was an `OverflowException` ("Value was either too large or too small for a Decimal"), `1.5` was accepted although the ACD says "Invalid integer value". **Correction of the audit claim:** the program does not die on a negative value, it RESETS it with a warning (`Warning: integer value out of range -1 less than (reset to) 0`; `-alternatives 0` -> 1) and runs; a value near `int.MaxValue` is UB in the program (its 32-bit scores overflow: `-gapopen 2147483647` prints a nonsense alignment with score 2147483647): the port refuses it by the integer-range check.
- **Fix.** `PairScoring.Create(.., allowPositiveGapOpen)` (internal; used only for `TopNTieOrder.Sim` with affine gaps), `SequenceAligner.EmbossInteger` (the ACD integer rule: finite, integral, 64-bit range, saturation, reset to the minimum with the warning), `MatcherProgram` reads `-alternatives`, `-gapopen`, `-gapextend` in the order of `matcher.acd`; the warnings are returned in the new `EmbossProgramResult.StandardError` (the program's stderr; `ErrorText` stays the error file).
- **Oracle numbers.** `matcher_gap_oracle.tsv` (`generate_matcher_gap_oracle.py`, seed 20261222): 872 rows (745 accepted by the program, 297 of them with `-gapopen` below `-gapextend`, 0 / 1 / 100, 36 with a reset warning; 127 refused or aborting; the 70 rows whose value is not a plain number - `abc`, `1e2`, the empty string - cannot be passed to the numeric API and are not compared): **all other rows equal**, alignment lists (score, coordinates, rows), the warning lines and the refusals.
- **Tests.** `SequenceAligner_MatcherGap_Tests` (3). **Commit.** 5b52e5f5.

### F179 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 / GENOMIC-TANDEM-001 (audit A6-4, WP43): null / degenerate arguments of the EMBOSS sets, Mash inputs and the report layer
- **Defect.** `SequenceAligner.NeedleAll` / `Supermatcher` with a null element of a set (`EmbossSetInput.Any` dereferenced `s.Qualifiers`), a member without `Name` / `Residues` (also `NeedleProgram` / `WaterProgram` / `StretcherProgram` / `MatcherProgram` / `MergerProgram` / `MegaMerge`) -> `NullReferenceException`; `SeqMatchAll` named the loop variable (`ArgumentNullException("s")`); `MashCommands.Dist` / `Triangle` with a null list element / `Records` / `Name` / `Sequence` -> `NullReferenceException` or "Value cannot be null (source)"; `EmbossReports.Fuzztran` with a hit made by hand (`default(TranslatedPatternHit)`): `InvalidOperationException` "Nullable object must have a value"; `EmbossReportWriter.Write` with `(EmbossReportFormat)9999` wrote GFF, with a null feature / field `NullReferenceException`.
- **Fix.** `SequenceAligner.RequireEmbossSet` / `RequireEmbossSequence` (`ArgumentNullException(paramName, "Sequence i is null." / "... has no Residues.")`), `RequireNoNullElements` in both `SeqMatchAll` overloads, `MashCommands.Sketches` (parameter names `references` / `queries` / `inputs`), `EmbossReports.*` (null names, `Fuzztran`: `ArgumentException` "Hit i has no EmbossStart / EmbossEnd"), `EmbossReportWriter.Write`: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for an undefined format and `ArgumentException` for a null field of the report or of a feature.
- **Tests.** `EmbossNullContract_Tests` (5), `MashCommands_Oracle_Tests` (null contract, parameter range). **Commit.** 12f13370 / 5b52e5f5.

### F180 - ALIGN-LOCAL-001 (audit A6-5, WP43): supermatcher `-wordlen` above the targets
- **Defect.** `Supermatcher(.., wordLength = int.MaxValue)` spent 30 s in the Rabin-Karp loops (`SupermatcherWords.Search` runs `wordLength - 1` multiplications and `wordLength` hash steps per query whatever the text length, no poll) and returned only the error-file text. **Measured on supermatcher 6.6.0:** the program loops too (`-wordlen 2147483647`: 8.9 s, a segmentation fault from about `-wordlen 1000000`, exit status 139) but prints `Error: no kmers found` on stderr whenever its word table is EMPTY: every `-wordlen` above the longest target (`-wordlen 24` / `30` with 23-base targets; not at `-wordlen 23`), or targets that hold only N / X runs; the error file lists every pair as usual; the exit status is 0.
- **Fix.** An empty word table returns before the loops: `EmbossProgramResult.StandardError` = `Error: no kmers found\n`, the error file as before (the loops cannot find anything; the program's crash for a huge word length is UB and not reproduced); the per-query poll stays. `SeqMatchAll` / `MegaMerge` / `DotMatcher` with `int.MaxValue` were verified (no hang: empty result / the program's `No match found` refusal).
- **Oracle numbers.** `supermatcher_wordlen_oracle.tsv` (`generate_supermatcher_wordlen_oracle.py`, seed 20261223): 260 rows (word length around, at and above the longest target and 100 / 1 000 / 100 000 / 999 999; 140 with `Error: no kmers found`): stderr, error file and the alignment list (names, scores) **260 / 260 equal**.
- **Tests.** `SequenceAligner_SupermatcherWordLength_Tests` (4: the oracle, `-wordlen int.MaxValue` returns at once, N-only targets, the sibling programs). **Commit.** 5b52e5f5.

### F181 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A6-7, WP43): minimap2 `-x PRESET` followed by an option whose value equals the default
- **Defect.** MCP `minimap2_chains` merged the preset with `Pick(given, default, fromPreset)` / `||` / `&&`: `k = 15`, `w = 10`, `minChainScore = 40`, `bestN = 5`, `rmq = false`, `outputSecondary = true` were indistinguishable from "not given" (`-x asm5 -k 15` is k = 15 in the program; the tool used the preset's 19), and a boolean could only be switched on. **Correction of the audit claim:** `-H` has NO negation in minimap2 2.26 (`main.c`: `ipt.flag |= MM_I_HPC`), so "`-H` off with `map-pb`" is not possible in the program either; the options with a value are `--rmq=yes|no`, `--secondary=yes|no` (and `--dual=yes|no`), the flags `-H -X -P --no-long-join --hard-mask-level --for-only --rev-only` only switch on.
- **Fix.** `MinimapOverrides` (nullable members = "not given") + `MinimapPresets.Apply(preset, overrides)` (the preset, then every given option, `-G` last; the ONE merge: it replaces the third copy of the field list in the MCP layer); `minimap2_chains` takes `int? k`, `int? w`, `int? maxGap`, `int? bandwidth`, `int? minChainScore`, `int? minAnchors`, `double? midOccFraction`, `int? minMidOcc` / `maxMidOcc`, `int? occDist`, `int? bandwidthLong`, `int? maxChainSkip`, `int? bestN`, `double? primaryRatio`, `bool? rmq`, `bool? outputSecondary`, `int? maxFragmentLength`, `int? maxIntronLength`, ... (null = not given; the flags stay `bool`), `mode = chains` uses the same resolved options.
- **Oracle numbers.** `minimap2_preset_oracle.jsonl.gz` got 40 `-x PRESET <options>` cases per preset after the A5-9 cases (the first 2 420 rows are byte-identical to the committed file; options `-k -w -g -r -n -m -p -N -e -f -U --max-chain-skip -M --rmq= --secondary= -H --no-long-join`, half of them with the DEFAULT value): 11 x 260 = **2 860 / 2 860 PAF texts equal** (the whole stdout).
- **Tests.** `Minimap2Presets_Tests` (exact counts per preset: cases, cases with `-F` / `-G`, cases with overrides, PAF lines), MCP `Minimap2PresetToolsTests` (whole PAF lines of `minimap2 -x asm5 -k 15`, `-w 10 -m 40 -n 3`, `-x ava-ont -m 40`). **Commit.** f78e1d38.

### F182 - GENOMIC-SIMILARITY-001 / ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A6-1 / A6-6, WP43; B09 for B06): streaming MinHash sketches, Mash refusals
- **Defect.** `KmerAnalyzer.CreateMinHashSketch` / `CreateFracMinHashSketch` built a `string` per distinct k-mer (`CountKmers` -> `HashSet<string>`) before hashing: auditor measurement 1 Mbp 1.8 s / 285 MB, 5 Mbp 9.3 s / 1.2 GB, 20 Mbp 40 s / 4.1 GB (`mash sketch` of the same genome: about 1 s, constant memory); `MashCommands` / `mash_dist` / `mash_triangle` inherited it and had no cancellation poll. **A6-6:** `mash dist -k 11 g.fa short.fa` (every record of a file shorter than k) exits with status 1 and "WARNING: All fasta records in input files were shorter than the k-mer size (11)." (or `ERROR: Did not find fasta records in "input files".` for a file without records: **correction of the audit claim:** the program prints the words "input files", not the file name); the port printed a result line. Two more crashes of the program have no output to mirror: `mash dist -i` with no reference sequence of k symbols (SIGFPE), `mash triangle -i` of sequences all shorter than k without `-E` (`std::out_of_range` abort) -> refused.
- **Fix.** A rolling 2-bit forward / reverse-complement window (k <= 32; two byte buffers above, FracMinHash has no k limit) hashed with the same MurmurHash3 input bytes, a bounded sorted set of the bottom-s hashes (Mash `MinHashHeap`) / the hashes <= max_hash (sourmash); optional trailing `CancellationToken` (a poll per 4 096 windows and per record); `MashCommands.Dist` / `Triangle` take a token (per input, per pair; the MCP tools pass theirs) and refuse a file without a record of k symbols with the program's text. Measured now (Release, the same genomes): 1 Mbp 0.11 s / 0.4 MB, 5 Mbp 0.26 s / 0.4 MB, 20 Mbp **0.83 s / 0.5 MB** (FracMinHash 1.05 s / 2 MB).
- **Oracle numbers.** The previous implementation is the test oracle (`KmerAnalyzer_SketchStreaming_Tests`): **1 200** random record sets for Mash (canonical and forward, k 1 .. 32, s 1 .. 100 000, case / N / IUPAC / U, null and short records, 708 non-empty) and **1 200** random sequences for FracMinHash (k up to 60, scaled 1 .. 1 000, abundance on / off, 535 non-empty, 100+ with k > 32), all 65 536 UTF-16 code units; the existing 440 + 660 Mash rows and the sourmash FracMinHash oracle unchanged; `mash_commands_oracle.jsonl.gz` got 80 `error` rows (`generate_mash_commands_oracle.py`, the program's non-zero statuses are kept: 1 and -8): status, message and exception equal **80 / 80**.
- **Tests.** `KmerAnalyzer_SketchStreaming_Tests` (8: equality, code units, allocation < 16 MB for 4 Mbp, cancellation), `MashCommands_Oracle_Tests` (error rows, null contract, cancellation), MCP `MashToolsTests`. **Commit.** 12f13370 (B06.md "Post-completion changes").

### F187 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A3-9c2, WP45): `minimap2 -c` / `-a` base-level alignment, the SAM writer and the ksw2 kernels of `align.c`
- **Defect.** Only the chaining stage of minimap2 2.26 was ported: no base-level alignment (`mm_align_skeleton`: ksw2 between the chained anchors, the end extensions, the Z-drop and inversion tests, `mm_fix_cigar`, `mm_update_extra`, `--eqx`), no `cg` / `cs` / `MD` / `NM ms AS nn ts de zd` output, no SAM writer, no spliced alignment (`ksw_exts2_sse`), no `ksw_ll_i16`; the PAF of `minimap2 -c` could not be produced.
- **Source (actually opened, lh3/minimap2 v2.26 at raw.githubusercontent.com, neutral User-Agent).** `align.c`, `hit.c`, `pe.c`, `map.c`, `format.c`, `main.c`, `options.c`, `bseq.c` / `bseq.h`, `index.c`, `seed.c`, `lchain.c`, `splitidx.c`, `ksw2.h`, `ksw2_ll_sse.c`, `ksw2_exts2_sse.c`, `ksw2_extz2_sse.c`, `ksw2_extd2_sse.c`, `ketopt.h`, `kseq.h`, `mmpriv.h`, `minimap.h`, `sketch.c`, `sdust.c`.
- **Reference cross-check.** Installed 2.26-r1175: **2 700 / 2 700** whole standard outputs equal (`minimap2_align_oracle.jsonl.gz`, `generate_minimap2_align_oracle.py`, seed 20261221): `-c` with `cg` / `cs` short and long / `MD` / `--eqx` for `map-ont`, `map-hifi`, `map-pb` (homopolymer-compressed), `asm5`, `asm10`, `asm20` (150 each), random alignment options (300), SAM (300: flags 0 / 16 / 256 / 2048, MAPQ, `SA`, clipping, header with `@PG CL`, `-Y -L --secondary-seq --sam-hit-only -R -y -Q`), short reads (300), spliced alignment (300: `-u f|r|b|n`, `-J 0|1`, `-C`, `--junc-bonus`, `--junc-bed` BED12 / BED6, `-G`), repeat families (300 secondary hits), Z-drop / inversion rescue (300: 102 `tp:A:I` cases). The C kernels `ksw_ll_i16`, `ksw_exts2_sse`, `ksw_extz2_sse`, `ksw_extd2_sse` (v2.26, compiled here with `gcc -msse4.1`, driver `scripts/alignment/ksw2/ksw2_oracle_driver.c`) equal `Ksw2Aligner.LocalScore` / `ExtendS2` / `ExtendZ2` / `ExtendD2` on **2 000 / 2 000** random inputs (every field of `ksw_extz_t` and the CIGAR); this also resolves the open "never compared with the C program" caveat of F125. CPU independence: the Debian binary has one SSE4.1 code path (no `cpuid`, no AVX, `pblendvb` / `pmaxsb` present, no `_sse41` / `_sse2` function suffixes); `valgrind -q --track-origins=yes` on two cases of each of the 27 oracle groups: clean.
- **Fix.** `Minimap2Chaining.Align.cs` (every function of `align.c`), `Minimap2Chaining.Output.cs` (`mm_write_paf3`, `write_tags`, `write_cs_or_MD`, `mm_write_sam3`, `mm_write_sam_hdr`), `Minimap2Chaining.Index.cs` (`mm_idx_getseq*`, `mm_idx_bed_read` / `mm_idx_bed_junc`, `mm_idx_alt_read`), `hit.c` (`mm_set_parent` with DP maxima and ALT scores, `mm_select_sub`, `mm_sync_regs`, `mm_hit_sort`, full `mm_set_mapq` + `mm_set_inv_mapq`, `mm_filter_regs`, `mm_squeeze_a`), `Minimap2Chaining.Pipeline.cs` (`mm_map_frag` with `align_regs`), `Ksw2Aligner.Splice.cs` (`ExtendS2`), `Ksw2Aligner.Local.cs` (`LocalScore`: the 16-bit striped local alignment lane by lane, the maximum before the lazy-F loop, padding lanes: an end coordinate beyond the query is possible and `mm_align1_inv` then starts before the region); `MinimapMapOptions` gets `Cigar`, `Eqx`, splice direction / flank / old model, `MinKswLength`, anchor extension, `MaxClipRatio`, rank options, `PairOrientation` / `PairBonus`, `NoEndFilter`, `NoInversion`, `AltDrop`, `MaxQueryLength`, `HashSeed`, `NoHashName`, `Scoring.Ambiguous`; `MinDpMax` default is 80 (the program sets it once from the default `-m` / `-A`, the old doc claimed it followed them); `ExtendD2` / `ExtendD` accept `e2 = 0` (`-E 2,0` is legal in the program; the F133 check refused it); `Minimap2Program` runs a whole command line; MCP `minimap2_map` (new) and `ksw2_extend` variants `exts2` / `ll`. (An `Optimize = true` for the Alignment project was tried to speed the lane emulation up 4x and reverted: it inlines `PairwiseIdentityDistance` / `AffineFill`, which two stack-frame based cancellation tests look for; the new oracle tests therefore run unoptimised, about 2 minutes wall / 8 CPU minutes on 4 cores.)
- **Tests.** `Minimap2Align_Tests` (13), `Ksw2SpliceLocal_Tests` (6), `Ksw2_GapPenalties_...` (e2 = 0), MCP `Minimap2MapToolTests` (7), tool documents / contract tests. **Commit.** aa614deed.

### F188 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A5-9b / A5-9c, WP45): the multi-segment (paired-read) mode of minimap2 2.26 and `mm_pair`
- **Defect.** `minimap2 -x sr ref.fa r1.fq r2.fq` (and interleaved reads with `--frag=yes`) was not ported: no segment ids in the anchors, no multi-segment `comput_sc` rule, no `mm_select_sub_multi`, no `mm_seg_gen`, no `mm_pair` (proper pairs, paired mapping quality, `pe_thru`), no `pe_ori` flipping, no mate fields in SAM.
- **Source (opened).** `map.c` (`collect_minimizers`, `mm_map_frag`, `worker_for`), `pe.c` (`mm_select_sub_multi`, `mm_set_pe_thru`, `mm_pair`), `hit.c` (`mm_seg_gen`), `lchain.c:123`, `bseq.c` (`mm_bseq_read_frag2`, `mm_qname_same`), `format.c` (`mm_write_sam3` mates).
- **Reference cross-check.** **2 100 / 2 100** whole outputs equal (`minimap2_pair_oracle.jsonl.gz`, `generate_minimap2_pair_oracle.py`, seed 20261222): two query files and an interleaved file, PAF without `-c`, PAF with `-c`, SAM; FR pairs with inserts 100 - 1500 bp and substitutions / indels, unmapped / wrongly oriented / distant mates, overlapping mates, adapters, N bases, repeats, 1 - 3 fragments per file, FASTA and FASTQ, `/1` `/2`, three reads with one name (`FI:i:`), `--frag=yes` without a preset (forward-forward), options `-F -N -p -k -w -A -B -O -E -s -z --end-bonus --no-pairing -r -g -n -m -M --secondary=yes --heap-sort=no -t -K -I -2`. The 2.26 program has no `--pe-ori` option (the orientation is the preset's, `-x sr`: 1 = FR, else FF): the library option `PairOrientation` carries it.
- **Fix.** `Minimap2Chaining.Pe.cs` (`SelectSubMulti`, `SetPeThru`, `Pair`, `SegGen`), segment ids in `Mm128.Y` bits 48 - 55 (`CollectSeedArray`, `PrepareQuerySeeds`: sketch per segment, offset positions, sdust per segment, `mm_seed_mz_flt` over all), the segment-aware `Score` (`comput_sc`: `MinimapChainOptions.Segments`), the re-chaining test of `mm_map_frag` for the number of chained segments, `collect_seed_hits_heap` (`--heap-sort`, set by the `sr` preset: anchors with equal reference position in the heap order, `ks_heapmake` / `ks_heapdown` ported), `MapFragment` (public: `MinimapFragmentResult`), `pe_ori` flipping and `--no-pairing` in `MapFragmentRegs`, the pair reader of `Minimap2Program`; presets `sr` / `splice` set `FragmentMode`, `PairOrientation`, `HeapSort`, `SpliceForward` / `Reverse` / `Flank`.
- **Tests.** `Minimap2Pair_Tests` (8), MCP `PairedReads_TwoFiles_AreAProperPair`. **Commit.** b6feca9cf.

### F189 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A5-9d, WP45): the other mapping / alignment options of `main.c` and the program around the pipeline
- **Defect.** No minimap2 option of the mapping and alignment stages beyond the chaining options was reachable: `-I` (the index in parts), `--split-prefix`, `--junc-bed`, `--alt` / `--alt-drop`, `--qstrand`, `-u` / `-J` / `-C` / `--junc-bonus` / `--splice-flank`, `--cap-sw-mem`, `--max-chain-iter`, `--chain-gap-scale` (MCP only), `--no-pairing`, `-R`, `-L`, `-Y`, `--secondary-seq`, `--sam-hit-only`, `--paf-no-hit`, `-y`, `-Q`, `--max-qlen`, `--seed`, `--no-hash-name`, `--min-occ-floor`, `--score-N`, `--end-seed-pen`, `--min-dp-len`, `--max-clip-ratio`, `--no-end-flt`, `-o`, `-v`, `-V`, `-h`, the option checks of `mm_check_opt`, getopt permutation and abbreviations, the kseq reader and its quirks.
- **Source (opened).** `main.c`, `options.c`, `ketopt.h`, `kseq.h`, `bseq.c`, `index.c` (`mm_idx_gen`: `mini_batch_size = min(50M, batch_size)`), `splitidx.c`, `map.c` (`merge_hits`, `mm_split_merge`), `format.c` (`sam_write_rg_line`).
- **Facts measured and ported.** `-I` splits the reference into parts of mini-batches `min(50 Mbases, -I)` and every part is mapped on its own (the first run of this batch claimed "no effect" and was wrong: 7 of 2 310 cases differed); `mid_occ` is computed from the first part; SAM without `@SQ` and a warning; `--split-prefix` merges (`merge_hits`) and writes `@SQ` after `@PG`, and with two query files without the fragment mode the merge pairs the wrong reads (reproduced); `-u f|r|b` switches splice on only at `mm_mapopt_update`; `-x splice -x asm5` is cumulative; `-V` returns at once; `-o FILE -o -` keeps the file; an invalid `-R` prints the header without the line and exits 1; `--idx-no-seq` with `-c` is an error; `-N 0` changes to `--secondary=no`; `kseq` details (a blank CRLF line is a 1-character sequence, malformed FASTQ ends the file with a warning, `U` becomes `T`). Without effect on the standard output (carried by oracle cases): `-t -K -2 -d --bucket-bits --no-kalloc --cap-kalloc --print-qname --print-seeds --print-chains --print-aln-seq`.
- **Reference cross-check.** **2 401 / 2 401** (`minimap2_options_oracle.jsonl.gz`, `generate_minimap2_options_oracle.py`, seed 20261223): groups `opt_index_parts`, `opt_chain`, `opt_output`, `opt_alt`, `opt_qstrand`, `opt_ava`, `opt_input` (300 each), a query of 610 kb with `CG:B:I` (`-L`), `opt_errors` (300: stdout, stderr at `-v 2`, exit status).
- **Fix.** `Minimap2Program.Run` (options, ketopt, readers, parts, merge, header, errors), `MinimapPresets.ApplyOn` (cumulative presets), `Minimap2Chaining.MergeParts`, `Minimap2Chaining.Index.cs`. `--spsc` named in the audit text does not exist in 2.26 (`main.c` option table).
- **Tests.** `Minimap2Options_Tests` (9). **Commit.** aa5606b03.

- **Finding.** `MultipleAlignmentDisplay.ShowAlign` ported the text output only; the HTML output of the program (`<pre>` wrapper, `<font color=...>` ranges of `-highlight`) and the ACD `range` syntax of `-highlight` / `-uppercase` were missing.

- **Fix.** `ShowAlignOptions.Html` / `Highlight`; `EmbossRangeSpec.Parse` (new, public, Analysis) = the program's range parser (strtok behaviour kept: `3-5,7-9` gives the text `,` for the first pair and none for the second; `a+n`, `a:b`, `a..b`, odd-count / `0` / `from > to` refused as the program refuses them, `@file` with `#` comments); the colour insertion repeats `embShowColourRange` on the growing string (the length of the overlap test and the clipping include the tags inserted so far) and `showInsertHTML`; MCP `showalign` gets `html` / `highlight` and parses `uppercase` with the same parser (`x-y` is an empty range in the program, no longer an error).
- **Oracle.** `showalign_html_oracle.jsonl` (`generate_showalign_html_oracle.py`, seed 20261127): 300 random alignments with every text option of F148 and `-html` with random `-highlight` (0-5 pairs of the forms `a-b`, `a:b`, `a..b`, `a+n`, colours incl. empty = red and `dark-blue`, overlapping and out-of-range pairs, `3-5,7-9`, range file): **300 / 300 texts byte-equal**.

### F192 - EMBOSS programs (audit A5-8c (a) (b), WP46): NCBI-style FASTA identifiers and pattern files
- **Defect.** (a) `EmbossFastaReader` ported only the plain branch of the `fasta` input format (`seqReadNcbi` -> `ajSeqParseFasta`); a header with `|` (`sp|P12345|NAME_HUMAN desc`, `gb|AB123456.1|locus`, `gi|1|gb|X|y`, `gnl|BL_ORD_ID|n`, ...) was read as a plain id, and `seqSetName` (`:` split, `,/\` -> `_`) and the `EMBOSS_nnn` name of an unnamed sequence were missing. (b) `fuzznuc` / `fuzzpro` / `fuzztran -pattern @file` (and `-pname`, `-pformat`, per-pattern `<mismatch=n>`) existed for the hits only: the reports knew one pattern; `FuzznucPattern.ParsePatternFile` cut a FASTA name at the first blank, numbered unnamed patterns by position instead of by line and ignored `<mismatch=n>`.
- **Sources actually opened (raw.githubusercontent.com, `Seqeron-review/1.0`).** EMBOSS `ajax/core/ajseqread.c` (`ajSeqParseNcbi` in full, `ajSeqParseFasta`, `seqReadNcbi`, `seqSetName`, the `fasta` / `ncbi` / `gifasta` / `pearson` format table), `ajstr.c` (the `ajStrToken*` family: leading delimiters skipped on assignment, runs of delimiters skipped after a token, reset on exhaustion), `ajax/core/ajpat.c` (`ajPatlistSeqRead`, `ajPatternSeqNewList`, `ajPatlistSeqDoc`, `patSeqInformat`), `ajax/acd/ajacd.c` (`acdSetPattern`), `emboss/fuzznuc.c` / `fuzzpro.c` / `fuzztran.c`, `nucleus/embpat.c` (`embPatlistSeqSearchAll`).
- **Fix.** `EmbossNcbiHeader.Parse` (Infrastructure, internal) = `ajSeqParseNcbi` (prefixes gi, gnl, gnl|BL_ORD_ID| (recursion), bbs / lcl, pat, pdb, gb / emb / dbj / tpd / tpg / sp / ref, pir / prf, and the "last two or three barred tokens" rule incl. its unsigned loop `i < nt - 3` that a header with exactly two barred tokens turns into 2^32 steps: the program needs ~28 s and leaves the sequence unnamed); `EmbossFastaReader.ParseHeader` uses it first and `seqSetName`; unnamed sequences are `EMBOSS_001`, `EMBOSS_002`, ... in the order of the unnamed ones. `EmbossPatternList.Read` (Analysis, public) = `ajPatlistSeqRead` (measured: `-pformat fasta` is the program's format 0 = decided by the first line; blank lines of a simple file count in `<pname><n>` and an empty pattern is dropped; a FASTA name is the whole header; `<mismatch=n>`); `EmbossReports.Fuzznuc` / `Fuzzpro` / `Fuzztran` and `EmbossReportPrograms` take pattern lists (forward hits of every pattern, then the complement hits of every pattern; fuzztran frame by frame, pattern by pattern; the header table has a row per pattern); `FuzznucPattern.ParsePatternFile` delegates to `EmbossPatternList` (names, numbering, mismatches: `NamedPattern.Mismatch`); MCP `emboss_report_file` gets `patternFile`, `patternName`, `patternFormat`.
- **Oracle.** `emboss_ncbi_pattern_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_emboss_ncbi_pattern_oracle.py`, seed 20261221): 3 programs x 24 formats x 8 runs with NCBI-style headers + the same with pattern files (simple / FASTA style, `<mismatch=n>`, `-pname`, `-pformat`, `-pmismatch`, `-complement`, `-frame`, every report option) + 6 runs with two-barred-token headers: **1 110 / 1 110 report files byte-equal** (the 12 000 of F184 still equal).
- **Registered (precise).** (c) the `diffseq` writer needs the seven-tag program `diffseq` itself (`diffseq.c` 1 148 lines + `embWordMatchMin` + feature-file output `-aoutfeat` / `-boutfeat`): registered as A5-8c3; protein patterns with mismatches (`fuzzpro` / `fuzztran` with `<mismatch=n>` in a pattern file: the program runs `embPatBruteForce` with the protein alphabet; the port's protein search has no mismatches): registered as A5-8c2.
- **Tests.** `EmbossNcbiPattern_Oracle_Tests` (6 + 2 oracle groups, worked values of the header parser and the pattern list), `GenomicAnalyzer_PatternHits_Oracle_Tests.ParsePatternFile_PlainAndFasta` (numbering and names corrected to the measured ones), MCP `FuzznucPatternFile_IsOnePatternPerRowOfTheHeader`. **Commit.** d53da9d17

### F193 - Mash (audit A5-10b, WP46): the sketch file (`.msh`, Cap'n Proto), `sketch -o`, `info`, `paste`, `.msh` inputs of `dist` / `triangle` / `screen`
- **Finding.** Mash's sketches could not be written or read as files: `mash_dist` / `mash_triangle` / `mash_screen` accepted FASTA only, there was no `sketch`, `info` or `paste`. The `.msh` file is a flat unpacked Cap'n Proto message of `MinHash.capnp` built by `capnp::MallocMessageBuilder`; a byte-identical file needs its allocation reproduced.
- **Sources actually opened (raw.githubusercontent.com, `Seqeron-review/1.0`).** marbl/Mash v2.3 `Sketch.cpp` (`writeToCapnp`, `initFromFiles`, `initParametersFromCapnp`, `loadCapnp`, `setAlphabetFromString`, `sketchFile` incl. the multi-file read rotation, `setMinHashesForReference`), `Sketch.h`, `capnp/MinHash.capnp`, `CommandInfo.cpp`, `CommandPaste.cpp`, `CommandSketch.cpp`, `CommandDistance.cpp`, `Command.cpp` (`printColumns`), `MinHashHeap.cpp`, `HashSet.cpp`; capnproto v1.0.1 `message.c++` (`MallocMessageBuilder::allocateSegment`: first segment 1 024 words, then `nextSize` = the total so far), `arena.c++` (`BuilderArena::allocate`), `layout.c++` (`WireHelpers::allocate`: far pointer + landing pad when the object does not fit into the segment of its pointer); the installed `mash` 2.3 and the field layout read off its files (data section: `kmerSize` / `windowSize`, `minHashesPerWindow` + the bits concatenated / noncanonical / preserveCase, `error` + `hashSeed` XOR 42; pointers: referenceListOld, locusList, alphabet, referenceList).
- **Fix.** `MashSketchFile` (Analysis): `Write` (the arena: segments, bump allocation, far pointers, composite lists, text / u32 / u64 lists; the order of `writeToCapnp`) and `Read` (any segmentation, single and double far pointers); `MashCommands.Sketch` / `SketchFile` (`-k -s -S -n -i -r -m -c -g -I -C -l`; a read set of several files is ONE sketch fed from the files in rotation, `Interleave`), `Info` (`-H -t -c -d`, `printColumns`), `Paste` (first file's parameters, incompatible files skipped, larger sketches reduced, counts dropped), `MashInput.SketchFile` (a `.msh` among the inputs of `Dist` / `Triangle` / `Screen`: the first file's k / s / seed / strand mode are inherited, later incompatible files skipped, larger reduced), `SeedFromOption` (measured: `-S 4294967295` is stored as 0); MCP `mash_sketch`, `mash_info`, `mash_paste` and `msh:` + base64 inputs of the other Mash tools. `MinHashSketch.Counts` (additive).
- **Oracle numbers.** `mash_msh_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_mash_msh_oracle.py`): 120 runs (genomes and read sets, 1 - 3 files, k 4 - 32, s 1 - 3 000, seeds incl. 42 = referenceListOld, `-n -i -I -C -r -m -c -g -l`; multi-segment messages with far pointers): the files **byte-equal** (read-set files: everything but the ORDER of the counts, see below) and `mash info` default / `-t` / `-H` / `-d` / `-c` **600 / 600** text-equal; `mash_msh_commands_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_mash_msh_commands_oracle.py`): 160 runs - `paste` 35 (byte-equal files), `dist` 51, `triangle` 38, `screen` 36 with sketch files among the inputs (mixed with sequence files, other parameters / smaller / larger sketches): all equal.
- **Measured quirk.** `mash info` prints its table with `printColumns`, which reads the terminal width with `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` into an UNINITIALISED struct when the standard input is no terminal: measured on the installed binary the width behaves as unlimited, and as 0 (every column on its own line) for a file without sketches, identically over repeated runs and stdin kinds; the port reproduces both. The seed 4294967295 of `-S` is stored as 0.
- **Registered (precise).** A5-10b3: a read-set sketch stores the multiplicities (`counts32`) in the iteration order of Mash's `robin_hood::unordered_map` (`HashSet::toCounts`) while the hashes are sorted, so they are not parallel to the hashes (a Mash defect); the port writes the right multiset parallel to the hashes (30 of 120 oracle rows differ in the ORDER only); the exact order needs the bundled `robin_hood.h` (`hash_int`, power-of-two table, Robin-Hood insertion, backward-shift erase) ported and fed with the insert / erase sequence of `MinHashHeap::tryInsert` (a libstdc++ `unordered_map` emulation was written and validated against g++ on 300 random sequences, but Mash uses robin_hood and it was removed). A5-10b2: the Bloom filter `-b` (`bloom_filter.hpp`, fixed salts), the alphabets `-a -z -Z` (protein sketches, the 6-frame `screen` of amino-acid queries), `mash taxscreen` (`CommandTaxScreen.cpp`).
- **Tests.** `MashSketchFile_Oracle_Tests` (4), `MashSketchFileCommands_Oracle_Tests` (1), MCP `MashSketch_Info_Paste_AsTheProgram`, `ToolRegistrationContractTests`. **Commit.** 2015bd1b1

### F194 - Mash (audit A5-10b3, WP47): the iteration order of the counts of a read-set sketch (`robin_hood::unordered_map`)
- **Defect.** F193 wrote the multiplicities (`counts32`) of a read-set sketch parallel to the sorted hashes; Mash lists them in the iteration order of the `robin_hood::unordered_map` of `HashSet` (`toCounts`), so 30 of the 120 oracle files differed in the order of the counts.
- **Sources actually opened (raw.githubusercontent.com, `Seqeron-review/1.0`).** marbl/Mash v2.3 `src/mash/robin_hood.h` (version 3.9.1: `hash_int`, `Table::keyToIdx`, `doCreateByKey`, `insert_move`, `shiftUp`, `shiftDown`, `erase`, `try_increase_info`, `increase_size`, `rehashPowerOfTwo`, `init_data`, `clear`, iterator `fastForward`), `HashSet.cpp` / `HashSet.h`, `MinHashHeap.cpp` / `MinHashHeap.h`.
- **Fix.** `RobinHoodMap` (Analysis, internal) = the flat map of the header, line by line; `KmerAnalyzer.CreateReadsMinHashSketch` keeps the counts in it (insert / add / erase exactly as `MinHashHeap::tryInsert`) and returns them in bucket order.
- **Oracle.** (a) `robin_hood_order_oracle.tsv` (`generate_robin_hood_order_oracle.py` compiles the real header with g++ and `robin_hood_order_harness.cpp`): 150 deterministic operation streams (bottom-s heap streams with 32- and 64-bit keys, random insert / erase) - size and FNV-1a over (key, value) in iteration order: **150 / 150 equal**; (b) `mash_reads_msh_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_mash_reads_msh_oracle.py`): 140 read-set `.msh` files of the installed `mash sketch -r` (10 - 1 200 reads, k 4 - 32, s 1 - 3 000, `-m -c -g -n`, 1 - 2 files): **140 / 140 byte-equal**, and the 120 files of F193 are now byte-equal in full (the order-insensitive comparison was removed).
- **Tests.** `RobinHoodMap_Oracle_Tests` (2), `MashSketchFile_Oracle_Tests.ReadSetSketchFile_EqualsMash_ByteForByte_CountsInRobinHoodOrder`, `SketchFile_EqualsMash_ByteForByte` (read sets now byte-equal). **Commit.** e3fae6804

### F195 - EMBOSS programs (audit A5-8c2, WP47): protein patterns with mismatches (fuzzpro / fuzztran `-pmismatch`), and the duplicate hits of fuzznuc with a range and mismatches
- **Defect.** (a) `fuzzpro` / `fuzztran` with `-pmismatch` / `<mismatch=n>` had no mismatch search (the port's protein search was exact only). (b) Measured while doing (a): the recursive brute force (`embPatBruteForce` -> `patOUBrute`, used for every pattern with a range when mismatches are allowed) pushes one hit PER SUCCESSFUL UNROLLING, so a window two unrollings match is listed twice (`fuzznuc -pmismatch 1 'N(0,1)A(0,1)G'` on `TTAGTT`: `3 4` twice); `PatternHitsLiteral` (the path of the report programs) listed each window once, sorted by position - 109 of 300 oracle patterns have such duplicates.
- **Sources actually opened (raw.githubusercontent.com, `Seqeron-review/1.0`).** EMBOSS `nucleus/embpat.c` (`embPatClassify`, `embPatGetTypeII`, `embPatCompileII`, `embPatFuzzSearchAllII`, `embPatBruteForce`, `patOUBrute`, `patBrute*`, `embPatTUBInit`, `embPatTUBSearch`, `embPatPushHit`, `patProteinTranslate`), `nucleus/embpatlist.c` (`embPatternSeqSearchAll`: the list is reversed for the first pass, popped as pushed for the complement pass), `emboss/fuzzpro.c`; the installed fuzzpro / fuzztran / fuzznuc 6.6.0.
- **Fix.** `ProteinPattern.ExpandPaths` / `TubText` / `UsesTarhioUkkonenBleasby`, `GenomicAnalyzer.FindProteinPatternHits` / `FindTranslatedPatternHits` (`maxMismatches`; `ProteinPatternHit.Mismatches`, `TranslatedPatternHit.Mismatches`): Baeza-Yates-Perleberg = a Hamming scan; Tarhio-Ukkonen-Bleasby (`EmbossTubSearch`, a verbatim port: its skip table knows A-Z only, so windows with a stop `*` are skipped - the first Hamming-scan version differed on 3 of 250 fuzztran rows); the recursive matcher (mismatches only in the mandatory part, a match fails when the sequence ends with elements left over, one hit per unrolling in push order); the fatal "Mismatches (n) must be less than the real pattern length (m)" of type 6; reports: Score = length - mismatches, `*mismatch` note after `*pat`; `PatternHitsLiteral` returns the program's order for a range pattern with mismatches (forward pass in push order, complement pass in reversed push order, duplicates kept; `EmbossReports.ReverseOrder` no longer re-sorts it); MCP `fuzzpro` / `fuzztran` `mismatch`, `emboss_report_file` `maxMismatches` for all three programs, hit items with `mismatches`.
- **Oracle.** `fuzzpro_mismatch_oracle.tsv` (`generate_fuzzpro_mismatch_oracle.py`, 1 000 random syntax-tree patterns, `-pmismatch` 1 - 3, planted near-misses, sequences with X B Z U J O * and lower case; 750 fuzzpro + 250 fuzztran (`-frame 6`) rows, 180 rejected by the program): **all equal** (multiset of window / length / mismatches, and the ERR rows); `fuzznuc_dup_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_fuzznuc_dup_oracle.py`, 300 range patterns with 1 - 2 mismatches, both strands, excel report): **all equal**.
- **Tests.** `GenomicAnalyzer_ProteinPatternMismatch_Oracle_Tests` (2), `EmbossFuzznucRangeMismatch_Oracle_Tests` (1), MCP `FuzzproFuzztranTests`. **Commit.** ec1a8d54a

- **Finding.** `diffseq` and its seven-tag report format were not ported (`EmbossReportFormat.DiffSeq` was a name that every program refused).
- **Sources actually opened.** EMBOSS `emboss/diffseq.c` (all 1 148 lines: `diffseq_DiffList`, `diffseq_Diff`, `diffseq_WordMatchListConvDiffToFeat`, `diffseq_Features`), `ajax/core/ajreport.c` (`reportWriteDiffseq`, `ajReportWriteHeader`, `ajReportWriteTail`, `ajReportAddFileF`), `ajax/core/ajfeat.c` (`ajFeatNewBetween`, `ajFeatTagSet`), `nucleus/embword.c` (`embWordGetTable`, `embWordMatchMin`), `nucleus/embprop.c` (`embPropTransition` / `embPropTransversion`), `diffseq.acd` (the installed one: `taglist`); the installed diffseq 6.6.0.

### F197 - Mash (audit A5-10b2, WP47): the Bloom filter `-b`
- **Finding.** `mash sketch -b` (and the `-b` of dist / triangle / screen read sets) was not ported.
- **Sources actually opened.** marbl/Mash v2.3 `MinHashHeap.cpp` / `MinHashHeap.h` (`tryInsert`, the filter parameters), `bloom_filter.hpp` (`bloom_parameters::compute_optimal_parameters`, `bloom_filter`, `generate_unique_salt`, `hash_ap`, `compute_indices`), `sketchParameterSetup.cpp` (`-b` implies `-r`, excludes `-m`), `Command.cpp` (the `Size` option type); the installed mash 2.3.
- **Measured quirk.** `MinHashHeap` asks for the optimal parameters with a false-positive probability of 0: the search gives -infinity bits for one hash function, the cast of -infinity to `unsigned long long` is out of range (0x8000000000000000 on x86-64) and is cut to `maximum_size` = 8 x the bound: ONE hash function over `bound x 8` bits (a Mac-native ARM build would convert to 0 and behave differently: the installed x86-64 binary is the oracle).
- **Implementation.** `MashBloomFilter` (Analysis, internal), `KmerAnalyzer.CreateReadsMinHashSketch(bloomFilterBytes)`, `MashReadsOptions.BloomFilterBytes`, `MashCommands.ParseSize`, MCP `bloomFilter` of `mash_sketch` / `mash_dist` / `mash_triangle`.
- **Oracle.** `mash_bloom_msh_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_mash_bloom_oracle.py`): 130 read sets, filters of 8 bytes - 2 MB: the whole `.msh` file byte-equal: **130 / 130**.
- **Registered (precise).** A5-10b2 remainder: the alphabets `-a -z -Z` (protein sketches, the 6-frame `screen` of amino-acid queries), `mash taxscreen` (`CommandTaxScreen.cpp`).
- **Tests.** `MashSketchFile_Oracle_Tests.BloomFilterSketchFile_EqualsMash_ByteForByte`, `ParseSize_AsMashCommandCpp`. **Commit.** ec1a8d54a
