## Duplication removed

- (WP49) `postnuc` and `postpro` shared two copies of `extendBackward` / `extendForward`: now `MummerExtension` (the nucmer oracle of 434 runs unchanged); the FASTA reader (`Read_String`) and the `mgaps` text writer are shared by `nucmer`, `promer` and the delta programs (`MummerFastaReader`, `MummerMgapsText`); `NucmerSwAlign.AlignEngine` takes the matrix type (the BLOSUM tables of `sw_alignscore.hh`) instead of a second engine; the amino-acid matching of `promer` and the `mummer` command use one engine (`MummerIndex`). `nucmer` itself keeps the canonical suffix-tree engine (`FindCommonRegions`, verified by the same oracle) - two engines verified against the same program, not two copies of one: noted for the sweep.

- ALIGN-MULTI-001 / REPEAT (audit A2-14, F104): the exact `printf("%.Nf")` formatter (BigInteger, ties to even) was written twice - `RepeatFinder.FormatCFixed` (TRF output) and a new one for the ClustalW guide-tree files; both now call `CFormat.Fixed` (Infrastructure, additive); `RepeatFinder.FormatCFixed` stays as a one-line delegate for its tests. `SequenceAligner.CreateSets` of the ClustalW state (private, steps of a binary NJ tree) was replaced by the faithful `groupSeqs` port `ClustalWCreateSets`, which also serves user trees - one implementation for both.

- GENOMIC-MOTIFS-001: `GenomicAnalyzer.FindMotif` was a copy of `MotifFinder.FindExactMotif` (same suffix-tree search, differing in sorting/validation) → delegates (F18); `FindKnownMotifs` no longer carries its own suffix-tree loop for few motifs but calls the canonical KMP `KmerAnalyzer.FindKmerPositions`; IUPAC and reverse-complement handling call `MotifFinder.FindDegenerateMotif` / `DnaSequence.GetReverseComplementString` (no new matcher).

- ALIGN-GLOBAL-001: the cancellable overload `GlobalAlign(string,string,scoring,ct,progress)` re-implemented the full NW fill/traceback; all 4 overloads now share `GlobalAlignCore` (same diagonal>up>left tie order, same progress/cancellation points). Pooled-buffer copy path removed. Behaviour change: empty input to the typed cancellable overload now returns the NW all-gap alignment (consistent with the typed non-cancellable overload) instead of `AlignmentResult.Empty`.

- ALIGN-SEMI-001: `SemiGlobalAlignCore` duplicated the NW fill; removed — `GlobalAlignCore` and semi-global both use `LinearAlignCore(…, fitting)`. Byte-identical outputs on 1628 cases.

- ALIGN-MULTI-001: `ReconcileAlignments` + `MultipleAlignClassic` no longer carry two merge variants (one `MergeCenterAlignments`); the T-Coffee primary-library loop existed twice (`BuildExtendedLibrary` and `BuildPrimaryLibraryForDiagnostics`) → one `BuildPrimaryLibrary`; private 4-mer hash → Core `CountKmersSpan`; the progressive/iterative/consistency aligners share `PairwiseIdentityDistance` / `BuildProgressiveGuideTree` (UPGMA is re-implemented here only because Phylogenetics depends on Alignment, circular reference — B09 sweep to re-check).

- GENOMIC-ORF-001: the hard-coded `StopCodons` / `IsStopCodon` / `StartCodon` constants → `GeneticCode` (via `OrfScanner`); the private per-frame ORF loop of `GenomicAnalyzer` and the character loop of `Translator.FindOrfsInSequence` (B02, "(B09 for B02)") → one shared `Core/OrfScanner.FindRegions` (DUP_MAP §2 hard-coded stops, §3 ORF engines); reverse strand → canonical `DnaSequence.GetReverseComplementString`.

- GENOMIC-REPEAT-001: `GenomicAnalyzer.FindPalindromes` (verbatim copy of `RepeatFinder.FindPalindromesCore`, DUP_MAP §17) → delegates to `RepeatFinder.FindPalindromes` (F27); `FindLongestRepeat` now uses the canonical `SuffixTree.FindAllLongestRepeatedSubstrings` (F29) instead of the tree's single-representative bookkeeping; `FindRepeats` / `FindMaximalRepeats` share one traversal collector. `FindRepeats` does **not** call `RepeatFinder.FindDirectRepeats` / `SuffixTree.FindMaximalRepeatedPairs`: their result set is maximal pairs, different from "all repeated substrings" (documented, F28).

- GENOMIC-SIMILARITY-001: private `GetKmers` + intersection/union loop of `GenomicAnalyzer.CalculateSimilarity` -> `KmerAnalyzer.JaccardSimilarity * 100` (F32, B06 request DUP_MAP §16).

- GENOMIC-TANDEM-001: `GenomicAnalyzer.FindTandemRepeatsCore` (a stand-alone exact tandem scan, DUP_MAP §17 "4 engines") → facade over `RepeatFinder.FindMicrosatellites` (F35). The remaining exact tandem engine outside B04 is `GenomeAnnotator`'s private scan (B11, minimum span + unit lengths up to 60; `FindMicrosatellites(…, maxUnit: 60)` + a span filter would replace it — request registered for B11 below); `GenomeAssemblyAnalyzer.FindTandemRepeats` (B10, 80 % purity) is legitimately different. The new `Analysis/MaximalRepetitions.cs` is the only runs engine in the repository (it reuses `SequenceComplexity.BuildSuffixArray` / `BuildLcpArray`, no new suffix-array code).

- ALIGN-GLOBAL/LOCAL/SEMI (A1-2, F41): the substitution-matrix aligners add no dynamic program: `PairScoring` feeds the existing linear/local/affine cores and traceback (scalar path = scale 1), so tie order, coordinates and empty-input contracts are identical by construction. ALIGN-STATS (A1-9, F43): the `infoalign` consensus reference calls `MotifFinder.GenerateEmbossConsensus` (B05) instead of a second `cons`.

- ALIGN-MULTI-001 (A1-12, F53): the private UPGMA (`BuildProgressiveGuideTree`, a copy of `PhylogeneticAnalyzer.BuildUPGMA`) is deleted — the guide tree is built by the canonical `PhylogeneticAnalyzer.BuildTreeFromMatrix` (UPGMA and NJ) through the additive `TreeBuildOptions`; the unused `Phylogenetics -> Alignment` project reference that "justified" the copy is removed. (A1-16, F54): `MultipleAlignClassic` (a second star-alignment path used by one explicit benchmark) removed from production code.

- ALIGN-LOCAL-001 / ALIGN-GLOBAL-001 (A2-28c, F124): the matrix / residue-code table that `NeedleCore` and `WaterCore` each built is one `EmbossScoreTable` (also used by supermatcher, needleall, `SimilaritySubHeader`). Duplication that stays: stretcher's row-wise score table (per-residue rows for its Myers-Miller scans); `Ksw2Aligner` next to `GlobalAlignDualAffine` (the SIMD recurrence is the program's, not the mathematical DP); the Biopython / EMBOSS / ClustalW writers of the same format names (F126: different bytes).

- ALIGN-MULTI-001 (A2-23, F127): the ProbCons pair-HMM (forward / backward / log-sum / EXP / parameter tables) is T-Coffee's `proba_pair` engine, shared (`TcProbaModel` second constructor, `TcProbaBackward` `endMatch`); the Defaults.h tables were verified equal to `TcProbaTables` (no second copy). Duplication that stays: `PcSparse` / the sparse consistency transformation next to `TCoffeeLibrary`'s relaxation (different data structure, normalisation and float order), the three-way maximum-expected-accuracy DP next to the other global DPs (the program's tie order).

- ALIGN-MULTI-001 (A2-26, F128): the POA graph DP is the program's own affine model with an explicit gap-length state (truncation / decay arrays, special initial-gap state); it is not a variant of `GlobalAlignAffine` and shares no code. `PoaScoreMatrix` is a third matrix-file reader (format differs from `SubstitutionMatrix` / `TcMatrix`).

- EMBOSS reader (audit A4-3, F153): the `ajSeqIsNuc` rule was written five times (`DotMatcher.IsNucleotide`, `MotifFinder.IsEmbossNucleotideSequence` + `EmbossNucGapChars`, `SequenceAligner.IsNucleotideText`, `PairWordMatcher`'s `IsNucleotideWordSequence`, `EmbossAlignmentWriter.IsNuc`) with three different alphabets (the megamerger / seqmatchall copy lacked X and the gap characters); all five now call `EmbossSequenceReader.IsNucleotide` (Infrastructure; the megamerger 600 / 600 and seqmatchall 330 / 330 oracles stay equal), and the cleaning of the input sequences exists once (`EmbossSequenceReader.Clean` / `CleanGapped`) instead of in none of the 20 entry points.

- **WP44 (F184):** the run-date layout `%a %e %b %Y %H:%M:%S` (private in `EmbossAlignmentWriter`) is now `EmbossDates.Report`, shared by the alignment and the report writers; the feature-report layer has ONE writer (`EmbossReportWriter`, Alignment assembly) instead of the two-format `Infrastructure.EmbossReportWriter`; `EmbossReportPrograms` calls the canonical `GenomicAnalyzer` searches, `EmbossInputSequence`, `EmbossSequenceQualifiers` (extended: `ParseInputsAndReport`), `CFormat`, `EmbossSequenceReader`; the reverse complement of the report writers is `EmbossInputSequence.ReverseComplement`.

### F206 - `gaps`, `delta2blocks`, `mummer-annotate`, `run-mummer1` (audit A3-9e, WP49)
- **Sources.** `gaps.cc`, `delta2blocks.cc` (`addition_from_mugsy.patch`), `annotate.cc`, the installed `run-mummer1` script.

Reproduced defects of the programs: `gaps` loops forever on text and segfaults on an empty list, `delta2blocks` dereferences a null array on a PROMER delta file, `run-mummer1` without its `-r` fails (empty argument to `mummer`).

- **Oracle.** `repeatmatch_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_repeatmatch_oracle.py`): `repeat-match` **370 / 370** (+ 24 stops of the program, 1 illegal option), `exact-tandems` installed **215 / 215**, intended pipeline **215 / 215**; 3 300 more random runs of `repeat-match` and 1 200 of each script variant equal; valgrind clean on 110 random runs. **Genuine non-determinism, proven:** an empty file or a file without a `>` line never writes the sequence buffer (valgrind: use of uninitialised values; under `MALLOC_PERTURB_=165` the program reports a genome of 9 999 bases) - refused; a header word of 500+ characters overflows the 500 byte name buffer (`*** buffer overflow detected ***`, abort) - refused. **Tests.** `MummerRepeatMatch_Oracle_Tests` (3), MCP `RepeatMatch_...`, `ExactTandems_...`. **Commit.** e3b816f7d

### F212 - `mapview` (audit A3-9e4, WP50): FIG maps of show-coords output with genes
- **Finding.** The perl script `mapview` (coords / mgaps input, UTR / CDS GFF genes, `-n` partition, `fig2dev` conversion) was not ported.
- **Sources actually opened.** The installed `mapview` (= `scripts/mapview.pl`, 967 lines) and `Foundation.pm` (`TIGR_GetOptions`) of the Debian source package; perl 5.38.2 behaviours checked by running it.

### F214 - Mash (audit A5-10b2, WP51): the alphabet options `-a`, `-z`, `-Z` and `screen` of amino-acid queries
- **Finding.** `mash sketch` / `dist` / `triangle` / `screen` knew the nucleotide alphabet only (`-a` amino acids, `-z TEXT`, `-Z` case kept were not ported; `screen` of a protein sketch translates the mixture in six frames).
- **Sources actually opened (raw.githubusercontent.com, `Seqeron-review/1.0`).** marbl/Mash v2.3 `Sketch.cpp` (`setAlphabetFromString`, `addMinHashes`, `initFromFiles`, `initParametersFromCapnp`, `reverseComplement` + its `complement` table, `getMinKmerSize`), `Sketch.h` (`Parameters`: the alphabet table sits right after `parallelism` / `kmerSize`), `sketchParameterSetup.cpp`, `CommandScreen.cpp` (`run`: the round-robin reader and the 2^20-character chunks, `hashSequence`, `translate`, `aaFromCodon`), `CommandDistance.cpp` (`compareSketches`, `pValue` with `kmerSpace`); the installed mash 2.3 (measured: `-z` with a byte of 0xFC sets `kmerSize` to 1, a `-z abc -Z` sketch screens nothing, two empty mixture files are no error).
- **Fix.** `MashAlphabet` (alphabet characters, case rule, `alphabetSize^k` k-mer space and `use64`, `-a` / `-z` imply `-n`, the 256 bytes of the installed build around `complement` for the out-of-range reads of `reverseComplement`), `KmerAnalyzer.CreateMinHashSketch(records, alphabet, ...)` / `CreateReadsMinHashSketch(..., alphabet)` / `MashPValue(..., kmerSpace)`, `MinHashSketch.AlphabetSize`, `MashScreenScan` (chunking, six-frame translation, the table of the mixture built before the case flag is set), `MashCommands.Dist` / `Triangle` / `Sketch` / `Screen` `alphabet`, the alphabet and case flag inherited from a `.msh`; MCP `protein`, `alphabet`, `preserveCase` and a nullable `k` (21, or 9 with `protein`).
- **Oracle.** `mash_alphabet_{sketch,dist,screen}_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_mash_alphabet_oracle.py`, seed 20261221): 300 sketch files (`-a`, `-z` with 15 alphabets, `-Z`, `-n`, genomes, `-i`, read sets with `-r -m -c -g -b`, k 1 - 32; `.msh` byte-equal and `mash info`), 300 `dist` / `triangle` texts, 300 `screen` runs (protein queries against nucleotide reads of 1 - 3 files incl. six mixtures over 2^20 characters and an empty file, `-w -i -v`): **900 / 900 equal**.
- **Not defined by the program (refused, proof).** `-z` with a non-ASCII character: the alphabet table is indexed with a signed `char`, a byte of 0xFC writes into the `kmerSize` field before it (measured: k becomes 1), a byte below 0xF8 writes outside the object; a non-ASCII byte in a SEQUENCE is read the same way (the port treats it as outside every alphabet).
- **Tests.** `MashAlphabet_Oracle_Tests` (3), MCP `MashSketch_Dist_AminoAcidAlphabet_AsTheProgram`. **Commit.** 8c4746f2b

### F216 - EMBOSS diffseq (audit A5-8c3b, WP51): the sequence qualifiers of both inputs
- **Finding.** `diffseq` refused `-sbegin1 ... -sreverse2` (and the other qualifiers of the inputs).
- **Sources actually opened.** EMBOSS `emboss/diffseq.c` (`ajSeqTrim` before the table is made; the report header reads `ajSeqGetBegin` / `ajSeqGetEnd`), `ajax/core/ajseq.c` (`ajSeqTrim`, `ajSeqGetBegin`, `ajSeqGetEnd`, `ajSeqGetBeginTrue`, `ajSeqGetEndTrue`, `ajSeqReverseDo`, `seqMakeUsa`), the installed diffseq 6.6.0.
- **Fix.** `EmbossDiffseqPrograms.Run` reads each input through `EmbossInputSequence` (the one reader of the qualifiers), works on the cut (and reversed) sequence, passes the trim offset to the report (the header shows the ORIGINAL range of the first sequence and 1 - length of the second), and writes the USA of a trimmed sequence as `seqMakeUsa` does after the trim (the range is gone, only `[::r]` of a reversed sequence stays); `EmbossDiffseqOutput.Result` (additive) carries the differences; MCP `diffseq` takes the qualifiers in `reportFormat` and returns the differences of the cut sequences.
- **Oracle.** `diffseq_qualifiers_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_diffseq_qualifiers_oracle.py`, seed 20261222): **260 / 260** runs equal (the report in 12 formats, `-rusashow`, `-raccshow`, both GFF3 files, the refusals; negative and out-of-range begin / end, `-sreverse1/2`, `-slower` / `-supper`, `-snucleotide` / `-sprotein`, `-sformat fasta`).
- **Tests.** `EmbossDiffseq_Oracle_Tests.Diffseq_SequenceQualifiers_EqualTheProgram_AllRows`, MCP `Diffseq_SequenceQualifiers_AsTheProgram`. **Commit.** 6fa655187 (with F217)

### F217 - EMBOSS fuzznuc / fuzzpro / fuzztran (audit A5-8c3b, WP51): patterns whose elements are all optional ranges (the empty hits)
- **Defect.** A pattern such as `C(0,2)C(0,1)`, `X(0,2)[AC](0,1)` has the empty match: the programs list a hit of length 0 (`end = start - 1`, score 0) at every start of the sequence (not at the end), the recursive matcher (`patOUBrute`, mismatches or an `N` / `X` in a range) and the regular-expression search (`embPatMatchFindAll`) alike; the port dropped them (240 of 300 oracle rows). Found on the binary: a pattern anchored at the end (`>`) matches the empty string AT the end (`start = length + 1`) when no match began at the last residue (the search loop stops when the position is the end); the `Translation` column of an empty fuzztran hit is the `ajStrAssignSubS` clipping of its positions (`pstart = 1, pend = 0` is the whole translation, otherwise the residue at `pstart`).
- **Sources actually opened.** EMBOSS `nucleus/embpat.c` (`embPatGetTypeII`, `embPatFuzzSearchAllII`, `embPatBruteForce`, `patOUBrute`, `patBrute*`, `embPatMatchFindAll`, `embPatPushHit`), the installed fuzznuc / fuzzpro / fuzztran 6.6.0.
- **Fix.** `FuzznucPattern.ExpandPaths(includeEmpty)` / `ProteinPattern.ExpandPaths(includeEmpty)`, `PatternHitsLiteral` (the empty unrolling at every start; the empty match at the end of an end-anchored regular-expression search), `ProteinPatternHitsCore` / `ProteinPatternHitsApproximate`, `FindTranslatedPatternHits` (`EmbossText.SubstringFromEnd`).
- **Oracle.** `fuzznuc_optional_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_fuzznuc_optional_oracle.py`, seed 20261223): **400 / 400** whole excel reports equal (200 fuzznuc, 100 fuzzpro, 100 fuzztran; `-pmismatch` 0 - 2, anchors `<` `>`, both strands, all frames); the earlier oracles (fuzznuc 3 300, 300 range / mismatch rows, fuzzpro 900 + 1 000, fuzztran 760) stay equal.
- **Tests.** `EmbossFuzznucRangeMismatch_Oracle_Tests.AllOptionalRangePatterns_ListTheEmptyHits_EqualsTheProgram`. **Commit.** 6fa655187

### F218 - EMBOSS diffseq (audit A5-8c3b, WP51): GenBank / EMBL inputs with feature tables
- **Finding.** `diffseq` read FASTA only: the features of GenBank / EMBL entries (the `first_feature` / `second_feature` notes: the features of each sequence that overlap a difference) were not ported, nor the entry readers, the location and qualifier parsers, and the feature table that follows the sequence under `-sbegin` / `-send` / `-sreverse`.
- **Sources actually opened (raw.githubusercontent.com, `Seqeron-review/1.0`).** EMBOSS `ajax/core/ajfeatread.c` (`featReadEmbl`, `featEmblFromLine`, `featEmblProcess`, `featEmblOperOut` / `OperIn` / `OperNone`, `featEmblLoc`, `featEmblLocNum` / `LocRange`, `featEmblTvTagVal` / `TvRest`), `ajax/core/ajfeat.c` (`ajFeatNewNucFlags`, `ajFeatNewNucFlagsSub`, `ajFeatTagAddSS`, `featTagSetDefault`, the special validators `featTagSpecialAll*`, `ajFeattableTrimOff`, `ajFeatTrimOffRange`, `ajFeattableReverse`, `ajFeatReverse`, `ajFeatGetStart` / `ajFeatGetEnd`, `featVocabRead*`, `featTableTypeInternal`), `ajax/core/ajseqread.c` (`seqReadGenbank`, `seqReadEmbl`, `seqPrefixGenbank`, `seqPrefixGenbankMore`, `seqSetName`, `seqAccSave`), `ajax/core/ajseq.c` (`ajSeqTrim`, `ajSeqSetRange`, `ajSeqReverseDo`), `ajax/core/ajstr.c` (`ajStrQuoteStrip`, `ajStrRemoveWhiteExcess`, `ajStrHasParentheses`), `emboss/diffseq.c` (`diffseq_Features`, `diffseq_AddTags`); the data files `Efeatures.*` / `Etags.*` of the installed 6.6.0 and the installed diffseq (measured: the type names).
- **Fix.** `EmbossSeqFeatureTable` (Infrastructure, internal) = the readers above (a join / order location is ONE feature from its lowest start to its highest end, its exons are sub-features; `complement()` of the whole is a strand, `complement(join())` swaps start and end; `<` `>` `(a.b)` `a^b` remote ids; a qualifier is the canonical tag of the vocabulary, an unknown one a `note` `*name: value`, a value of a special tag that fails its check a `note` too; `ajFeattableTrimOff` deletes a feature one of whose exons lies outside the range), `EmbossFeatureVocabulary` (`generate_emboss_feature_vocab.py`: the tags parsed from the data files, the 449 type names MEASURED on the installed diffseq), `EmbossEntryReader` (GenBank with the control flow of `seqReadGenbank`, EMBL, the format of the text), `EmbossSequenceQualifiers.Format` (`-sformat`), `EmbossDiffseqPrograms.Run` (feature notes before the program's own notes, `ajuint` comparison, the USA `genbank::file:name`), MCP `diffseq` takes the text of a GenBank / EMBL file.
- **Quirks of the program reproduced (measured).** (1) In a GenBank entry the line after the SOURCE block (`SOURCE` + `ORGANISM` + lineage lines, all `GB_MORE`) is SKIPPED: `seqPrefixGenbankMore` compares from the second character, so the ORGANISM branch never runs and the loop reads one line too many; an entry whose SOURCE block is followed directly by `FEATURES` has no features. (2) `ajStrHasParentheses` means BALANCED, so `join(1..5,7..9)` is unwrapped. (3) `ajFeattableTrimOff` deletes a feature when any exon is outside the kept range. (4) `diffseq_Features` compares positions as `ajuint` (the first difference of `-globaldifferences` with no match starts at -1).
- **Oracle.** `diffseq_features_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_diffseq_features_oracle.py`, seed 20261224): **420 / 420** runs equal (GenBank and EMBL entries with up to 8 random features each - 25 types incl. aliases, unknown keys and other case; locations simple, complement, join, order, complement(join), single, `a^b`, `<` `>`, `(a.b)`, remote entries, beyond the sequence; qualifiers quoted over several lines, unquoted, void, doubled quotes, db_xref, protein_id, translation, codon_start, unknown / other-case names; mixed with FASTA, `-sformat1`, `-sbegin` / `-send` / `-sreverse` on both inputs, 12 report formats, `-raccshow -rdesshow -rusashow`); two more seeds of 600 and 800 rows equal during development.
- **Not done here:** the qualifiers with a special validator other than `db_xref`, `protein_id`, `translation`, `codon`, `estimated_length` (refused with `NotSupportedException` at this commit: done in F219), the feature output formats (F220); the rest is registered at F220 (A5-8c3d).
- **Tests.** `EmbossDiffseq_Oracle_Tests.Diffseq_FeatureTableInputs_EqualTheProgram_AllRows`, MCP `Diffseq_GenbankAndEmblFeatures_AsTheProgram`. **Commit.** 5b7cd8d8a

### F220 - EMBOSS diffseq (audit A5-8c3c, WP51): the feature output formats `-offormat4` / `-offormat5` of both feature files
- **Finding.** `-aoutfeat` / `-boutfeat` were always written as GFF3 and `-offormat4` / `-offormat5` (and `-ofopenfile`, `-ofname`, `-ofextension`, `-ofdirectory`, `-ofsingle`) were refused. The program writes the conflict features of each sequence in any of the output feature formats of `ajfeatwrite.c` (`featOutFormatDef`: gff, gff2, gff3, bed, embl, em, genbank, gb, ddbj, refseq, refseqp, pir, nbrf, swiss, sw, swissprot, uniprot, dasgff, draw, debug, unknown).
- **Sources actually opened.** EMBOSS `ajax/core/ajfeatwrite.c` (`ajFeattableWrite`, `ajFeattableWriteGff2` / `Bed` / `Draw` / `Debug`, `featWriteEmbl` / `featDumpEmbl`, `featWriteRefseqp` / `featDumpRefseqp`, `featDumpPir`, `featDumpSwiss`, `featDumpGff2`, `featDumpBed`, `ajFeattablePrint`, the Dasgff writer, `featTagQuoteEmbl` / `featTagQuoteGff2`, `featTagEmblDefault`, `featTagGff2Default`, `ajFeattabOutOpen`, `featoutUfoProcess`, `featFindOutFormatC`), `ajax/core/ajfeat.c` (`ajFeattableGetScorerange` / `ajFeatGetScorerange`: the scores are never used, `curmax` is assigned 0), `ajax/core/ajacd.c` (`acdSetFeatout`), the installed diffseq.
- **Fix.** `EmbossReportWriter.WriteFeatureTable` (Alignment, new file `EmbossReportWriter.FeatureOut.cs`: the format table `featOutFormatDef` with its nucleotide / protein validity, the new writers gff2, bed, draw, debug (`ajFeattablePrint`), refseqp; the embl / genbank / pir / swiss / dasgff writers of the report layer reused, embl and genbank with the QSPECIAL tag `replace` and its default note `/note="replace: ..."`), `EmbossSequenceQualifiers.ParseInputsAndReport(program, text, featureOutputs)` + `EmbossFeatureOutQualifiers` (`-offormat`, `-ofopenfile` of each output), `EmbossDiffseqPrograms` (`OpenFeatureOutput` = `acdSetFeatout` + `ajFeattabOutOpen` + `featoutUfoProcess`: `format::name` prefix, `-ofopenfile` without `-offormat` leaves the format "unknown" and writes nothing, a name that is no format is written as gff3; `EmbossDiffseqOutput.FeatureFileName1` / `FeatureFileName2`; the header of the report names the file written), MCP `diffseq` (`reportFormat` carries the qualifiers, `DiffseqToolResult.FeatureFileName1` / `FeatureFileName2`). **Facts measured and reproduced:** (1) the writers share the static string `featoutStr` of `ajfeatwrite.c`: embl / genbank / refseqp leave the text of their last tag in it, dasgff the text of its last `<NOTE>`, swiss / pir / gff2 clear it, and gff2 and pir PRINT what is in it in front of their first tag (`/replace="t"note "gb_a"` in a GFF2 file written after an EMBL file); (2) the report is written AFTER the feature files, so a PIR report prints the text the last feature writer left in front of its first note (`EmbossReportOptions.FeatureLeftover`); (3) a format that is invalid for the sequence kind (embl for a protein pair, pir for nucleotides, `unknown`) leaves an EMPTY file and only a message; (4) `ajuint` start / end are printed with `%d` by bed and draw (`-2`, `-1`); (5) dasgff's feature file has no closing `</GFF></DASGFF>` (only the report writes it); (6) `-ofname`, `-ofextension`, `-ofsingle`, `-ofdirectory` do not change what is written (the file name is the value of `-aoutfeat`, default `name.diffgff`).
- **Oracle.** `diffseq_featout_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_diffseq_featout_oracle.py`, seed 20261226): **500 / 500** runs equal (333 nucleotide and 167 protein pairs, 24 format names incl. other case, `fasta` / `bogus` / `gff4`, the `format::file` prefix, `-ofopenfile`, `-ofname` / `-ofextension` / `-ofsingle`, 33 % with sequence qualifiers, 25 % with a report format: table, gff, embl, genbank, dasgff, pir, swiss, simple, tagseq, debug; names with quotes, long names, bases the `replace` validator refuses): report and every written file byte for byte; 2 700 more rows over five development seeds equal.
- **Tests.** `EmbossDiffseq_Oracle_Tests.Diffseq_FeatureOutputFormats_EqualTheProgram_AllRows`, MCP `Diffseq_FeatureOutputFormats_AsTheProgram`.
- **Not done (registered, precise): A5-8c3d.** (a) features READ from a separate file (`-ufo`, `-fformat`, `-fopenfile`: a residue string has no file; they stay accepted without effect) and the other feature input formats (gff2 / gff3, swissprot, pir, refseq) and sequence formats with features (swiss, gff, genpept): the readers `featRead*` of `ajfeatread.c`; (b) the feature output formats of `wordmatch` (`-aoutfeat` / `-boutfeat` of its set tables: several tables per file, the same writers). **Commit.** 12f581064 (F219 + F220 together)

### F221 - test defect (WP51): `B05AuditFuzzTests.DecipherAndEmbossAuto_RandomInput_OnlyDocumentedExceptions` expected the raw row length
- **Defect.** The test (Fuzzing tier, not in the targeted tier) compared the length of the `GenerateEmbossConsensus(rows, true, Auto)` result with the longest RAW row; since A4-3 (F153) the rows are read as EMBOSS reads an alignment row (digits, blanks, `_` and other characters are dropped before the padding), so the consensus is shorter whenever a random row holds such a character (expected 16, was 14; proof: the same failure at `08379e30e`, the tip before WP51, in a clean worktree; none of WP51's files is involved).
- **Fix.** The expected length is the longest row after `EmbossSequenceReader.CleanGapped`. **Commit.** aaf7c2dee

### F232 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A2-26c, WP53): SPOA 4.0.8 command line (`SpoaProgram`, `SpoaGraph`, `SpoaEngine`), MCP `spoa_command`
- **Finding.** SPOA (Vaser et al. 2017; installed Debian `spoa` 4.0.8-1) had no port. The installed binary runs the SIMD engine; a sequential engine (`SisdAlignmentEngine`) differs from it in 4 % of random runs (semi-global alignments, rows whose maximum lies in a padding lane), so the SISD source cannot serve as the reference.
- **Sources actually opened.** `spoa_4.0.8.orig` (`src/graph.cpp`, `src/sisd_alignment_engine.cpp`, `src/simd_alignment_engine_implementation.hpp` (`Linear`, `Affine`, `Convex`, `Initialize`, `_mmxxx_max_value`, `_mmxxx_index_of`), `src/alignment_engine.cpp`, `src/main.cpp`, `include/spoa/*.hpp`), bioparser `fasta_parser.hpp` / `fastq_parser.hpp` / `parser.hpp`, biosoup `sequence.hpp` (`ReverseAndComplement`), cloned from github.com into the scratchpad and built three ways (SISD, `-msse4.1`, `-mavx2`) for the reference runs.
- **Fix (additive).** `SpoaGraph` (nodes, edges with `uint32` labels and `int64` weights, aligned-node rings, the topological sort, heaviest bundle with branch completion, MSA rows, DOT, `AddAlignment` with unit / Phred weights), `SpoaEngine` (the SIMD engine emulated lane by lane: int16 / int32 variant by `WorstCaseAlignmentScore(len + 8, nodes)`, vectors of 16 / 8 lanes (AVX2, 128-bit = 8 / 4 gives the same result), padding lanes with `-max(|m|, |n|, |g|, |q|)`, wrapping lane arithmetic, the shifted prefix maxima, linear / affine / convex initialisation, `_mmxxx_max_value` starting at 0, `_mmxxx_index_of`, the traceback with `extend_left` / `extend_up` loops), `SpoaProgram` (glibc `getopt_long` loop with permutation / abbreviations / diagnostics, `atoi` into 8-bit integers, `-l -r -d -s --version --help`, bioparser's chunked FASTA / FASTQ state machines (64 kB buffer, names shortened at the first white space, invalid format = `std::invalid_argument` abort, empty input = `std::length_error` abort, status 134), gzip input, `ReverseAndComplement` twice when the forward strand wins). MCP `spoa_command` (586 tools; catalog, README, MCP_STATUS, traceability, tool-map, EXPECTED_COUNTS regenerated).

The 128-bit engine gives the same 441 results. Valgrind of the installed program on 36 runs: no error (so no non-determinism).

### F233 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A2-27d, WP53): EMBOSS alignment formats of three or more rows (`unknown`, `multiple`, `simple`, `srs`; `alignConsStats`)
- **Finding.** `EmbossAlignmentWriter` wrote `simple` / `srs` / `multiple` / `unknown` for pairs only; the installed `aligncopy` writes them for any number of rows, with the consensus of `alignConsStats` under the rows and its Identity / Similarity / Gaps counts, and REFUSES every pair-markup format (`pair`, `srspair`, `markx0..3`, `markx10`, `match`, `score`, `sam`) for three or more rows ("Alignment format pair specifies at most 2 sequences, alignment has 3").
- **Sources actually opened (raw.githubusercontent.com, `Seqeron-review/1.0`).** EMBOSS `ajax/core/ajalign.c` (`alignConsStats`, `alignSim`, `alignWriteSimple`, `alignWriteSrsAny`, `alignWriteHeaderNum`, the `nseq > 2` markup rule), `ajax/core/ajdefine.h` (`E_FPEQ`, `E_FPZERO`, `U_FEPS`), `ajax/core/ajseq.c` (`ajSeqcvtNewStr`: a case-insensitive table, code = label index + 1, 0 for every other character), the installed EMBOSS 6.6.0 `aligncopy`.
- **Fix (additive).** `EmbossAlignmentConsensus` (`Calculate`: float weights, `fplural = totweight * 51 / 100`, per-column identical / matching weights, the plurality rule, `#` when the best residue is the only one, upper / lower case = identical / similar, the matrix EDNAFULL or EBLOSUM62 chosen by the first row; `Markup` = `alignSim`), `EmbossMultiAlignment` + `EmbossAlignmentWriter.Write(EmbossMultiAlignment)` (the `Pair` data class generalised to n rows; `WriteHeader` / `WriteSimple` / `WriteSrs` loop over the rows; the markup under the rows for n > 2, no markup for `srs`; the default matrix name in the header), the program's refusal as `ArgumentException`. MCP `write_alignment` accepts three or more rows for these formats.
- **Oracle.** `emboss_multirow_oracle.tsv` (`generate_emboss_multirow_oracle.py`, seed 20261322): **1 200 / 1 200** runs of `aligncopy` equal - 800 outputs byte for byte (200 each of `unknown`, `multiple`, `simple`, `srs`; 3 - 8 rows of 10 - 130 columns, DNA and protein, lower-case residues, gaps, `-awidth`) and 400 refusals of the seven pair-markup formats (message equal). **Not done:** `tcoffee` of three or more rows (the library-style output of `alignWriteTCoffee`, registered).
- **Tests.** `EmbossMultiRowAlignment_Oracle_Tests` (2), MCP `EmbossFormatTests.WriteAlignment_ThreeRows_...`. **Commit.** 5fa273cab

### F234 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A2-27d, WP53): Biopython `Bio.Align` bigBed writer and reader (`AlignmentCoordinateFormats.WriteBigBed` / `ParseBigBed`)
- **Finding.** `AlignmentCoordinateFormats` had no `bigbed`: Biopython 1.88 `Bio/Align/bigbed.py` (2 241 lines) writes the UCSC binary format (header, autoSQL block, total summary, B+ tree of the chromosomes, zlib-compressed data blocks, R-tree, zoom levels with the red-black range tree `_RangeTree`, optional extra B+ tree indices) and reads it back (header + endianness, B+ tree, R-tree, zoom headers, blocks, extra indices, bedN / declaration fields).
- **Sources actually opened.** the installed Biopython 1.88 (`Bio/Align/bigbed.py`, `Bio/Align/__init__.py`), UCSC `bigBed` format description (genome.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/help/bigBed.html) as quoted in the module.
- **Fix (additive).** `AlignmentCoordinateFormats.BigBed.cs` (writer: `BbExtractFields` bedN 3 - 12 plus custom declarations / extra fields incl. arrays, reductions, `BbRangeTree`, summaries, `BbBuildRTree` / `BbWriteLeaves` / `BbWriteIndexLevel`, B+ tree with the chromosomes and the extra indices, all 42 Biopython `RuntimeError` offset-mismatch refusals reproduced) and `.BigBedRead.cs` (`ParseBigBed`); the compression is injectable (`BigBedWriteOptions.Compress`) because the bytes of `zlib.compress` depend on the zlib build: the oracle records every `zlib.compress(input) -> output` call of Biopython and the test feeds these back, so the WHOLE file is compared byte for byte.
- **Oracle.** `biopython_coord_oracle.tsv` (3 825 rows now), `oracle_sections_bigbed.py`: **216 writer rows** (bedN 3 - 12, compress on / off, itemsPerSlot 1 - 512, blockSize 2 - 256, 1 - 3 chromosomes, custom declarations with string / int / float / `int[count]` fields, extra indices, refusals) equal to the written bytes and **229 reader rows** (the written files, truncated files, garbage; structural equality of alignments, targets and declaration, error type for the refusals).
- **Tests.** `AlignmentCoordinateBigBed_Tests` (3). **Not done (registered):** bigmaf, bigpsl (`bigmaf.py` / `bigpsl.py` wrap this writer); the binary format is not yet exposed by the MCP tools (they carry text). **Commit.** 9bafac681

- **Finding.** No `bigmaf`: `Bio/Align/bigmaf.py` writes every alignment as a BED3 item of its reference row (`reference.chromosome` -> `chromosome`, the target of the item) whose `mafBlock` (`lstring`) is the MAF text of the alignment with `;` for the line ends, through the bigBed writer with the `bedMaf` declaration, and reads the blocks back with the MAF parser of the C extension `PrintedAlignmentParser`.

- **Oracle.** `oracle_sections_bigmaf.py`: **231 writer rows** (1 - 3 chromosomes, 1 - 15 alignments of 2 - 5 rows, scores, `pass`, empty regions, quality / `i` lines, compress on / off, byte-equal with the zlib calls of Biopython injected) and **963 reader rows** (the written files + 40 files x 19 damaged blocks written with the bigBed writer: wrong sizes, negative start, dots, missing fields, bad strands, stray `q` / `i` / `e` lines, bad statuses; truncated files, garbage) equal (577 are refusals with the same outcome).

### F239 - EMBOSS wordmatch (audit A5-8c3e (c), WP53): the sequence qualifiers of both inputs
- **Finding.** `wordmatch` refused `-sbegin1` ... with `NotSupportedException`.
- **Sources actually opened.** the installed wordmatch 6.6.0 (measured), EMBOSS `emboss/wordmatch.c` / `ajacd.c` (`acdSetSeqset` / `acdSetSeqall`) as already ported for needleall / supermatcher.
- **Facts established (measured on 6.6.0).** The first input is a seqset: every member is cut by `-sbegin1` / `-send1` (the positions of the report and of the feature file start at 1 in the cut sequence, `##sequence-region` has the cut length), reversed by `-sreverse1` through `ajSeqsetReverse` (decided once from the first member), and a forced type decides the unknown symbol whose words are left out (`N` for `-snucleotide1`, `X` for `-sprotein1`, whatever the letters say). The second input is a seqall read member by member: `-sbegin2` / `-send2` are IGNORED by the program (the whole sequence is scanned and `##sequence-region` has the full length), `-sreverse2` reverses it. A reversed sequence is reported on the reverse strand with the positions of the reversed sequence counted down (`28..24`) and the feature file keeps strand `+` with the same positions.
- **Fix.** `EmbossWordmatchPrograms.Run` reads both inputs through `EmbossSetInput.ReadAll` (set / stream) with the qualifiers of the `-sbegin1` ... text (`featureQualifiers`), the stream without its range, the reversed flag on the aligned rows, `GenomicAnalyzer.Wordmatch(..., nucleotide)` for the forced type; `EmbossWordmatchOutput.Result` (the tool returns the matches of the qualified run); MCP `wordmatch` description / `featureQualifiers` parameter.
- **Oracle.** `wordmatch_seqopts_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_wordmatch_seqopts_oracle.py`, seed 20261328): **330 / 330** runs equal - 308 outputs (alignments in 8 formats, the log, both feature files; ranges including negative and beyond the end, `-sreverse1/2`, `-slower` / `-supper`, `-sprotein` / `-snucleotide`, `-scircular`) and 22 refusals ("Sequence is not nucleic" / "not a protein").
- **Tests.** `EmbossWordmatch_Oracle_Tests.Wordmatch_SequenceQualifiers_EqualTheProgram_AllRows`, MCP `Wordmatch_SequenceQualifiers_AsTheProgram`. **Commit.** 6692bcafc

### F241 - EMBOSS feature library (audit A5-8c3e (a), WP54): the vocabularies and the readers of every input format (`featRead*` of `ajfeatread.c`)
- **Finding.** Only the GenBank / EMBL feature reader of F218 existed (and its vocabulary was MEASURED on the installed diffseq): features could not be read from gff2 / gff3 / swissprot / pir / refseq / genpept / refseqp / dasgff files or from a file separate from the sequence, the reader's file-buffer semantics (format finding, tables without features, end of file), static state and messages were not ported, and the model lacked source, score, group, remote id, label, GFF3 tags and the library's flag values.

- **Fix.** `EmbossFeatureVocab` (+ `EmbossFeatureVocabData.g.cs` from `generate_emboss_feature_vocab_data.py`): `featVocabReadTags` / `featVocabReadTypes` ported as they are, including the in-place edit of the value string of a `name = id` line (two keys share it) and the static token string of `ajStrParseWhite` that `storetype` points to, replaces the measured tables (`EmbossFeatureVocabulary*`, `generate_emboss_feature_vocab.py` removed). `EmbossSeqFeatureTable` (+ `.Formats`, `.Dasgff`, `.Output`): model with the library's fields and flag values (`AJFEATFLAG_*`), `NewNuc` / `NewProt` (`ajFeatNew*Flags[Sub]`: group counter also for sub-features), `TagAdd` (protein or DNA vocabulary), `GfftagAdd`, `NewFeat` (copies re-add every tag), the readers refseq, genpept, refseqp (`featRefseqpFromLine`), pir, swiss (`featSwissFromLine`: the static feature the last call returned), gff2, gff3 (ID table, parents), gff3emboss, dasgff; `EmbossFeatureLines` = `AjPFilebuff`; `EmbossFeatureStream` = `feattabinRead` (blank lines, format loop over the `Try` formats, unbuffered explicit format, the retry after end of file); `EmbossFeatureInput` = the ACD `features` input (`format::`, `[range]`, `-fbegin` / `-fend`, two attempts, the died message); `CStr` = the `strto*` conversions (a string that is not entirely a number is 0 / false). Quirks of the program reproduced (all measured): the empty line of a feature table is a new feature with an empty key; `ajStrAssignSubS` returns at least one character (a location starting with a comma never ends: refused with an exception, as are GFF2 / GFF3old group fields the tag pattern cannot parse and a reader that returns tables at the end of the file); `featRegMore` is compiled by whichever of the two flag readers runs first; `ajFeatGetId` looks for `Id`, never `ID`; `LocNum` leaves the number it read before failing (`108..121binding` ends at 121); positions are unsigned (`-fbegin -47`).
- **Oracle.** `featread_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`generate_featread_oracle.py`, seed 20261501): **2 600 / 2 600** `featcopy -features FILE -offormat debug` runs equal (stdout file and stderr; embl 237, genbank 237, refseq 237, genpept 237, refseqp 236, gff2 236, gff3 236, gff3emboss 236, swiss 236, pir 236, dasgff 236; no format / `format::` prefix / `-fbegin1` `-fend1` / damaged and mixed files; 56 files on which the program never stops); a further 1 500 of seed 777 equal; `emboss_feature_vocab_oracle.tsv.gz` (`emboss_feature_vocab_dump.c` over libajax): **2 406 / 2 406** table entries of the ten vocabularies.
- **Tests.** `EmbossFeatureVocab_Oracle_Tests`, `EmbossFeatureReaders_Oracle_Tests.FeatureReaders_EqualFeatcopyDebug_AllRows`. **Commits.** c1a33581c (vocabularies), e51bcaf9e (readers).

The installed `seqret -debug` trace was read to follow the try-each-format loop.
- **Fix.** `EmbossSeqin` (Infrastructure) is `seqRead` / `seqReadFmt` over the library's line buffer (`EmbossFeatureLines`: the lines carry their line feed, a last line without one gets it), with the readers of fasta (ncbi, pearson, gifasta, dbid), gcg (gcg8), embl (em; the sequence of a CO contig line is refused), swiss (sw, swissprot, uniprot; the `DE` description of `RecName` / `AltName` / `SubName` / `Includes` / `Contains` / `Flags` assembled as the library does, the `Contains` block of the library that prints the CD-antigen names twice instead of the short and EC names kept), nbrf (pir), genbank (gb, ddbj, refseq), refseqp, genpept, codata, strider, ig, igstrict, iguspto, staden, textonly (plain, asis, unknown), fastq (sanger, illumina, solexa), sam, gff2, gff3 (gff), gde, raw and the alignment readers that share `seqin->SeqData` (clustal / aln, msf, fitch, mase, biomart, treecon, acedb: the first call reads the alignment, every call returns the next member); the ACD type check of the input (`gapany` for seqret, `any` for most programs: `ajSeqTypeCheckIn`, `seqTypeFix`), `ajSeqSetNuc` (x / X become n / N), the unnamed sequences `EMBOSS_001`, the `asis::` text, `format::` prefix and `-sformat`, the messages of the library (bad characters, zero-length sequences, unknown formats, end of file, Iguspto first line, FASTQ quality) and the feature tables of embl / genbank / refseqp / swiss / nbrf / gff2 / gff3 through the feature readers of F241 (`EmbossSeqFeatureTable`). `EmbossSeqall` is the `seqall` input of the ACD, `EmbossSeqretPrograms.Seqret` the program (FASTA output, feature output in every writer of F244). The other alignment, protein-databank and binary formats (phylip, phylipnon, nexus, mega, selex, stockholm, hennig86, jackknifer, ace, experiment, pdb, abi, bam, nibble, scf, das, ensembl) are recognised by the first line / magic and refused (A5-8c3h).
- **Facts measured on 6.6.0** (all in the tests): the static `seqToken` of the library leaks from one reader to the next (the sam reader leaves its first token, the strider reader accepts it as a name: a file that starts with `@` and is no SAM is read as strider); `thys->Format` is set only from the NAMED format, so a sequence found by the try loop is typed by its letters (x / X become N only for nucleotide); a read that hits the end of a file clears the static line (iguspto); the first line of genbank / genpept is read with `ajBuffreadLine` (not counted in the records, so one blank line after an entry is silent and two print "end-of-file before end of data"); an unterminated last line gets its line feed; after all formats fail the text reader is not used but the file is "unknown" (the `strider` / text fallbacks above); `ajFeattableNewSeq` of an EMBL entry before its residues are read has the type P (the GFF header says Protein for a nucleotide entry with no feature); a PIR table read after `ajSeqSetProt` keeps the empty type (the GFF header says DNA); gff2 sequence files go through the GFF3 feature reader; a GFF3 file read with its features that holds none makes the program dereference a null table (valgrind: Invalid read of size 4 in `ajFeattableIsCircular`, a fault, refused with `InvalidOperationException`).
- **Oracle.** `seqret_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`scripts/alignment/generate_seqret_oracle.py`, seed 20265603): **9 800 / 9 800** `seqret -auto [-feature] -sequence in.dat [-sformat1 F] -outseq o.fa -osformat2 fasta -offormat2 gff3 -ofname2 o.gff` runs equal (200 inputs of each of 49 format names; the inputs are `seqret -osformat` writer outputs and feature entries converted with `seqret -feature`, 30 % damaged; `-sformat1`, `F::in.dat`, an upper-case name, no format, `-firstonly`, `-slower` / `-supper` / `-snucleotide` / `-sprotein`, with and without `-feature`; 151 runs are the fault above and are refused). Test `SequenceReaders_EqualSeqret_AllRows`, MCP `Seqret_ReadsTheSequenceFormats_AsTheProgram`. **Commits.** 53afc7e08 (readers + seqret), 8115f0fe7 (MCP `seqret`, ACD profiles of seqret and the feature programs), 242491c00 (the alignment readers, oracle of 9 800 runs), c391d8379 (docs of the alignment readers), c0589a474 (entries, WP56 section, Evidence, report, algorithm doc)

### F251 - EMBOSS sequence input (audit A5-8c3h (2b), WP57): the readers of phylip, phylipnon, nexus / paup, mega, selex, stockholm / pfam, jackknifer, hennig86, experiment, ace / consed, pdb, pdbseq, pdbnuc, pdbnucseq
- **Sources actually opened.** `ajseqread.c` (`seqReadPhylip`, `seqReadPhylipnon`, `seqPhylipReadseq`, `seqReadHennig86`, `seqReadJackknifer`, `seqReadNexus`, `seqReadMega`, `seqReadSelex`, `seqSelex*`, `seqReadStockholm`, `seqReadExperiment`, `seqReadAce`, `seqReadPdb`, `seqReadPdbseq`, `seqReadPdbnuc`, `seqReadPdbnucseq`, `seqitemSetName`, `seqnameSetName`, `seqAppend`, `seqDefine`), `ajnexus.c` (raw.githubusercontent.com `kimrutherford/EMBOSS/master/ajax/core/ajnexus.c`: `ajNexusParse`, `nexusBlockSave`, `nexusCommand`, `nexusParse*`, `nexusGet*`, `nexusSetSequences`), `ajlist.c` (`ajListstrToarrayAppend`), `ajtable.c` (`ajTablePut`), `ajstr.c` (`ajStrAssignSubS`, `ajStrCutRange`, `ajStrQuoteStripAll`, `ajStrSetResRound`, `ajStrToUint`), `ajbase.c` (`ajResidueFromTriplet`, `ajBaseFromDoublet`), `ajcvt.c` (`ajCvtSposToPosStart`); the installed 6.6.0 under valgrind.
- **Fix.** The `ReadUnported` stub of `EmbossSeqin.Text.cs` is replaced reader by reader on the `seqin->SeqData` machinery of F248: phylip (interleaved; the fall-backs to phylipnon on a repeated name, different lengths in the first block or an incomplete last block) and phylipnon (`EmbossSeqin.Phylip.cs`), jackknifer and hennig86 (`EmbossSeqin.Tree.cs`), nexus / paup with the parser of `ajnexus.c` (`EmbossSeqin.Nexus.cs`: the comment levels, the shared command queue, the block parsers, `nexusSetSequences`, the messages `Unknown taxon` / `Nexus sequence length`), mega (`EmbossSeqin.Mega.cs`: header, [comments], identical / indel characters, gene / domain blocks), selex and stockholm / pfam (`EmbossSeqin.Selex.cs`; the buffer is rewound to the first line as `ajFileSeek` does), experiment and ace (`EmbossSeqin.Staden.cs`), pdb / pdbnuc (ATOM residues) and pdbseq / pdbnucseq (SEQRES) (`EmbossSeqin.Pdb.cs`). The residue checks of the readers look at the text up to a NUL character (the C string of the library). The oracle generator closes the title quote that the 6.6.0 jackknifer writer leaves open, builds rich hand-made NEXUS, experiment and PDB files, and runs the formats whose readers have memory faults under valgrind (`memerr` rows).
- **Reference faults (BLOCKED class, proof by valgrind / repeated runs; the port refuses such inputs with `InvalidOperationException`, the test accepts the refusal).** (a) `seqReadAce`: `acedata->Names` is a null pointer after the `AS` line - the process dies by a segmentation fault on EVERY ACE file (all 400 ace / consed oracle inputs that start with `AS`). (b) `seqReadHennig86`: `for(cp = ...; cp; cp++)` never ends (a pointer is never NULL) and the line after the name is not read again - the loop writes over the heap until the process dies or the limit stops it (185 of 200 inputs). (c) `nexusSetSequences`: `ajTablePut` of a taxon label that is in the table deletes the old key, which is the string of the label list, and the library then reads and deletes it again (valgrind: Invalid read of size 8 in `ajStrGetPtr` via `ajTablestrHash`, Invalid read / write of size 4 in `ajStrDel`; the output depends on how the heap is reused, six repeated runs of one input print the same messages, other inputs print a different label or no message). (d) `ajListstrToarrayAppend` counts `array[j]` instead of `(*array)[j]`: a second `taxlabels` / `matrix` command reads the memory behind the structure. (e) `seqReadSelex` / `seqReadStockholm`: more lines in a block than sequences, `#=SS` before the first sequence, no sequence count - writes past a heap array (valgrind Invalid write; 33 of 200 selex inputs, 1 of 400 stockholm / pfam). (f) `seqReadMega`: an identical character in a sequence that is longer than the first one reads the zero-filled memory behind the first sequence (the string grows by `ajStrSetResRound`, which zero fills) and, past it, other heap memory: the zero reads are reproduced, the runs valgrind reports as invalid are refused (98 of 200 mega inputs).
- **Oracle.** `seqret_oracle_<format>.jsonl.gz` (`scripts/alignment/generate_seqret_oracle.py`, seeds 20265701 - 20265710): **3 400 / 3 400** runs equal (phylip + phylipnon 400, jackknifer + hennig86 400, nexus + paup 400, mega 200, selex + stockholm + pfam 600, experiment + ace + consed 600, pdb + pdbseq + pdbnuc + pdbnucseq 800; 200 inputs of each of the 17 names, 30 % damaged, `-sformat1 F`, `F::in.dat`, no format, `-firstonly`, the case / type options, with and without `-feature`); the rows on which the reference dies, hangs or has a valgrind error are refused (phylip 19, nexus / paup 29, selex 33, stockholm / pfam 1, mega 98, hennig86 185, ace / consed 400 less the files that do not start with `AS`, pdb 3). Test `SequenceReaders_EqualSeqret_AllRows` (66 formats), MCP `Seqret_ReadsTheSequenceFormats_AsTheProgram`. **Commits.** 76e86559c (phylip, phylipnon), 210ce128f (jackknifer, hennig86), 4b964dcda (nexus, paup), 5d6a1957d (mega), b88490356 (selex, stockholm, pfam), 58169954b (experiment, ace, consed), 70a8130f9 (pdb, pdbseq, pdbnuc, pdbnucseq)

### F255 - EMBOSS sequence input USA forms (audit A5-8c3h (2d), WP58): ranges, list files, queries on files, `-sbegin` / `-send` / `-sreverse` on the output and its features, `-sid`, `-sdbname`, `-iquery`, `-ioffset`, `-squick`
- **Sources actually opened.** `ajseqread.c` (`ajSeqAllRead`, `ajSeqRead`, `ajSeqinUsa`, `ajSeqinClear`, `ajSeqinClearPos`, `seqinUsaProcess`, `seqinListProcess`, `seqListNoComment`, `seqUsaSave`, `seqUsaRestore`, `seqinFormatSet`, `seqRead`, `seqReadFmt`, `seqDefine`, `seqQueryMatch`, and the readers `seqReadRaw`, `seqReadStrider`, `seqReadNbrf`, `seqReadTreecon`, `seqReadGcg`), `ajquery.c` (`ajQuerystrParseFormat`, `ParseListfile`, `ParseRange`, `ParseRead`, `queryDbfind`, `queryRegInit`, `ajQueryKnownFieldC`, `ajQueryAddField*`, `ajQuerySetWild`), `ajnam.c` (`ajNamFileQuery`), `ajtextread.c` (`ajTextinAccessFile` / `Offset` / `Asis`, `ajTextinClear*`, `ajTextinStore*`), `ajacd.c` (`acdSetSeqall`, `acdSetSeq`), `ajseq.c` (`ajSeqSetRange`, `ajSeqSetRangeRev`, `ajSeqReverseDo`, `ajSeqTrim`, `ajSeqGetBegin`, `ajSeqGetEnd`, `ajSeqClear`), `ajseqwrite.c` (`ajSeqoutWriteSeq`, `seqClone`, `ajSeqoutSetNameDefaultS`), `ajseqtype.c` (`ajSeqTypeCheckIn`, `seqTypeSet`), `ajfeat.c` (`ajFeattableSetRange`, `SetReverse`, `Reverse`, `TrimOff`, `PosI` / `PosII`), `ajstr.c` (the wildcard compares, `ajStrTrimC`, `ajStrExtractWord`, `ajStrTokenNextParseDelimiters`, `ajStrToInt` / `ToLong`), `ajlist.c` (`ajListPushlist`), `ajfile.c` / `ajfileio.c` (`ajFilebuffIsEnded`, `ajBuffreadLinePos`, `ajReadlineTrim`), `ajbase.c` (`ajBaseAlphacharComp`), `emboss/seqret.c`, `union.c`, `maskfeat.c`, `descseq.c` (raw.githubusercontent.com `kimrutherford/EMBOSS/master`), and the `-debug` traces (`seqret.dbg`) and valgrind runs of the installed 6.6.0.
- **Fix.** `EmbossSeqall` (Analysis) is the ACD item and `ajSeqAllRead` / `ajSeqRead`: the USA is cut by the parsers of `ajquery.c` (`EmbossQueryParse` in Infrastructure: the `format::` prefix, the range `[begin:end:r]` and the forms `:begin:end` / `:begin..end:r`, `list::` / `@`, `asis::`, the file name with `file:id`, `file:field:query`, `file{a|b|...}`, `file%offset`, the `-iquery` text, all the messages) and opens the file; a list file (`seqinListProcess`) is read line by line (comments after `#`, `Bad record`, `Failed to open list file`), every entry keeps the range, strand, offset, features and format of the list it was named in (`seqUsaSave` / `seqUsaRestore`), the entries of a nested list go to the START of the list (`ajListPushlist`), the first read of a list clears the position (`ajSeqinClearPos`) so only the first sequence of a file named in a list gets the range, and the messages `Failed to read sequence` follow the loop of `ajSeqRead`. A query keeps the entries that match one of its fields (`seqQueryMatch`: id, sv, gi, acc, org, key, des; `EmbossWild` = `ajCharCmpWild` / `ajCharMatchWildNextC` / `ajCharMatchWildWordC`). The range of the sequence object (`EmbossSeqRange`: `ajSeqSetRange` / `ajSeqSetRangeRev` / `ajSeqReverseDo` with the exact complement table of `ajBaseAlphacharComp` (X stays X, U becomes A), `ajSeqTrim` for `union`, the cut of `seqClone`) and the range of its feature table (`ajFeattableSetRange`, `SetReverse`) reach the output of seqret / seqretsplit, maskfeat and descseq (the `acdSetSeq` path: no `ClearPos`, the strand is applied at once) and union (`ajSeqTrim`). `-sid` names every sequence (`seqDefine`: `Name = Entryname`), `-sdbname` its database, `-ioffset` starts the line readers at a byte position (the binary reader of raw reads the file from its first byte whatever the offset, and finds the file ended when the offset is past its end), `-squick` is accepted. The ACD qualifiers are kept by `EmbossSequenceQualifiers.ParseFile` (`EntryId`, `DbName`, `QueryFields`, `Quick`, `Offset`). A reader defect found on the way: the nbrf reader leaves its type token in the static `seqToken`, which the strider reader then takes as the name of a one-line entry (`>P1;P12345` with no newline is read as `P1`).
- **Reference faults and loops (BLOCKED class, proof by valgrind / repeated runs / the source; the port refuses such inputs with `InvalidOperationException` / `NotSupportedException`).** (a) A list that names itself in a later line is expanded again and again: the program never stops and writes without end; one that names itself first dies with `USA List too deep` (`ajFatal`, exit code 1, no output: the port returns the message as the program prints it). (b) A query that no entry of a format satisfies on a reader that does not consume the refused entry (`FMT_NOMATCH` loop) never stops; the whitespace loop of `seqReadGcg` on a file that starts at an offset in the middle of a line never stops. (c) `seqReadTreecon`: a file whose first line is a count and that holds no sequence reads `Names[0]` of an empty array (valgrind: Invalid read at 0x20 in `ajSeqAllRead`; exit by SIGSEGV). (d) A file name that ends with `|` is a command the library runs (`ajSysCreateInpipeC`), and `ftp:` / `http:` names are read from servers: the data are not part of this port. (e) `file*` file name wildcards list the directory in the order of `readdir`, which the file system decides.
- **Oracle.** `usa_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`scripts/alignment/generate_usa_oracle.py`, seed 20265801): **1 500 / 1 500** `seqret -auto [-feature] -sequence SPEC ...` runs equal or refused with proof (1 473 equal, 27 refused): ranges and strands in every form (`[3:10]`, `[:5]`, `[-4:]`, `[5:2]`, `[0:0:r]`, `:3:10`, `:3..10:r`, invalid `:x`), `format::` prefixes (also unknown), list files (`@`, `list::`, `LIST:`, comments, bad records, missing files, nested lists, ranges and formats of the entries, a range on the list), queries on files (`:id`, `:acc:`, `:des:`, wildcards, `{a|b}`, `%offset`, unknown fields, `-iquery`), the sequence qualifiers `-sbegin1 -send1 -sreverse1 -sid1 -sdbname1 -squick1 -slower1 -supper1 -sprotein1 -snucleotide1 -scircular1 -iquery1 -ioffset1 -firstonly`; the FASTA file, the GFF3 file (with the sequence range and strand applied to the features) and the messages byte for byte. The sequences of a database carry its name (`seq->Db`, `UsaOf`) and the type of the database decides the sequence type (`seqTypeSet`: a database of type P reads nucleotide-looking residues as protein, so `-sreverse` does nothing). `EmbossFeatureLines` reads a LIST of files (`FileEnds`): a read past the end of a file finds the end of the file while the buffer holds lines and goes on in the next file when the buffer is clear (`ajBuffreadLinePos`, `ajFileReopenNext`), so an entry (the FASTA part of a GFF3 file, the last entry of a flat file) ends with its file. `EmbossSeqretRequest.Definitions` carries the configuration text; the MCP tools read the databases through `files` and the USA in `sequenceValue` (a parameter for the configuration text follows with `entret`, registered below).
- **Reference limits (BLOCKED class).** The method `direct` reads the files of the directory in the order of `readdir`, which the file system decides (measured: `ls -f` lists b, c, a for files created a, b, c), so a database with several matching files is used only for queries for an identifier that occurs in exactly one file and whose files all read cleanly in the format of the database; the port reads the names in ordinal order. A GFF3 file without features read with `-feature` makes the library die by a segmentation fault when its table is null (valgrind: Invalid read in `ajFeattableIsCircular`): refused. The methods that need an index (`emblcd`, `emboss`, `blast`, `gcg`), a network (`entrez`, `url`, `srs`, `dbfetch`, `mrs`, ...), servers and data resources are not implemented (registered below).

### F261 - EMBOSS `union -feature -source` (audit A5-8c3h (4), WP58): `union_CopyFeatures`, the source features, the feature file
- **Sources actually opened.** `emboss/union.c` (`union_CopyFeatures`, the loop of `main`), `ajfeat.c` (`ajFeattableNewSeq`, `ajFeatNew`, `ajFeatNewFeat`, `ajFeattableAddNew`, `ajFeattableNewFtable`, `ajFeattableTrimOff`, `ajFeatTrimOffRange`, `ajFeattableTrim`, `ajFeattableSetRange`, `ajFeatTagAddCC`), `ajseq.c` (`ajSeqNewSeq`, `ajSeqTrim`, `ajSeqGetFeatCopy`), `ajseqwrite.c` (`ajSeqoutWriteSeq`, `seqClone`), `ajfeatwrite.c` (`ajFeattabOutOpen`, `featoutUfoProcess`, `featFindOutFormatC`, `ajFeattableWriteUfo`, `ajFeattableWrite`; fetched from `ajax/core/ajfeatwrite.c`), `ajfile.c` (`ajFilenameTrimAll`) and the installed program (default file names, messages).
- **Fix.** `EmbossUnionProgram` joins the feature tables as the original does: the table of the output is made for the first sequence before the sequence is trimmed (`ajFeattableNewSeq`: the length of the untrimmed sequence), every sequence is trimmed (`ajSeqTrim`: the table of the sequence has the range of the sequence, so `ajFeattableTrimOff` shifts its features by TWICE the offset: the table range `Start` is the begin and the offset is begin - 1), copied (`ajSeqGetFeatCopy`) and its features copied again by `union_CopyFeatures` (the positions of the feature, NOT of the parts of its location, moved by the offset; the feature that is a source feature of an earlier union is not duplicated; `ajFeattableAddNew` renumbers the groups and raises the length with unsigned arithmetic, so a start before the sequence is the largest length), a source feature (`-source`: type source, source union, tag `*origid: NAME`) is made for every sequence; the copies of the sequence (`ajSeqNewSeq`: uniseq before the trim, prev_seq after it) check the tags again, so a bad tag value warns again for every copy. The feature file is called after the base of the output (`ajFilenameTrimAll`) and the feature format as typed (default `gff`), or `-ofname2`; an unknown feature format is written as gff3 and reported twice ("will write as gff3 instead", "will write as gff instead"); a format that does not fit the sequence type is "Feature format 'pir' not supported for nucleotide sequence features" + "ajSeqWriteSeq features output failed UFO: ''" + "No features written to output file". Features that a sequence output format writes INSIDE the sequence file (nbrf, pir, embl ...) are refused (registered under (2c-rest)).

### F263 - EMBOSS `twofeat` (audit A5-8c3h (4), WP58): pairs of features in a required relation, reported
- **Sources actually opened.** `emboss/twofeat.c` (`twofeat_find_features`, `twofeat_MatchFeature`, `twofeat_MatchPatternTags`, `twofeat_rippledown`, `twofeat_check_match`, `twofeat_report_hits`, the conversion of the ACD values in `main`), `ajreport.c` (`ajReportWrite`, `ajReportClose`: the warning "No hits in output report file", `ajReportSetSeqstats`), `ajseqread.c` (`ajSeqallNext`: `Totlength` += `ajSeqGetLenTrimmed`), `ajseq.c` (`ajSeqallGetseqBegin` / `GetseqEnd`), `ajlist.c` (`ajListPush`: at the head), `ajfeat.c` (`ajFeatIsLocalRange`, `ajFeatNew`, `ajFeatTagAddSS`, `ajFeatGetStart` / `GetEnd` / `GetStrand`, `ajFeatTypeMatchWildS`), the installed program (the fatal message, the echo of the header).
- **Fix.** `EmbossTwofeatProgram`: per sequence the local features in the range of the stream that match the criteria of A and of B are copied into two tables (`ajFeatNewFeat`: the tags are checked again), every pair (A in table order, B in table order) is tested by `twofeat_check_match` and the hits are reported in the REVERSE order they were found (`ajListPush`); the quirks of the original are kept: the scores are cut to integers, `-asense -` is read as any sense, the distance criteria are ignored unless `minrange < maxrange`, the opposite sense with the strands different falls through the switch into `ajFatal("Unknown sense type: 2")` (the program dies: "EMBOSS An error in twofeat.c at line 932"), the order switch is made on the SENSE code (the same sense means "A then B" from the middle of the features), `-order` is not used, a feature is never paired with itself. The hits become features of source twofeat and type `-typeout` (start of the first, end of the last, strand minus only when both are minus, tags `*startA` `*endA` `*startB` `*endB` as notes) or, with `-twoout`, the copies of the two features; the report is written by the engine of F262 with the tags startA / endA / startB / endB, `ajReportClose` (the footer with the numbers of sequences and the trimmed lengths, "No hits in output report file" when nothing was reported, also when the report format was refused for every table).
- **Reference limits (BLOCKED class).** The gff3 files without features read with the features of the sequence (SIGSEGV, valgrind Invalid read in `ajFeattableIsCircular`): 38 of the 1 000 rows; refused. The opposite-sense fatal error is NOT a reference fault: the program stops and the port reproduces its message (7 rows).
- **Oracle.** `twofeat_oracle.jsonl.gz` (`scripts/alignment/generate_twofeat_oracle.py`, seed 20265809): **1 000 / 1 000** runs of `twofeat -auto -sequence in.dat -outfile o.rep [-sformat1 F] [-sbegin1 N] [-send1 N] [-asource ..] [-atype ..] [-asense 0|+|-] [-aminscore X] [-amaxscore X] [-atag ..] [-avalue ..] [-bsource ..] [-btype ..] ... [-overlap A|O|NO|NW|AW|BW] [-minrange N] [-maxrange N] [-rangetype N|L|R|F] [-sense A|S|O] [-order ..] [-twoout] [-typeout T] [-rformat2 FORMAT] [-raccshow2] [-rdesshow2] [-rscoreshow2 N] [-rstrandshow2 N] [-rusashow2] [-rmaxall2 N] [-rmaxseq2 N]` equal or refused with proof (962 equal, 656 with a report in 21 report formats, 191 with `-twoout`, 7 fatal errors, 38 refused): EMBL entries with CDS / mRNA / exon / gene / misc features (joins, complements, orders, partial ends, tags, 1 - 3 entries per file), the reader oracle inputs in 7 formats, damaged files, the command-line echo of the header, dates faked. ### F264 - EMBOSS sequence writers ncbi, gifasta, nib / nibble, dasdna, das, asn1 (audit A5-8c3h (2c-rest), WP58)
- **Sources actually opened.** `ajseqwrite.c` (`seqWriteNcbi`, `seqWriteGifasta`, `seqNcbiKnowndb`, `seqWriteNibble`, `seqWriteDasdna`, `seqWriteDasseq`, `seqCleanDasdna`, `seqCleanDasseq`, `seqWriteAsn1`, `seqWriteSeq` (`linepos`), `seqClone` (`Setdb`, `Db`, `Gi`, `Offset`), `seqDeclone`, `ajSeqoutWriteSeq`), `ajfileio.c` (`ajWritelineSpace`, `ajWritebin*`) and the installed program (the bytes of the nibble files: `3aede96b` + length + 4-bit codes; the footer of a DAS file with `-ossingle`).
- **Fix.** `EmbossSeqWrite` (Infrastructure) writes the formats: `ncbi` / `gifasta` (the identifier `gi|N|db|version|name (version) description` from `Gi`, `Setdb` / `Db` (`unk` when there is none), the version (`Sv`, else the accession), the databases of `seqNcbiKnowndb`, `lcl`, `bbs` (ncbi only), `BL_ORD_ID` with the run-wide counter of each writer (`EmbossSeqWriteRun`: a `static` of each C function), `gi|000000|` for gifasta without a GI), `nib` / `nibble` (the file is REWOUND before every sequence, so the entry of a later sequence overwrites the start of the file and the rest of a longer earlier entry stays; the magic number and the length little endian; the residues as 4-bit codes A 2, C 1, G 3, T / U 0, other 4), `dasdna` / `das` (the XML header when the run wrote no sequence yet - `-ossingle` does not reset the count -, `start` / `stop` with the offset of the range, the footer written when the file that is open at the end of the run is closed: with `-ossingle` only the last file has it; the programs extractfeat, coderet and union write it too), `asn1` (`seq { ... }` with the residues in lines of 78 characters, the first after the 17 characters of `iupacna "`). With `-ossingle` and no sequence written the library does not warn "No sequences written" (there is no open file). nib, nibble and dasdna write nucleotide sequences only ("Sequence format 'nib' not supported for protein sequences"); ncbi, gifasta, das and asn1 also write proteins.
- **Oracle.** `seqout_oracle_ncbi.jsonl.gz`, `seqout_oracle_nibble.jsonl.gz`, `seqout_oracle_das.jsonl.gz`, `seqout_oracle_asn1.jsonl.gz` (`scripts/alignment/generate_seqout_oracle.py`, seeds 20265810 - 20265813): **260 / 260 runs per format** of `seqret -auto -sequence in.dat [-sformat1 F] -outseq OUT -osformat2 FMT [-ossingle2 [-osextension2 E] [-osdirectory2 sub]] [-osname2 N] [-firstonly]` for ncbi, gifasta, nib, nibble, dasdna, das and asn1 (1 820 runs, all equal): the reader-oracle inputs (writer outputs, entries with features, damaged texts) and entries with NCBI-style identifiers (`gi|N|db|acc.ver|name`, `lcl|`, `gnl|BL_ORD_ID|N`, ...), with the names of the formats in any case, the `format::file` forms, `-ossingle`, extensions and directories. Test `EmbossSeqout_Oracle_Tests.SequenceWriters_EqualSeqret_AllRows` (now 26 names), MCP `Seqret_WritesTheNcbiDasAndAsn1Formats_AsTheProgram`. **Commits.** 37fd625db (code, oracles, tests, MCP descriptions).

### F274 - EMBOSS readers nibble / nib verified (audit A5-8c3h (2b-rest), WP59)
- **Sources actually opened.** `ajseqread.c` (`seqReadNibble`, the format table: nibble and nib share the reader), the installed program.
- **Measured.** `seqret -sformat1 nibble` and `-sformat1 nib` fail on every file - FASTA text, and the nibble file that `seqret -osformat2 nibble` writes (magic `3aede96b`, length, 4-bit codes) - with "Error: Unable to read sequence" and "Died: seqret terminated: Bad value for '-sequence' with -auto defined" (valgrind clean): the reader ends with `ajTextinGetRecords()`, which is false for an input it read without counting records, after it has appended the residues. The port now fails the same way (before: `InvalidOperationException` "not read by this port"). Test `EmbossNibbleReader_Tests`. **Commits.** a1dfead43. Open (registered in WP59): with a valid magic number the try-every-format loop leaves the buffer ended, so the formats after nibble in the table cannot read the file.

### F275 - EMBOSS databases of the method emboss (the index files of dbxfasta / dbxflat / dbxcompress) and the server / resource / include / if blocks of the configuration (audit A5-8c3h (c), WP60)
- **Sources actually opened.** `ajindex.c` (`ajBtreeReadParamsC`, `ajBtreeCacheNewReadC` / `ajBtreeIdcacheNewC`, `btreeGetBlockC`, `btreeGetPointers`, `btreeGetNumPointers`, `btreeReadIdbucket`, `btreeIdbucketIdlistAll`, `btreeIdentFetchMulti*`, `btreeNumbucketBthitlist` / `Btidlist`, `btreePribucketIdlist` / `FindId`, `btreeSecbucketIdlist`, `btreeSecTreeList`, `btreeReadAllSecLeaves`, `ajBtreeIdentFetchHit`, `ajBtreeIdentFetchwildHit`, `ajBtreeKeyFetchHit`, `ajBtreeKeyFetchwildHit`, `btreeKeyFullSearchHit`, `btreeKeywordFullSearchHit`, `ajBtreeReadEntriesC`, `btreeHitCmp`, `ajBtreeHitHash`, the page layout of `ajindex.h`), `ajtable.c` (`ajTableNewFunctionLen`, `ajTablePutClean`, `ajTableResizeHashsize`, `ajTableMergeOr` / `And` / `Eor` / `Not`, `ajTableToarrayValues`, `ajTablestrHash`), `ajlist.c` (`ajListSortTwoUnique`), `ajstr.c` (`ajStrFmtQuery`, `ajStrMatchWildS`), `ajtextdb.c` (`textAccessEmboss`, `textEmbossQryOpen`, `textEmbossQryEntry`, `textEmbossQryQuery`, `textEmbossQryNext`, `textEmbossAll`), `ajnam.c` (`ajNamDbData`, `ajNamDbGetDbalias`, `namProcessFile`, `namListParse`, `namRsAttrFieldS`, `ajNamGetValueC`, `namError`), `ajseqread.c` (`seqRead`, `seqQueryMatch`), and the installed `dbxfasta`, `dbxflat`, `dbxcompress`, `seqret`, `entret` (the index files are made by the indexers; the bytes are read back by the port).
- **Fix.** `EmbossBtreeCache` (Infrastructure) reads a B+tree index file as the library reads it (parameter file `NAME.pEXT`; pages of `Pagesize` bytes at the offsets of the page pointers - a compressed index keeps its pages packed and its pointers are offsets in the compressed file, so the same reads work; primary id / acc / sv trees with their id buckets and the secondary trees of the duplicates, secondary keyword trees des / key / org with their primary buckets, the numeric buckets); `EmbossHitTable` is the chained hash table of `ajtable.c` with the hash of `ajBtreeHitHash` (the hits of the fields of a query come back in the order of its buckets, the merges of the link operators `|` `&` `^` `!` and the else rule are those of `ajTableMerge*`); a hit whose entry cannot be read ends the read; `QryDone` unless `caseidmatch`, so with `caseidmatch: Y` the entry is compared again with the lower-case words of the query as the reader does), the fatal messages of the library with their source lines (e.g. `btreeGetPointers: No keys in node` at line 6844 for an index with no keyword). `EmbossSeqall` reads one entry per hit (`textin->Single`). `EmbossNames` is now `namListParse`: `RES` / `RESOURCE` (attributes of the type Index: `idlen`, `acclen`, ... checked against `fields`), `SERVER`, `INCLUDE` (the included file is an entry of `files`; ### F276 - EMBOSS coderet -sreverse1 on GFF3 features (audit A5-8c3h (d-rest), WP60)
- **Defect.** `coderet -sreverse1` on a GFF3 entry: the reference writes the whole sequence as one non-coding region and a CDS of one residue; the port wrote the regions between the features. **Cause.** A GFF3 feature table has no length, so `ajFeatReverse` gives the positions `1 + 0 - End` (negative); `ajFeatGetStart` / `ajFeatGetEnd` return `ajuint`, so `ajStrFmtLowerSub(&copyseq, ajFeatGetStart(gf)-1, ajFeatGetEnd(gf)-1)` and `ajStrAppendSubS(.., ajFeatGetStart(gf)-1, ..)` (`ajFeatGetSeq`, `ajFeatGetSeqJoin`) get huge positive `ajlong` values that are clipped to the last residue, not positions counted from the end.
- **Fix.** `EmbossCoderetProgram.LocMark` and `EmbossExtractfeatProgram.GetSeq` / `GetSeqJoin` take the positions as `unchecked((uint)(start - 1))`; the `-sreverse1` rows are back in the coderet oracle (1 100 / 1 100 equal; the generator no longer needs `CODERET_NOREVERSE`). **Commits.** 88f6ef93c.

### F277 - EMBOSS union output qualifiers and the experiment writer with features (audit A5-8c3h (d-rest), WP60)
- **Measured on 6.6.0.** `union -ossingle2 -osdirectory2 D -osextension2 E -osname2 N -ofdirectory2 D2 [-outseq F]`: the joined sequence is written to `D/name.E` (lower case; `-osdirectory2` is also the directory of the output file, the default name is `BASE.format` with the name of the first sequence or `-osname2`); a missing directory ends the program ("Failed to open output file ... in directory", "Unable to write sequence to") or, with `-ossingle2`, kills it by a fault (refused); the feature file goes to `-ofdirectory2` (a directory that does not exist: the warnings "Failed to open output file" and "ajSeqoutWriteSeq features output file open failed" / "seqWriteListAppend features output failed to open UFO"); the unknown feature format message comes after the opening of the sequence file. The experiment writer calls `seqoutUfoLocal` (EMBL features inside the file; Swiss-Prot features for a protein), which `seqret -feature -osformat2 experiment` had not done in the port; `union` writes bam, debug (the feature table size of the joined table, the input format of the first sequence) and experiment.
- **Fix.** `EmbossUnionRequest.OutSingle` / `OutDirectory` / `OutExtension` / `OutName` / `OutFeatDirectory` / `DefaultOutSeq` / `ExistingDirectories`, `EmbossUnionOutput.SingleFiles` / `SequenceFileName` / `FeatureDirectory`; the table flag of the experiment format; `LocalFeatureFormat(format, protein)`. The tag check of a copy of the feature table is repeated by the set writers (`seqWriteListAppend`). MCP `union` `outputSingle` / `outputDirectory` / `outputExtension` (`singleFiles`).
- **Oracle.** `union_feature_oracle.jsonl.gz` regenerated (**1 200 / 1 200 runs equal**: 12 % with `-ossingle2`, `-osextension2`, `-osdirectory2`, `-osname2`, `-ofdirectory2`, no `-outseq`; the output formats now include experiment, debug and bam), `seqout_oracle_features_experiment.jsonl.gz` (220 runs of `seqret -feature -osformat2 experiment`, equal). **Commits.** 706a9232a, a15416a6b.

### F278 - EMBOSS featreport / twofeat report file qualifiers and the features input qualifiers (audit A5-8c3h (d-rest), WP60)
- **Measured on 6.6.0 (`acdSetReport`, `acdOutFilename`, `ajFilenameReplacePathS`).** Without `-outfile` the report is `BASE.featreport` / `BASE.twofeat` (BASE = `-rname3` with `ajStrFmtWord` (blanks become underscores, the part before the last colon is cut), else the lower-case name of the first sequence; the extension `-rextension3` unless it is empty); `-rdirectory3` is put in front of a name that has no directory (also of `stdout`: the file `sub/stdout`); a directory that does not exist stops the program ("Warning: Failed to open output file", "Error: Unable to open report file", "Died: ... Bad value for '-outfile'"); `-outfile ''`: "Report file is required"; a report format that needs more tags than the program has stops the program before the file is opened. The qualifiers of `-features` (`-fformat2`, `-fopenfile2`, `-iquery2`, `-ioffset2`, `-fask2`, `-freverse2`, `-fcircular2`) change nothing (`ajFeattableReverse` does nothing for a table that is not flagged; the format is set on a field the reader does not use); `-fbegin2` / `-fend2` give the range. Found on the way: a dasgff report wrote its XML header for every table (the first only, as `ftout->Count`), and the motif report never stops after a feature of a negative length (`ajStrAssignResC` / `ajStrSetResRound` double a reserved size of 0 for ever: `MotifTmpRes`, refused).
- **Fix.** `EmbossReportQualifiers.Name` / `Extension` / `Directory` / `FeatureInput`, `EmbossOutPath.OpenReport`, `EmbossFeatreportRequest` / `EmbossTwofeatRequest.DefaultReportFile` / `ExistingDirectories`, `EmbossFeatureReportOutput.ReportFile`; MCP `featreport` / `twofeat` `outputFile` and `reportFile` in the results.
- **Oracle.** `featreport_oracle.jsonl.gz`, `twofeat_oracle.jsonl.gz` regenerated (1 000 runs each, 30 % with the file qualifiers and, for featreport, the features qualifiers; all equal or refused with proof). **Commits.** 4420f8ec0, a15416a6b.
