### F280 - EMBOSS sequence programs (audit A5-8c3h, WP61): getorf, revseq, transeq, extractseq, cutseq, degapseq, trimseq, skipseq, nthseq, notseq, pasteseq, trimest, newseq, yank, seqcount, splitter, maskseq, maskambignuc, maskambigprot, trimspace, nospace, notab, noreturn
- **Sources actually opened (raw.githubusercontent.com, EMBOSS 6.6.0 mirror).** The programs `getorf.c transeq.c revseq.c extractseq.c cutseq.c degapseq.c trimseq.c skipseq.c nthseq.c notseq.c pasteseq.c trimest.c newseq.c yank.c seqcount.c splitter.c maskseq.c maskambig*.c trimspace.c nospace.c notab.c noreturn.c` and their `.acd`; the library `ajtrn.c` (genetic code tables, `trnComplete`), `ajseqtype.c` (the type table, `ajSeqTypeCheckIn`, `ajSeqTypeCheckS`, `seqTypeFix`), `ajseq.c` (`ajSeqTrim`, `ajSeqReverseDo`, `ajSeqReverseOnly`, `ajSeqGetBegin`, `ajSeqAssignSeqLenC`, `ajSeqClear`, `seqMakeUsa`), `ajseqread.c` (`ajSeqallNext`), `ajrange.c`, `ajstr.c` (`ajStrRemoveGap`, `ajStrKeepRange`, `ajStrCutRange`, `ajStrInsertS`, `ajStrAppendSubS`, `ajStrRemoveWhiteExcess`), `ajfileio.c` (`ajReadlinePos`, `ajWritelineNewline`), `ajacd.c` (`acdSetSeq`, `acdInTypeSeqSave`, `acdArgSave`), `ajmath.c` (`ajRandomSeed` for the random programs).
- **Defects found and fixed in the library (all by the oracle).** (1) `Translator.FindOrfs` models getorf with the NCBI tables and four documented corrections; the program (`getorf_FindORFs`) differs, so the scan got a second model, `Translator.FindOrfsGetorfProgram` (the same loop, the EMBOSS genetic code tables of `EmbossTrn` = `ajtrn.c` with `trnComplete`, the residues as the program holds them, the quirks of the program: a START at the last codon is never written, the full-length circular record is the translation in every mode, the frame-3 size test is `>= maxsize`); getorf is `EmbossGetorfProgram` over it (800 / 800). (2) The sequence type check was three special cases; now the whole table of `ajseqtype.c` (`EmbossSeqType`: every type, the fix of bad characters, the messages), used by the readers and by the type check of an output sequence (`seqClone`: gaps converted or every non-letter removed, `?` converted). (3) The sequence object of a stream is ONE object that every read refills: `ajSeqClear` does not reset `Offset` / `Offend`, so they stay from the sequence before (getorf headers of the second sequence of a file with `-send` show it; `ajSeqAssignSeqS` and `ajSeqReverseForce` reset / swap them): `EmbossSeqall` carries them. (4) For an ACD `sequence` input `-sbegin` / `-send` replace the range of the USA (`yank in.dat[3:15:r] -send1 71` is `[3:71:r]`). (5) An output sequence with no `type` takes the type of the first input (`acdInTypeSeq`; `maskseq` removes the mask character `#`, `-`, `?` of an `any` output). (6) `ajWritelineNewline` of an empty string writes nothing, not even the newline (hennig86 with an empty sequence); the nexus and msf writers die by a fault on an empty sequence (refused). (7) The SAM `@PG CL:` line quotes the arguments that are no word.
- **New infrastructure (additive).** `EmbossTrn` (+ `EmbossTrnData.g.cs`, generated from the `EGC.*` files), `EmbossSeqType`, `EmbossNuc`, `EmbossSeqoutStream` (the sequence output of a program: format by name, the sets written at close, `-ossingle`, the footer / BAM blocks, the `No sequences written` warning), `EmbossAcdArgs` (the ACD command line: `acdArgsParse` through `AcdCommandLine`, integers with the limits and the warning `integer value out of range V less than (reset to) L`, menus with the messages `'x' is not a valid menu option`, ranges with `Bad range specification`), `EmbossProgramRunner.Run(program, args, files)` -> `EmbossRunResult(Stdout, Stderr, ExitCode, Files)`; ACD profiles of the 46 programs of the work package (`generate_emboss_acd_profiles.py`). MCP tools (generated by `scripts/docs/gen_emboss_wp61_tools.py`): 19 tools.
- **Oracle.** `scripts/alignment/emboss_prog_oracle_lib.py` + `generate_emboss_prog_getorf_oracle.py` / `generate_emboss_prog_seq_oracle.py`: every row is one run of `<program> -auto ARGS` (input formats fasta embl genbank gcg nbrf raw ig ncbi staden codata fastq, 25 output formats, sequence qualifiers, option values, invalid values): standard output, error stream, exit status and every written file byte for byte. Rows per program: getorf 800, every other program 320; the reference runs that die by a signal or never end are refused by the port (trimseq with a window not shorter than the sequence reads outside it, the nexus / msf writers with an empty sequence). Test `EmbossPrograms_Oracle_Tests.Program_EqualsTheInstalledProgram_AllRows` (one case per embedded oracle). **Commits.** e458dfe71, 5698e9d17, 6b056ec97.

### F281 - EMBOSS programs of work package 62 (audit A5-8c3h, WP62): shuffleseq, msbar, makenucseq, makeprotseq, nthseqset, listor, infoseq, wordcount, seqxref, showorf, prettyseq (and the date of the WP61 oracles)
- **Sources actually opened (raw.githubusercontent.com, EMBOSS 6.6.0 mirror).** The programs `shuffleseq.c msbar.c makenucseq.c makeprotseq.c nthseqset.c listor.c infoseq.c wordcount.c seqxref.c showorf.c prettyseq.c` and their `.acd`; the library `ajmath.c` (`ajRandomSeed`, `ajRandomDouble`, `ajRandomNumber`), `ajstr.c` (`ajStrRandom`, `ajStrInsertC`, `ajStrCutRange`, `ajStrKeepRange`, `ajStrParseC` / `ajStrParseWhite`, the `ajStrToken*` family, `ajStrCmpCaseS`), `ajsort.c` (`ajSortUintIncI`, `ajSortIntIncI`), `ajtable.c` + `embword.c` (the hash table of `wordcount`: `ajTableNewFunctionLen`, `ajTablePut`, `ajTableResizeHashsize`, `ajTableToarrayValues`, `embWordGetTable`, `embWordPrintTableFI`), `ajseqread.c` (`ajSeqsetRead`, `ajSeqsetallRead`, `seqDefine`, `seqinFormatSet`, `ajSeqParseNcbi`), `ajseqwrite.c` (`ajSeqoutWriteSet`, `seqsetClone`, `seqClone`), `ajseq.c` (`ajSeqsetFromList`, `ajSeqsetReverse`, `ajSeqsetIsNuc`, `ajSeqxreflistSort`), `ajlist.c` (`ajListSort`, `ajListSortUnique`), `ajacd.c` (`acdSetList`, `acdListValue`, `acdSetInt`, `acdSetSeqset`, `acdSetSeqsetall`, `acdSetInfile`, `acdSetCodon`, `acdArgsParse` / `acdArgSave`), `ajcod.c` (`ajCodRead`, `codReadEmboss`, `codFix`, `ajCodGetCodonlist`, `ajCodNewCodenum`), `ajtime.c` (`ajTimeSetLocal`, `ajTimeSetS`, `ajTimeRefToday`), `ajdan.c` (`ajMeltGC`), `ajrange.c`, `ajbase.c` + the data file `Ebases.iub`; the installed programs. Reference data: the installed EMBOSS 6.6.0 (`/usr/bin/<program>`, libajax 6.0.5).
- **Defects found and fixed (all by the oracle).** (1) The oracles of WP61 were recorded on the day of their generation: every row that holds the run date (genbank, embl, gff, mase, ... headers) could pass on that one day only (the port used `DateTime.Now`). The programs now run under a clock (`EmbossRunEnvironment`: the date of the writers, the microseconds of `gettimeofday`, the variable `timetoday`), the oracle runs them under the shim `scripts/alignment/faketime.c` with a date per row (`epoch`), the 23 WP61 files were re-recorded by `refresh_emboss_prog_oracle_clock.py` (only the rows with a date changed) and the test passes the clock to the port. (2) `ajTimeRefToday` (the headers of the set formats: hennig86, nexus, msf, ...) takes the clock, while `ajTimeRefTodayFmt` (genbank, embl, gff, mase) takes the variable `timetoday` (`SET timetoday "yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss"`, read by `ajFmtScanS` with the fields it does not give 0, years since 1900, `mktime` normalisation: `1` is 30 Nov 1900): `EmbossSeqWriteRun.RefToday`. (3) The command line of a run is what `acdArgSave` keeps (`-slower` is `-slower1`, `-sformat` is `-sformat1`, a boolean without its value): `AcdCommandLine.SavedCommandLine` (the SAM `@PG` line). (4) `acdSetInt` checks the default against the limits too (`-minimum 30` resets the default `-maximum 10`). (5) An exhausted `seqall` that is read again reads from an empty USA (`ajSeqallClear`): "Failed to open filename ''" at every later call (msbar reads its `-othersequence` that way once per mutated sequence). (6) A set is read by `ajSeqsetRead` / `ajSeqsetallRead`: every member is a new object (no date object, accuracy buffer or offsets of the member before) and, after the first member, the members have the format the input found (`seqinFormatSet`), so `seqDefine` gives the members of a nucleic-only format the type N and every `x` becomes `n` (`EmbossSeqin.MarkFormatSet`); a `seqsetall` starts a new set when a reader finishes one (`Multidone`: phylip, phylipnon, treecon, jackknifer, nexus, mega); `-sreverse` of a set reverses every member after reading (`ajSeqsetReverse`) and does not touch the members of a `seqsetall` range. (7) `ajSeqoutWriteSet` is not `ajSeqoutWriteSeq`: the format is not asked whether it supports the kind of the sequence, an unknown format is reported at every call and written as FASTA; the EMBL writers write a protein by `seqWriteSwiss` (the port refused it). (8) `acdListValue`: exact code, exact description, unique prefix (an empty value matches nothing), the messages `'x' is ambiguous (...)` / `'x' is not a valid menu option` / `Menu needs / allows no more than N values`.
- **Refused with proof (no defined result in the reference).** `msbar` with a block of size 0 (`-minimum 0`: `msbar_Insert` with no residue calls `ajStrInsertS` on a NULL string: segmentation fault; valgrind: invalid read at address 0x10), a deletion from an empty string (`ajStrCutRange` writes before the buffer); `msbar` inputs the program takes more than 8 s to read (an NCBI-style FASTA identifier with two barred tokens: `for(i=0;i<nt-3;++i)` with an unsigned `nt` takes 28 s, the result is the one the port already returns); a multi-dataset mega file of `nthseqset` (valgrind: invalid read in the reader), multi-dataset nexus. `showorf` and `prettyseq` read one byte before a string (`p[-1]`): that byte is the high byte of the size field of the heap chunk, 0 on every glibc, so the loops stop there as at a NUL; the oracle does not count this one valgrind report as an error (`valgrind_bad(..., tolerate_underflow=True)`), every other report refuses the row.
- **New infrastructure (additive).** `EmbossRandom` (the generator of `ajmath.c`, `ajStrRandom`, the Shell sorts), `EmbossRunEnvironment`, `EmbossSeqset` (`seqset` / `seqsetall`), `EmbossSeqoutStream.WriteSet`, `EmbossAcdArgs.List` (ACD multiple lists), `EmbossWordTable` (`ajTable` of `embword.c`), `EmbossStrParse` (`ajStrParseC` with its static state and warning), `EmbossStrtod`, `EmbossCodonUsage` (the EMBOSS / cusp format of `ajCodRead`), the programs in `EmbossSequencePrograms.Random.cs` / `.Sets.cs` / `.Report.cs`; MCP tools (generated by `scripts/docs/gen_emboss_wp62_tools.py`): shuffleseq, msbar, makenucseq, makeprotseq, nthseqset, listor, infoseq, wordcount, seqxref (the random tools take the microseconds of the clock).
- **Oracle.** `scripts/alignment/generate_emboss_prog_random_oracle.py` (shuffleseq msbar makenucseq makeprotseq: every row has a fixed clock, `usec` or `timetoday`; every row is run twice and dropped when the runs differ; rows that touch invalid memory are run under valgrind and stored as refusals) and `generate_emboss_prog_report_oracle.py` (nthseqset listor infoseq wordcount seqxref showorf prettyseq). Rows: shuffleseq 300, msbar 300, makenucseq 300, makeprotseq 300, nthseqset 300, listor 300, infoseq 300, wordcount 300, seqxref 300, showorf 300, prettyseq 300; each row compares standard output, error stream, exit status and every written file byte for byte. **Commits.** 27c4bd68d, 0a3771470, 6782590c5, fc64f3804, affaf75de, 21ebd3da1, 79f764b03, 807e4f7a9, f5012a699, 1f05b9a09.

### F282 - EMBOSS programs of work package 63 (audit A5-8c3h, WP63): tcode, checktrans, plotorf, wordfinder, marscan; the report / graph / feature-output / alignment adapters of the ACD runner
- **Sources actually opened (raw.githubusercontent.com, EMBOSS 6.6.0 mirror).** `tcode.c checktrans.c plotorf.c wordfinder.c marscan.c preg.c dreg.c tfscan.c` and the `.acd` of the installed programs (`/usr/share/EMBOSS/acd`), the library `ajacd.c` (`acdSetInt` clamping, `acdSetFloat`, `acdSetReport`, `acdSetGraphxy`, `acdSetFeatout`, `acdSetAlign`, `acdInFileSave`, `acdArgSave`), `ajgraph.c` (`ajGraphxySetDevicetype`, the `graphType` table, `GraphxyDisplayToData`, `GraphxyDisplayToBedgraph`, `GraphxyDisplayToDas` / `ToWiggle`, `GraphClose`, `ajGraphDataReplace`, `ajGraphdataSetTruescale`, `ajGraphdataAddposRect`), `ajreport.c` (header, `ajReportClose`: "No hits in output report file"), `ajfeat.c` (`ajFeattableClear`), `ajfeatwrite.c` (`ajFeattableWrite`), `ajalign.c` (`ajAlignValid`, `alignConsStats`, the format table), `ajseq.c` (`ajSeqNewRangeC`, `ajSeqIsNuc`, `ajSeqcvtNewStr`), `ajseqwrite.c` (`ajSeqoutWriteSeq`), `ajarr.c` (`ajArrCommaList`, `ajFloatGet`, `ajFloatPut`), `ajstr.c` (`ajStrTokenAssignC` / `ajStrTokenNewC`, `ajStrParseCountC`), `embword.c` (`embWordBuildMatchTable`, `wordOrderMatchTable`), `embaln.c` (`embAlignReportLocal`), `embpatlist.c` (`embPatlistRegexSearchAll`), `ajreg.c` (`ajRegExecall`: the DFA search of PCRE). Reference: the installed EMBOSS 6.6.0 (libajax 6.0.5; plplot 5.x), valgrind.
- **Defects found and fixed (all by the oracle).** (1) `EmbossProgramBase.DefaultOutfile` (the default name of an `outfile` of `showorf`, `prettyseq`, `wordcount`, `seqxref`, `yank`, `seqcount`, `listor`) took the base name of the input FILE; `acdInFileSave` keeps the NAME of the first sequence (lower case, `ajFilenameTrimAll`): `showorf -sequence file.dat` writes `myname.showorf` (`listor` names the set by its file and has the extension `list`: `q.list`). The oracles of WP61 / WP62 always gave `-outfile`, so they never saw it; the generators now omit it in 10 % of the rows. (2) The alignment writer marked a column of two identical non-letters (`*` of a stop) with `|`: the markup line is made from the consensus character (`alignConsStats`: the upper case residue), and a character that is no letter has none, so EMBOSS prints a blank (the Similarity count still counts the column: `water` of two `...W*K...` rows says 20/20 and prints a blank under the stop). `SequenceAligner.EmbossColumnMarks` now blanks identity / similarity marks of non-letters (needle, water, supermatcher, wordfinder, ...). (3) The sequence-style alignment formats (msf, clustal, mega, nexus, fasta, ...) name an unnamed row EMBOSS_001, EMBOSS_002 ... (`ajSeqoutSetNameDefaultS`; the counter runs on across the alignments of one file). (4) `EmbossSeqoutStream`: an unknown `format::` prefix of the output name is a USA the library cannot write to ("Unable to write sequence to 'dir/foo::s.out'", the program dies), an unknown `-osformat` is only reported when the first sequence is written; the type checks of `ajSeqoutWriteSeq` use `ajSeqIsNuc` / `ajSeqIsProt` (the residues of a sequence that has no type). (5) `ajFloatPut` of an unsigned index below 0 (tcode: a later sequence shorter than the window less one) asks for 16 GB (`Memory allocation failed in ajMemCallocZero`, status 255): refused (the result depends on the memory of the machine); `x[-1]` of a plot without a point (valgrind: invalid read) and a step of 0 (the arrays grow until the program is killed) are refused as well. (6) `ajStrTokenAssignC` skips the leading delimiters and `ajStrTokenNewC` does not: `ajArrCommaList(",ATG")` counts 1 token and parses the first one, an empty string (plotorf `-start ,ATG` finds no start codon). (7) `ajAlignValid`: an explicit `-awidth` below 10 is reset to 10 with the warning "Alignment width (-awidth=N) too narrow, reset to 10".
- **Refused with proof.** Graph devices that draw with plplot (ps, cps, hpgl, hp7470, hp7580, meta, png, gif, pdf, svg, xterm, tek, tekt, x11: files of the plplot drivers, "Can't open display", terminal escape codes) are not ported (registered below); `-graph das` / `wig` (`GraphxyDisplayToDas` reads `graphdata->numofpoints` before it is set: the program writes no file); `-graph bedgraph` of several graphs (plotorf: the file name is pushed once per graph on the list of the created files and `GraphClose` frees it every time: valgrind invalid read of freed memory); tcode `-plot` of a sequence without window.
- **New infrastructure (additive).** `EmbossReportArgs` (`acdSetReport` of the ACD runner: `-outfile -rformat -rname -rextension -rdirectory -raccshow -rdesshow -rscoreshow -rstrandshow -rusashow -rmaxall -rmaxseq`, the tag list, the precision, the default format, validation, the report file, "No hits in output report file", the footer totals), `EmbossGraphXy` / `EmbossGraphArgs` (`acdSetGraphxy`, the device table and its error messages, the data file `tcode1.dat`, the bedgraph file, the null devices incl. the plplot warning about hardware fills, `Created file` on the standard output), `EmbossFeatout` (`acdSetFeatout`: `-outfeat -offormat -ofname -ofdirectory -ofopenfile`, the unknown-format errors, "Feature format ... not supported", "No features written"), `EmbossAlignArgs` (`acdSetAlign`: `-aformat -awidth -aaccshow -adesshow -ausashow -aglobal -adirectory -aname -aextension`), `AcdCommandLine.SavedEntries` (the command line of a report header), `EmbossAcdArgs.IntClamped / IntAssoc / BoolAssoc`, `EmbossReport.TableSeqId / Multi` (the table that `ajFeattableClear` empties between sequences, `multiple` of the debug format), `EmbossAlignmentWriter.Take`, `EmbossSeqoutStream.Take`, the programs in `EmbossSequencePrograms.Tcode.cs / .Checktrans.cs / .Plotorf.cs / .Wordfinder.cs / .Marscan.cs`; MCP tools (generated by `scripts/docs/gen_emboss_wp63_tools.py`): tcode, checktrans, plotorf, wordfinder, marscan. The oracles of showorf / prettyseq / wordcount / seqxref / listor / yank / seqcount / nthseqset were re-recorded with rows without `-outfile`; `prettyseq` refuses the ranges that write beyond the block of the translation string (valgrind: invalid write, `ajRound(len + 1, 32)` bytes).
- **Oracle.** `scripts/alignment/generate_emboss_prog_wp63_oracle.py` (tcode checktrans plotorf wordfinder marscan; every row is run twice and dropped when the runs differ or time out; rows with a plot run under valgrind and are stored as refusals when it reports): 300 rows each, every row compares standard output, error stream, exit status and every written file byte for byte (tcode: 222 defined rows; checktrans 299; plotorf 259; wordfinder 300; marscan 300). **Commits.** 4c9c85f74, 53f866414, 38ea96dc4, 5b043bf94.

### F283 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A2-19b, WP64): MAFFT 7.505 stage 2 - three and more sequences, the progressive strategies FFT-NS-1 / -2 and NW-NS-1 / -2 with every option of `disttbfast`; rows and the program's standard error equal the installed `mafft` on 6 530 / 6 530 sets
- **Finding.** `MultipleAlignMafft` refused three or more sequences (`NotSupportedException`, "registered A2-19b"). **Sources actually opened** (`mafft_7.505.orig.tar.gz`, deb.debian.org, `core/`; read as text and compiled with `gcc -O2` into a scratch directory as an oracle-of-the-oracle: its binaries gave byte-equal output with the installed `mafft` on the first test input, `gcov` listed the functions that a default run executes): `mafft.tmpl` (options -> arguments of `disttbfast`, strategy names, the epilogue text), `disttbfast.c` (`arguments`, `main`, `treebase`, `msadistmtxthread`, `seq_grp*`, `makepointtable*`, `WriteOptions`), `Salignmm.c` (`A__align`, `Atracking`, `match_calc`, `createcpmxresult`, `creategapfreqresult`, `createogresult`, `createfgresult`), `Falign.c` (`Falign`, `mymergesort`), `fftFunctions.c` (`getKouho`, `alignableReagion`, `blockAlign2`, `zurasu2`), `fft.c`, `tddis.c` (`fastconjuction_noname`, `cpmx_calc_new`), `mltaln9.c` (`commonsextet_p`, `fixed_musclesupg_double_realloc_nobk_halfmtx_memsave`, `setnearest`, `counteff_simple_double_nostatic_memsave`, `topolorderz`, `naivepairscore11` / `naivepairscorefast`, `makeskiptable`, `commongappickpairfast`, `st_OpeningGapCount`, `st_FinalGapCount`, `new_OpeningGapCount`, `new_FinalGapCount`, `gapcountf`, `outgapcount`, `gapireru`), `constants.c`, `JTT.c`, `miyata.h`, `blosum.c`, `DNA.h`, `io.c` (`getnumlen`, `getnumlen_casepreserve`, `load1SeqWithoutName_realloc*`, `onlyAlpha_*`, `kake2hiku`, `charfilter`, `setstacksize`, `reporterr`), `defs.c`, `replaceu.c`, `restoreu.c`, `Galign11.c`.
- **Port (additive API).** `SequenceAligner.RunMafft` (the alignment and the program's standard error: `MafftRunResult`), `MultipleAlignMafft` for any number of sequences, `MafftOptions` gained `GapExtension` (--exp), `GapOpenDistance` (--opdist), `TerminalGapPenalty` (--termgappenalty), `Unweight`, `ScoringModel` / `Pam` (--bl / --jtt / --tm / --kimura), `Kappa`, `FrequencyModel` (--fmodel), `WildcardN` (--nwildcard), `ForceFft` (--fft), `TupleSize` (--6merpair / --10merpair), `TreeMixing` (--averagelinkage / --minimumlinkage / --mixedlinkage), `LegacyGapPenalty` (--leavegappyregion), `Quiet`, `Threads` (default 0 as the script). The script's option -> binary mapping is explicit (`MafftScript.DisttbfastArguments` builds the argument list of `disttbfast` exactly as `mafft.tmpl` does, awk number formatting of `--ep` / `--exp` included; `MafftGlobals.Parse` is `arguments()`; `MafftGlobals.Constants` is `constants()`); `MafftRun` holds the state of one run: `Disttbfast` (6-mer / 10-mer distance with the length factor, UPGMA of MUSCLE with the mixed linkage `-X`, branch-length weights, `treebase`, second distance matrix from the first alignment (`-E 2`), second tree and second alignment), `AAlign` (`A__align` with the gap-frequency scaled penalties, the profile history `cpmxhist` of groups of more than 20 sequences, the boundary gaps `sgap` / `egap` of `Falign`), `Falign` (FFT of polarity / volume or of the letter `a`, 20 candidate shifts, windows, `blockAlign2`, segments aligned by `G__align11` or `AAlign`), `G__align11`, the scoring models BLOSUM / JTT / TM / Kimura with `--fmodel`, `--nwildcard`, `--kappa`; the two-sequence path of F119 runs through the same engine (884 / 884 pairs and T-Coffee `mafft_pair` 460 / 460 unchanged). Tables are generated from the program's source (`scripts/alignment/gen_mafft_tables.py`: JTT / TM mutation counts, polarity, volume). MCP `multiple_align_mafft` (28 parameters; the result carries `standardError`).
- **Quirks of the program reproduced (each is in the oracle: a port that "fixes" them differs).** (1) `blockAlign2` compares `crossscore[i-1][k] > maxj` (not `maxi`) and keeps `maxi / maxj / pointi / pointj` as statics across calls; (2) `A__align` reads `ogcp1[1]` / `ogcp2[1]` of its work arrays when a group is one column long (the value of an earlier call; the arrays are cleared only when a longer sequence needs bigger ones and at the end of `treebase`: `A__align( NULL ... )`); (3) `nlen[m1] = 0.5 * ( nlen[m1] + nlen[m2] )` is stored in an `int` (truncation) and decides `ffttry`; (4) the polarity table has 256 entries, so the letter B (index 20) adds 0 to the FFT vector; (5) for nucleotides the FFT uses only the indicator of `a` (`n20or4or2 == 1`); (6) `new_FinalGapCount` compares the last column with the terminating NUL, so the boundary gap pattern `egap` has no effect on the final-gap counts; (7) `G__align11` / `A__align` read the terminating NUL as a letter of score 0 in the last row when `tailgp == 1`; (8) the first guide tree is built from the 6-mer distances (shared 6-mers over the shorter self count, times the length factor of the program), the second from `naivepairscorefast` distances capped at 10 (a negative one is reported and set to 0); (9) the sequences keep their input gaps in `seq` (their positions count in `nlen` and `nlenmax`, which sets `alloclen` and the text "Reallocating..done. *alloclen = N") and lose them by `gappick0` before the alignment; `--anysymbol` adds the two lines of `replaceu` ("inputfile = orig", "N x max - min p") to the standard error; (10) `setstacksize` prints "stacksize: 8192 kb" (the limit of the process; `MafftRun.StackSizeKb`).
- **Reference cross-check (numbers).** `scripts/alignment/generate_mafft_progressive_oracle.py` -> `mafft_progressive_oracle.tsv.gz`: **6 530 sets in 28 strategy groups (at least 210 sets each)**: FFT-NS-2 (default; protein, DNA, 21 - 45 sequences, one-residue to 14-residue sequences, unrelated sequences, `--anysymbol` with unusual symbols, '-' in the input; 20 refusals of the plain command), FFT-NS-1 (`--retree 1`), NW-NS-2 (`--nofft`), NW-NS-1, `--retree 3`, `--6merpair`, `--10merpair`, `--op` / `--ep`, `--exp`, `--opdist`, `--bl` 30 / 45 / 80, `--jtt`, `--tm`, `--kimura`, `--kappa`, `--fmodel`, `--nwildcard`, `--leavegappyregion`, `--termgappenalty`, `--unweight`, `--averagelinkage`, `--minimumlinkage`, `--mixedlinkage`, `--reorder`, `--fft`, `--thread 4`, `--nuc`, `--amino`; 3 - 45 sequences of 1 - 600 residues. **6 530 / 6 530 rows equal the program; the standard error (SHA-256 of the whole text; the full text for 253 sets) equals on 6 310 / 6 310 sets without `--thread`** (with `--thread` the progress text is written by competing threads: 220 sets, rows only: the rows of the `--thread 4` runs equal the single-thread runs, so the alignment does not depend on the thread order; scratch comparisons of more than 2 800 further sets, every option, agreed). The scratch comparison used the program compiled from source: no difference to the installed binary.
- **Non-determinism check.** Every row is reproduced by a second run of the port; the installed program is deterministic for these options (`--thread 4` rows equal the single-thread rows); the stale-array read of (2) is deterministic for a given sequence of calls in one thread, which is what `--thread 0` (the script's default) runs.
- **Tests added.** `SequenceAligner_MafftProgressive_Tests` (33: one test per strategy group over its 210 - 650 sets, rows and standard error; oracle shape; thread independence; `--reorder`; contracts), MCP `MafftTests` (4); `SequenceAligner_Mafft_Tests.Contracts` and `KalignTests.MultipleAlignMafft_Validation` now expect three sequences to align. **Commits.** d02ba1cd0 (code), the documents of this entry.
- **Not done in this entry (DOABLE, registered by name).** `--parttree` / `--dpparttree` / `--fastaparttree` (`splittbfast.c`; `--fastaparttree` needs `fasta34`, which the sandbox lacks: Docker package), `--retree 0` (`--treeout` / `--nodeout` / `--distout`), `--treein`, `--pileup`, `--randomchain`, `--large` / `--memsavetree` / `--stepadd` / `--youngestlinkage` (`compacttree`), `--add` / `--addfragments` / `--addprofile` / `--addfull` / `--addlong` / `--addtotop` (`addsingle.c`), `--merge` / `--seed` / `--seedtable`, `--allowshift` / `--unalignlevel` / `--shiftpenalty` (the warp of `A__align` / `G__align11`), the memory-saving mode for groups longer than 30 000 columns (`MSalignmm.c`), `--aamatrix` / `--text` / `--textmatrix`, `--thread -1` log lines ("OS = linux", "The number of physical cores"); the iterative and pair-library strategies (A2-19c).

### F284 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A2-19c part 1, WP64): MAFFT 7.505 `--maxiterate` (FFT-NS-i / NW-NS-i): `dndpre` + `dvtditr` ported; rows and standard error equal the installed `mafft` on 5 360 / 5 360 sets; the iterative step with threads is non-deterministic in the program (proof)
- **Finding.** `--maxiterate N` was not available (registered A2-19c). **Sources actually opened** (same tarball and scratch build as F283): `mafft.tmpl` (the iterative branch: `dndpre -M 2`, `dvtditr -I`, the limit of 16 iterations of the parallelization strategy BAATARI2, the strategy text), `dndpre.c` (`arguments`, `main`, the distance, `WriteHat2_pointer`), `dvtditr.c` (`arguments`, `main`: the segments, the order file), `tditeration.c` (`TreeDependentIteration`, single-thread path: the branch loop, the accept rule, the oscillation test), `treeOperation.c` (`treeCnv`, `calcBranchWeight`, `calcW`, `syntheticLength`, `weightFromABranch`, `distFromABranch`), `tddis.c` (`OneClusterAndTheOther_fast`), `mltaln9.c` (`searchAnchors`, `fixed_musclesupg_double_treeout`, `setnearest_double_fullmtx`, `intergroup_score`), `Falign.c` (the `kobetsubunkatsu` paths), `io.c` (`WriteHat2_pointer`, `readhat2_pointer`, `input_new`, `commongappick`).
- **Port (additive API).** `MafftOptions.MaxIterate` (--maxiterate; the script lets at most 16 iterations run), `ThreadsIterate` (--threadit); `MafftGlobals.ParseDndpre` / `ParseDvtditr` (the two programs' `arguments()`), `MafftRun.Dndpre` (distance of the rows of the alignment `maxdist x (1 - sp score / min(self))` with the default scoring, capped at 9.9; the values come back through the file `hat2` as six-character `%#6.3f` text, i.e. rounded to three decimals), `MafftRun.Dvtditr` (UPGMA of these distances with complete member lists, `order` of `--reorder` from this tree, cut of the alignment at the windows of `searchAnchors` (20 columns, 65 % of 600), refinement of every piece by `TreeDependentIteration`: for every branch (forward and backward in turn, the root branch once) the two groups are re-aligned by `Falign` in its `kobetsubunkatsu` form (no FFT: the anchors are the windows of the groups' own columns; the segments are freed of all-gap columns before the dynamic program), the weights of the sequences are the products of the branch weights of the unrooted tree (`MafftUnrootedTree`: `treeCnv`, `calcBranchWeight`, `weightFromABranch`), the new alignment is kept when its `intergroup_score` is not lower, `2 n` unchanged branches in a row end the piece (`Converged.`), a repeated score the refinement (`Oscillating.`)), the standard error of both programs. MCP `multiple_align_mafft`: `maxIterate`, `threadsIterate`.
- **Quirks of the programs reproduced.** (1) `dndpre` is not given `-f` / `-g` / `-h`: its distances use the default gap penalty and offset of the scoring model whatever `--op` / `--ep` say, and `maxdist` 2; (2) `dvtditr` reads the distances from the three-decimal text of `hat2`; (3) `dvtditr -K` prints "nadd = " followed by the value of `-I` (the program prints `niter`); (4) for two sequences `dvtditr` sets `weight = 0`, `niter = 1`; (5) `searchAnchors` sums the first window of scores past the end of an alignment shorter than 20 columns (the sum is not used: the window loop does not run); (6) the progress text uses `\r` after every branch and writes the whole run on lines of "STEP 001-001-0 identical." / " accepted." / " rejected." which the oracle compares byte for byte; (7) `dvtditr` writes `order` (its own tree) after `disttbfast` wrote one, so `--reorder` follows the tree of the distances of the alignment.
- **Non-determinism (BLOCKED class, proof).** With `--thread n` (n > 0) and `--maxiterate m` the iterative step runs `dvtditr -C min(n, 8)` in the parallel strategy: ten runs of `mafft --quiet --maxiterate 3 --thread 4 in.fa` on one input gave ten different alignments (ten different md5 sums); `--thread 4 --threadit 0` gave the single-thread result in every run, and `--thread 0` / `--thread 1` give the program's deterministic output. The port refuses `Threads > 0` with an iterative refinement unless `ThreadsIterate = 0` (`NotSupportedException`): those rows cannot equal the program. `--thread n` without iteration is deterministic (220 + 220 committed sets).
- **Reference cross-check (numbers).** `scripts/alignment/generate_mafft_iterative_oracle.py` -> `mafft_iterative_oracle.tsv.gz`: **5 360 sets in 23 strategy groups (at least 210 each)**: `--maxiterate` 1 / 2 / 5 / 1000, `--nofft`, `--retree 1`, `--bl`, `--jtt`, `--tm`, `--op` / `--ep`, `--exp`, `--leavegappyregion`, `--unweight`, the linkage options, `--reorder`, `--kappa`, `--fmodel`, `--nwildcard`, `--6merpair` / `--10merpair`, `--thread 4 --threadit 0`, `--anysymbol`, `--nuc` / `--amino`, two sequences (220), 3 - 43 sequences of 1 - 600 residues; **5 360 / 5 360 rows equal the program; the standard error (SHA-256; the full text for 205 sets) equals on 5 140 / 5 140 sets without `--thread`** (the 220 `--thread 4 --threadit 0` sets: rows only); 8 refusals of the plain command on letters outside the alphabet. Scratch comparisons of about 1 300 further sets agreed.
- **Tests added.** `SequenceAligner_MafftIterative_Tests` (26: one test per strategy group, oracle shape, the refusal of threads in the iterative step, the strategy text), MCP `MafftTests` (+1). **Commits.** code 3eb16b8a5 (this entry), documents: the commit after it.

### F285 - ALIGN-MULTI-001 (audit A2-19c part 2, WP64): MAFFT 7.505 `--globalpair` / `--localpair` / `--genafpair` (G-INS-1, L-INS-1, E-INS-1: `tbfast` with `pairlocalalign`, `Galign11` / `Lalign11` / `genalign11`, the pair-library constraints of `A__align`) ported; rows and standard error equal the installed `mafft` on 13 386 / 13 386 sets
- **Finding.** The pair-library methods (registered A2-19c) were not available. **Sources actually opened** (same tarball and scratch build as F283 / F284): `mafft.tmpl` (the branches `distance=global` / `local` / `localgenaf` with `memsavetree=0`: `tbfast _ (pair arguments) _ -+ iterate ...`; the E-INS-i parameter rules: offset 0.000 for the progressive stage, `-Z` and zero `--lep` / `--lexp` of the pair stage unless `--oldgenafpair`; `termgapopt`; the strategy and explanation texts), `tbfast.c` (`arguments` with the `_ ... _` split and the second call, `main`: `pairlocalalign` inside, `opt / 5.8 * 600`, `hat3.seed`, UPGMA of the pair distances, `treebase` with `constraint == 2`, `calcimportance_half`, `fastshrinklocalhom_half`), `pairlocalalign.c` (`arguments`, `pairalign` serial loop, `score2dist`, `selfscore`), `Galign11.c` (`G__align11`, `G__align11_noalign`), `Lalign11.c` (`L__align11`, `L__align11_noalign`, `Ltracking`), `genalign11.c` (`genL__align11`, `gentracking`), `io.c` (`putlocalhom2`), `mltaln9.c` (`calcimportance_half`, `fillimp`, `movereg`, `movereg_swap`, `makedynamicmtx`, `dist2offset`), `tddis.c` (`fastshrinklocalhom_half`, `fastconjuction_noname`), `Salignmm.c` (`A__align` with `constraint`, `imp_match_init_strict`, `imp_match_out_vead*`, `Atracking_localhom`), `constants.c` (`penalty_OP`, `penalty_EX`). `gcc -E` of `Lalign11.c` / `genalign11.c` was used to read the code that is compiled in.
- **Port (additive API).** `MafftOptions.PairLibrary` (`MafftPairLibrary.Global` / `Local` / `Genaf`), `WeightI` (`--weighti`, 2.7), `GlobalPairOpen` / `Offset` / `Extension` (`--gop` / `--gep` / `--gexp`), `LocalPairOpen` / `Offset` / `Extension` (`--lop` / `--lep` / `--lexp`), `GenafOpen` / `GenafExtension` (`--LOP` / `--LEXP`), `OldGenafParameters` (`--oldgenafpair`). `MafftGlobals.ParsePairlocalalign` / `ParseTbfast` (the two programs' `arguments()`), `MafftScript.TbfastArguments` (the command the script builds), `MafftRun.PairLocalAlign` (all pairs: `G__align11` / `L__align11` / `GenL__align11`, `putlocalhom2` blocks with `opt = isum x 5.8 / (600 x overlap)`, distance `2 (1 - score / min(self))`), `MafftRun.Tbfast` (the progressive alignment), `CalcImportanceHalf`, `FillImp` (`impmtx`), `ShrinkLocalHom`, `MafftRun.AAlign` with the `imp` matrix (`constraint`), `MafftRun.L__align11`, `MafftRun.GenL__align11`. MCP `multiple_align_mafft`: `pairLibrary`, `weightI`, `globalPair*`, `localPair*`, `genafOpen`, `genafExtension`, `oldGenafParameters`.
- **Quirks of the programs reproduced.** (1) `tbfast` builds the matrix of every step with `makedynamicmtx( dep[l].distfromtip )` (disttbfast only with `--amax`): the distances of a pair library can be NEGATIVE (a matrix whose scores are shifted by the offset: the pair stage uses `--lep` 0.1, the progressive stage 0), the matrix of each step is then shifted by `offset x 600` and the program keeps such sequences apart (found by the oracle: `--globalpair --fmodel` on short DNA without G; hand-run test `NegativeDistances_ShiftTheMatrixOfEveryStep`); (2) `impmtx` of `Salignmm.c` is static and only `[0, len1) x [0, len2)` is cleared by a call: with end gaps penalised (G-INS) the dynamic program reads row `len1`, which holds what earlier, larger steps left there: emulated; (3) `L__align11` writes "maxwm <- 0.0" to standard error when no cell scores above the threshold (the pair then has distance 2 and no block); (4) `Atracking_localhom` chooses the end of the alignment without the end-gap term when the end gaps are free (L-INS, E-INS: `-O`); (5) `fillimp` swaps the block coordinates when the sequence number of the first group member is larger; (6) the E-INS-1 strategy has no explanation in the script ("?" and "Not tested."), its epilogue carries the note about the parameters changed in 7.243; (7) conversions of infinities and NaN to `int` follow `cvttsd2si` (INT_MIN), not the saturating conversion of .NET (`--fmodel` with a letter that does not occur); (8) two sequences take the same path (tbfast of two sequences).

## Simplifications kept (with reason) / LIMITATIONS proposals

- ALIGN-STATS-001: none for the counted statistics. The markup reproduces EMBOSS for exactly two sequences (EMBOSS's >2-sequence consensus statistics are the `cons` program, implemented in `MotifFinder.GenerateEmbossConsensus` by B05). Residue-pair matrices other than BLOSUM62 / PAM250 / EDNAFULL are available through the public `SubstitutionMatrix` constructor, not as built-ins (the three are the ones EMBOSS needle/water use by default or the unit validates against).

- ALIGN-MULTI-001 (declared in the algorithm doc §5.3): (1) linear-gap model for all MSA methods, `GapOpen` unused — the exact SP objective with affine natural gap costs (Altschul 1989) depends on the whole column history of every row pair; MSA programs use quasi-natural/position-specific approximations and no exact polynomial profile-profile DP exists; the 2-sequence case is covered by `GlobalAlignAffine`. (2) ~~UPGMA guide tree instead of NJ for the T-Coffee path~~ **resolved (A1-12, F53): `MsaOptions.GuideTree = NeighborJoining`, ClustalW's tree and order verified against clustalw 2.1**; (3) single best SW alignment per pair instead of Lalign's top-N non-intersecting alignments and no sequence-redundancy weights. (2) and (3) change merge order / library density only. (4) the program's progressive stage (relaxation + linked pair-wise DP) is available as `MsaConsistencyEngine.TCoffeeLinked` / `MultipleAlignTCoffee` (A1-13, F58), exact for an explicit library + tree; the program's own primary libraries, k-tuple NJ tree and default method are `MultipleAlignTCoffeeProgram` (A1-13b, F66).
- ALIGN-MULTI-001 (A1-10c a / a2, F65 / F69 / F70 / F76): `-maxiters 1 / 2` of `MultipleAlignMuscle` equals the MUSCLE 3.8.1551 binary on 420 / 420 user-run sets (F69); every other option and command line of the program (iterations >= 3, `-anchors`, `-objscore`, `-weight*`, `-distance*`, neighbour joining + `-root*`, `-brenner`, `-usetree`, `-tree1/-tree2/-distmx*/-computeweights`, `-profile`, `-refine`, `-spscore`, `-ppscore`, `-maketree`, `-refinew`, `-sw`) equals it on 630 / 630 recorded sets of the second user-run round (F76, after six defects were fixed). Residual: `-matrix` of a file without the `*` column (8 unrecorded sets) and of nucleotides, corner cases: round 3 package `handoff/A1-10c-muscle-r3` awaits the user's run (A1-10c a3).
- ALIGN-SEMI-001: only the *fitting* (query-in-reference) semi-global variant is provided; overlap / all-ends-free variants are not implemented. Scope choice, documented in XML + algorithm doc; no LIMITATIONS entry needed.

- GENOMIC-MOTIFS-001: the former limitations "no IUPAC / no reverse strand" are implemented (F19), not left as limitations. Left as documented scope: mismatch-tolerant motif search (fuzznuc `-pmismatch > 0`) = `ApproximateMatcher` / PWM units, not exact known-motif matching.

- GENOMIC-ORF-001: the former "not implemented" items (alternative start codons, non-standard genetic codes, nested vs. longest reporting, partial ORFs, NCBI length convention) are implemented (F21–F25), not left as limitations. **Done (F57, A1-18/A1-19):** ORFfinder's cross-frame "Ignore nested ORFs" (`-n`), `-b/-e`, the `-ml` clamp, `-strand`, the partial flags and tables 27/28/31 were measured on the real NCBI 0.4.3 binary (user-run Docker package) and implemented; `-c` (circular) is a no-op in the binary (identical output on 68 pairs), so nothing is implemented for it. Input scope: A/C/G/T `DnaSequence` or (A1-21, F50) an IUPAC nucleotide string through the string overload (ambiguous codons: stop only if every concrete codon is a stop, never a start).

- GENOMIC-REPEAT-001: none. The former "maximal-repeat classification not implemented" and "tie-break unspecified" are implemented (F29, F30). Left as documented scope: the reverse complement is not searched by `FindRepeats` (dispersed inverted repeats = `RepeatFinder.FindInvertedRepeats` / `FindReverseComplementRepeats`, B04).

- GENOMIC-SIMILARITY-001: none kept. Mash/sourmash strand-agnostic k-mers (`canonical`) are implemented (F33), not a limitation. Left as documented scope: MinHash sketching (Mash `-s`) is not needed for the exact index (`KmerAnalyzer` has the Mash distance); Jaccard distance = `1 - result/100`. Empty-union value is a convention (no source fixes it).

- GENOMIC-TANDEM-001: none kept. The former "exact only / brute-force / not implemented: approximate repeats" items are resolved: complexity fixed (F36), approximate repeats exist in-repo (F37). Left as documented scope: exact copies only (Benson's approximate copies = `RepeatFinder.FindApproximateTandemRepeats`); the unit is the left-end motif phase (MISA/pytrf), rotations are not canonicalised.

- ALIGN-MULTI-001 (F126): the NEXUS reader implements the data block (dimensions, format datatype / interleave, matrix with quoted taxon names, comments) as written by Biopython / PAUP, not the whole Bio.Nexus grammar (trees, sets, charstatelabels, `matchchar`, parenthesised ambiguity); the Stockholm reader does not expose `alignment.operations`; both are documented in the XML docs, registered with A2-27c.
- ALIGN-GLOBAL-001 (F125): the Z-drop, approximate-mode and banded SIMD results of `Ksw2Aligner` are ported from the C source but unverified against the C program until the Docker package output is integrated (A2-29c); the exact cases are verified.

- ALIGN-MULTI-001 (F127): `-go` / `-ge` on profiles of unequal size and gapped MSF / Clustal input crash or give garbage in the program itself (heap overflows, valgrind-confirmed); the port implements the intended algorithm for them and the oracle covers only the defined cases (equal-size merges, gap-free alignment files).

- ALIGN-MULTI-001 (F128): MSA / PO file input of `poa` and the standard-error progress lines are not ported (the latter print undefined `%ld` arguments); spoa / abPOA are not claimed.

- ALIGN-MULTI-001 (F187 - F190): the `[M::...]` progress log of minimap2 and `-d` (index file) are not reproduced; inputs that make the C program abort (`k` above 28, a window of 256 or more) raise `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`; the traceback of the ksw2 SIMD kernels is bounded by `Ksw2Aligner.MaxTracebackBytes` (1 GiB, the C code has none); the reader warnings of a malformed FASTQ are printed once per part, not once per mini-batch.

- WP51 (F214 / F215), refusals that are the program's own undefined behaviour (proof in the entries): `mash sketch -z` with a character of 0x80 or more; `mash taxscreen` with a taxon whose parent is missing from `nodes.dmp` (uninitialised pointer, valgrind). The `ajStrToInt` / location parsers of the diffseq GenBank / EMBL readers are ported statement by statement; no qualifier value, location or feature-output combination of the committed oracle rows (420 + 450 + 500) or of the thousands of development rows differs. Unfinished work, registered (A5-8c3d, F220): features read from other file formats and the feature output formats of `wordmatch`.

- pytrf/MISA comparison of the canonical scan (F38: `pip install pytrf` declined by the sandbox) is informational; the three-method Python oracle is complete (B04 F5 holds the MISA/pytrf comparison).

### Part 4 - defects and contract holes found by the correctness review of the round-1 code

- [x] (4e2f3ef7, WP23 2026-11-19: F80: one scoring contract (gaps <= 0, path score < 2^28, 64-bit sum of pairs), repro values rejected / exact, 7 tests.) **A2-37 DOABLE - scalar `ScoringMatrix` integer overflow gives a silently WRONG score; `int.MinValue` gaps crash:** `GlobalAlign("A"x50, "A"x50, new ScoringMatrix(1_000_000_000, -1, -2, -1)).Score` = 1 999 999 904 (true 5e10), `LocalAlign` = 2 000 000 000, `GlobalAlignAffine` = 1 999 999 900 - no exception; `GlobalAlignAffine(.., new ScoringMatrix(1, -1, int.MinValue, int.MinValue))` -> `IndexOutOfRangeException` (negation overflow; through `MultipleAlign(.., Affine)` it surfaces as `AggregateException`). The matrix path has the guard ("Score range too large for the integer dynamic program", SequenceAligner.cs:127) but the scalar `ScoringMatrix` (`implicit operator PairScoring`, SequenceAligner.cs:53) does not, and `ScoringMatrix` (AlignmentTypes.cs:23) validates nothing; also a POSITIVE gap score is rejected for `MatrixScoring` ("GapOpen must be a finite score <= 0") but accepted by the scalar path (`GlobalAlign("ACGT","AC", new ScoringMatrix(1,-1,5,5))` = 30). Fix: one range / sign validation shared by both paths (ArgumentException with the same message), `checked` arithmetic or a conservative bound `(|max score| + |gap|) * (m + n) < int.MaxValue`; tests with the exact repro values; also the MSA sum-of-pairs scorers (`ComputeSumOfPairsScore`, `SumOfPairsScore`) which accumulate in `int`.

- [x] **A5-1 - DONE (WP41, c4f2e8229, F167: `X31Hash` sign-extends the first byte and ends at NUL; new oracle group `qname`, 330 PAF cases (189 non-ASCII first byte, 99 with U+0000) equal minimap2 2.26, the first 1 320 rows reproduced byte for byte)- DOABLE (proven defect) - `Minimap2Chaining.X31Hash` does not sign-extend the first byte; a query name starting with a non-ASCII character orders equal-score hits differently from minimap2.** `Minimap2Chaining.Hits.cs:136` `uint h = bytes[0];` where khash.h `__ac_X31_hash_string` is `khint_t h = (khint_t)*s; ... h = (h << 5) - h + (khint_t)*s` over a SIGNED `char` (the loop of the port already uses `(uint)(sbyte)bytes[i]`; only the first byte is zero-extended). The hash of the query name seeds the tie order of chains of equal score (`hash ^= ...; Hash64Full(...)`, `GenRegs`), so for a first byte >= 0x80 the primary / secondary choice differs. Measured against `minimap2 2.26` (`Map` with `queryName` vs `minimap2 ref.fa q.fa` PAF, 60 random references with three equal copies of a 300-600 base segment, query = the segment): ASCII names 0 / 60 and 0 / 60 differ; names starting with `U+00E9` 57 / 60 differ, with `U+4E2D` 53 / 60 (e.g. port primary `0:802-1195`, program primary `0:202-595`); with the one-line fix `uint h = (uint)(sbyte)bytes[0];` (throwaway copy) 0 / 60 and 0 / 60. Also: C strings end at NUL, so a name containing U+0000 hashes only its prefix (port: whole string). The 1 320 committed PAF rows never use a non-ASCII or NUL-containing name (oracle gap). Fix the function, add rows with multi-byte / NUL names (`generate_minimap2_map_oracle.py`, query names from a UTF-8 pool) + a unit test, regenerate byte-identically.
